messages.text: Do Not Use
Enter
Leave
The massive gates of this mountain stronghold are locked fast.
Selkie guards lounge among great rocks in the middle of this lake.
An old man carefully makes his way along the rocky shore towards you. He says, 'I heard the wreck last night. You are lucky to be alive. Usually the wreckers don't allow their victims to survive.'
'Wreckers?' You ask. 'Yes', he nods, 'times have been tough and some of the locals have taken to luring ships onto the rocks by tying a lantern to a mule and walking it along the cliffs.'
The gates of Ryn are closed. A lazy sentry, with a face like a fist, slurs that strangers are not permitted entry.

'The Wreckers then collect the "abandoned" cargo from the wreck. A shameful and cowardly act.' He notices your shivering and says, 'join me in my home above the cliffs. I will go and start a fire.' He moves purposely to the north.
Approach the gates?
Back off
You are admitted to Lord Godolphin's manor. Enter?
Its too dangerous on this island to rest.
You cross the bridge and return to the surface.
You enter Maeth's cottage.

You awake shivering. Your clothes and equipment are drenched with salt water. Your cargo is nowhere to be found. The ship you chartered passage on lies around as so much debris. You have no idea where you are but at least you are alive.
You look for the lighthouse whose lights you saw just before the awful ripping of timbers upon rocks. However there is no lighthouse. How strange.
You hear someone approaching from the north.

The old man continues to talk as you trudge along, 'by the way my name is Maeth. Welcome to Karnak. Although you probably don't feel too welcome arriving as you did. Just the same, this land needs some sorting out. You might be the catalyst we need.'
Maeth welcomes you to his home. You sit around his fire and feel the warmth seep into your bones.
You enter a damp and sandy cave.  This cave has seen a lot of human activity. A rough door has been bolted over a smaller section of the cave.

Just as you are about to open the door, several lightly armed men walk into the cave leading a mule. 'I told you we should have finished them on the beach', one says to another, 'now we'll have to finish the job'. They spring to the attack.
You find a collection of goods and equipment in the back of the cave. Unfortunately your cargo is not here. It probably sits at the bottom of the sea.
Looks like passing ships are now safe from these cowardly fools. However, you are still stranded here. Might as well make the most of it.
You engage Maeth in conversation.

'Karnak is an ancient nation. It was once a proud, strong land but a series of invasions has weakened us terribly. I moved from the towns to avoid watching the degeneration of my kinfolk. Strange forces take advantage of our weakness and roam the land.'
A weathered sign reads: 'Welcome to Carclew'
You enter a simple shop.
An entrance to an abandoned tin mine lies here. A hastily drawn sign reads:           'Danger! Knockers'
You push cobwebs and debris aside as you scramble down the hole into darkness.
The entrance to the Knocker lair.
A sign over the gates reads House Godolphin.
A crowd of townspeople stand before the gates listening to a large bearded man wearing fine chainmail. You stand unnoticed at the back of the crowd.

He says: 'People of Carclew, calm yourselves and listen. We have all suffered losses from the Arn-cursed Runics. Do not despair. As I speak my eldest son Cairbre moves to hold the Eastern passes and protect us against any further raids.'

'My men and I are gathering a war party to subdue the vile and cowardly folk of Ryn. As you know they are collaborating with the Runics ... examples must be made of them before any other towns think of turning traitor. Who will join me?'
Members of the crowd look doubtfully at one another and one by one shrink past you and into town. You are left alone with the now crestfallen speaker and several of his aides.

The man eyes you warily. 'Greetings strangers, I am Lord Godolphin. Welcome to Carclew. I cannot offer you much but as you can see I certainly require the aid of anyone who will help me. Will you join my war party?'
Join war party?
Maybe later.
'Very well', Goldophin says, 'I may be seeing you around.'

'Excellent,' Godolphin says, 'I look forward to battle. We are expecting light resistance. For your troubles I can only give 100 gold upon completion of this raid. Meet us by the well in the north of town. Come prepared for battle.' He turns away.
Godolphin and several tough looking armsmen and women are gathered around the well. They seem to be lost in meditation ... but arise as one as you approach. 'Ready?' Godolphin growls.
To arms!
Just a minute
The warriors nod grimly ... and march out of Carclew to the north. You stop amid some fields in front of a small town. 'There is Ryn', Godolphin says.

He seems shocked for an instant as the gates open and a motley group of characters move toward you. 'How could they have known we were coming', Godolphin says, almost to himself. 'No matter - to battle!' You charge.
You find a strange key upon the large man with the black armour.

You quickly gather the wounded and return to Carclew.  'Well done!' Godolphin exclaims,  'here is your reward and a badge of Godolphin. Wear it boldly, for there are those in this land who remember our name.'

'The Ryn guard seemed to know we were coming. I suspect it had something to do with the big man with the axe. He is connected to the Silverband, a bunch of thieves and knaves headquartered in the Red Dragon, our local inn.'

'I would consider it a great service if you would look into this matter for me. They would see me coming a mile away and would simply scarper. I shall go to Ryn to restore order. Seek me out there if you find something.'
The doors of Lord Godolphin's house are open.
Journey to the south?

A lone man sits on a log playing a whistful tune on some pipes. He stops at your approach. 'Oh', he says, 'I guess you heard my pipes. To be honest I was trying to attract someone else. I saw the most beautiful woman in the world near here last week.'
'Ah, well met, but please return when you  can tell me what the Silverband are truly up to'. Godolphin returns to his heated discussions with the townsfolk.
Llywarch falls lifeless. Your intuition tells you that some vital part of the Struggle has been left undone.
You leave the Knocker lair.

You come across a bizarre scene. A group of hairy little men are preparing to do battle with some reptilian men. Each groups pauses a moment as you enter the room. The hairy little men take this opportunity to flee to the south. The reptiles attack you!
You are not entirely sure what these things twitching at your feet are. You move on.
A small hairy man lies dead here. It looks like he was dragged here and jabbed with spears.

A group of hairy little men are gathered here. They clutch their spears and watch you expectantly. A particularly old and hairy man steps forward. He says, 'I am Byrm of the Knockerkin'. His voice is surprisingly deep and resonant.

'You defeated the Laerg', he says solemnly, 'we are in your debt.  We don't know where they came from - they seem to have dug a cave complex into our home to besiege us. Join me in my private quarters down the hall and we will talk privately.'
Byrm awaits you.

Byrm says, 'We Knockerkin are facing a grave danger. These Laerg attack us mercilessly and without any cause. We are not a people knowledgeable in the ways of war. Our hunters were sent out to explore the Laerg caves but have not returned.'
'I am not aware what fate befell them. Now we are left with only the aged and young to defend our homes. Please explore the cave network and find out what happened to our hunters. Will you aid us?'
Accept
Decline
'Very well, return if you feel you have something to contribute', Byrm says bitterly. He turns away.
'Excellent, please return to me when you have found something. The Laerg appear to come from the caves east of the exit to the surface.'
Byrm takes the hunters note and reads it. Although saddened by the devastating loss of so many Knockerkin Byrm seems excited by the note's contents.
The Gray Archon falls to the ground as a lifeless suit of armour. A spirit spreads from the heap of metal and leaves the room.
Byrm politely asks you to return when you have completed your mission.
A group of Laerg are here readying themselves for an incursion into the Knocker lair. They attack!
You open the door to discover Laerg guards waiting for you with weapons drawn.
You disturb some huge Laerg growling at each other around a rough table.
A motley collection of Laerg and their snarling pets await you in this room.

You see an exhausted Knocker in here. As you open the door he wakes and waves you towards him. He whispers, 'I don't who you are but I heard you kill the Laerg ... so you must on our side. I led some hunters against the Laerg but we were taken.'

'I managed to hide a note in the wall behind me - take it to Byrm, our elder, he will know what to do. For me the fight is over, please rescue any remaining hunters you find.' With that he closes his eyes and expires.
You find a note hidden in the debris.
You find a dead Knocker hunter here. The Laerg clearly tortured him to death.
A Knocker hunter lies here. His fear is so great that he dies of fright when you sets his eyes upon you.
A Knocker strains against his chains in here. There is a lot of fight left in him. He lunges at you but the chains hold him. His eyes seem to clear and he realizes you are not Laerg.
The Knocker looks at you hopefully and says, 'free me and help me rid these caves of the Laerg scum. They killed my brethren and I will have my vengeance. I am Welk, a great hunter among my people. '
Free Welk
Leave him to rot
Welk joins you after collecting a few weapons from the dead Laerg in the hall.
A pile of dead Knockers lie in the corner. A gruesome sight.
The stench overpowers you.
This cell contains a dead gray seal. Why would the Laerg want to shackle a seal?

You interrupt an angry exchange between the Laerg. A large Laerg hisses, 'itsss sssafe, Sssaemael, I threw it to the Ungrow asss you ssaid ...' He stops as you clear the door. The one he was addressing turns to you with a toothy grin.

'What nature of beassst iss thiss', he muses looking you over, 'certainly not those patheric Knockersss. A worthy addition to my collection, methinksss.' He eyes you sideways and then calls for his underlings to collect your heads.

You find a odd assortment of what look like digging tools. They seem to be clawed gauntlets which the Laerg must put over their already impressive claws to aid them in tunnelling. Useless to you, you leave them.
You step in a big pile of Laerg dung. You will probably reek for days.

A crude idol lies before you on a pile of rocks. It seems to depict a brownish dragon baring its fangs. The idol appears to be ancient but of such craftmanship you wonder how Laerg claws could have fashioned it.
Welk urges you to destroy the idol.
The idol lies seemingly helpless before you.
Bash it's many heads in.
Back off
The idol rather anticlimatically falls to pieces. Disappointed, you leave the rockpile.
A Knocker runs by your group fleeing as fast as his little hairy legs will take him.
Two bizarre creatures uncoil from their stalagmite perchs and attack.
The creatures have gathered some shiny objects in this dark corner. Amid some worthless rocks lies a battered but powerful looking sword.
You find another exit to these caverns. Take it?
'It seems that the hunters were chained in a cell with a Selkie for some time. They were our allies in ancient times, so it is said. However, none have been seen in living memory.'
'The Selkie claimed to have arrived in the Laerg caverns through another entrance. They too fight the Laerg. Please find the Selkies and tell them of our plight.'
You leave the rocky coast and enter a secluded beach.
A weathered sign reads: 'Cantref y Gwaelod'.
Townspeople wander by. Their eyes are vacant and they shuffle about aimlessly. They seem oblivious to your presence.
A pack of wild dogs run by.
You feel that you are being watched. The hair on the back of your necks stands on end. You search the cave but there is nothing to find.
You walk around some rotting crops. It looks like these fields have lain fallow for some time.
The gates bang open and shut in the wind. The gatehouse is abandoned. There is no one in sight.

An impressive looking manorhouse dominates Tre Mordin. This seems to be the centre of activity among the vacant eyed townsfolk. A constant stream of them courses out of the manor. None so much as notice you. Enter?
A frantic voice calls down from this lone tree. 'What do you want ... back away before you catch leprosy.' Stay?
The ring of Gwyddno glows for an instant. The rock face at the back of the dark cave fades to reveal a passage leading into the mountains. Enter?
Laerg attack!
Ryn guardsmen eye you up and down as you pass the gates.
You approach House Godolphin. An ancient butler patiently informs you that Lord Godolphin is not at home.
At the back of the cave you find some loose boulders. Pushing them aside reveals a dark passage leading into the mountain.
'It is said that the wreckers hang around the caves near the mouth of the river to the west. You would be wise to relieve them of your purloined cargo.'

'The town of Carclew lies to the west, led by an able but headstrong man called Godolphin. Further west of there lies the town of Tre Garrick and its famous inn. North of Carclew lies the town of Ryn and east across the lakes lies Tre Mordin.'
The ground seems disturbed but try as you might you are unable to discover why. After some futile searching you move on.
This seems a fairly tense inn. Several townsmen are sitting around the bar. All eyes turn to you as you walk up to the bar. The innkeeper seems quite cheerful though, and asks what you want.
The innkeeper pulls some pints and hands them to you. Hey not bad, this town does have something going for it.

'Times are sad around here. We lost a lot of young'ns fighting off the Runic swine. The other towns seem to be content to sit behind their walls. But I know for a fact the Runics are coming for us.' The innkeeper grows more agitated as he speaks.

'Don't know of any honest work to be had around here these days, but you might want to enquire with the local Lord in his manor house. He's always cooking some scheme to further himself off of the labour of others'. He says the last bit quietly.
'Haven't seen much of the Wreckers these days have you? Perhaps they finally met someone who didn't appreciate their brand of humour'
'I'm moving off to Tre Garrick soon with the wife. I fancy their walls ought to keep us safe from those Runics. I'm too old this %#$@'
'Nobody bothers to come here anymore since those thieves moved in. I wouldn't dare hang around the alleys outside, its full of cut-throats and muggers.'

'My cousin hasn't come back from Tre Mordin yet. It's been weeks. I hope the Runics haven't got him ... or worse'. - 'What's worse than the Runics?'. -  'Between you and me he said it was to be his last trip; said something evil lurked around there'.
'I would love to go fight the Runics. I'd show them a thing or two. But its my knee you see, thats what keeps me at home.'

'My crops got the blight. Its the work of those damned Knockers. I just know it. Always wrecking things and causing mischief.' - 'No such thing as a Knocker'. - 'There is, they say they live in the hills to the south of town'. '
The skeleton of a fir'bolg lies here. Its bones seem to have been crushed by a mighty blow. You salvage a fine looking robe and an interesting ring from the skeleton.
Lord Godolphin is in residence.

'Please investigate the Silverband. I don't know what they're up to but if they have allied themselves with the Runics then they are enemies. I have my hands full dealing with these Ryn idiots'. He glowers at the townspeople around him.  You depart.

You inform Godolphin about the Groats. 'A ruse, eh. Those cunning Runics', he exclaims, 'having us suspect possible allies'. He pauses. 'I shall return to Carclew, my work here is done. You should seek out my son Cairbre. He holds the eastern passes.'

He continually makes reference to the fact that he is unable to deduce who really is in charge here. The Demon Lord scares him but it seems deferential to another strange man who Garanhir refers to as 'Darvik the Damned.'
A lonely tower stands atop this lookout point. The architecture is of an unusual design. Enter?

There are several well thumbed books on the shelves. The subject matter indicates the wizard had a keen interest in plants and biology. Within a large tome you find a map to some mountain cave. Several useful scrolls are also on the shelves.
You see a hastily constructed Karnak stronghold before you.
Arrows pelt you from the battlements. 'Get back you Runic scum'. You retreat.
'I bring tidings of Lord Godolphin to his son Cairbre', you shout. The sentries seem satisfied by this and raise the gates.

A young man approaches you, clad for battle. You tell him of the Groats and of the Silverband. He ponders this. 'My father was wise to enlist your aid. Our need is great, the Runics grew bold in their assaults upon Karnak soil.'

'Even now a large force of them moves through the pass towards us. Every able-bodied man is being mobilised to prevent this incursion. If they break through the pass they will crush us with their numbers. Will you join us?'
But of course
Not my fight.

'Follow me, the bards will sing of this battle for years to come!' Cairbre cries to those around him. He seems to the only one enjoying himself though. The Karnak troops seem weary of this constant fighting.

An intimidating sight lies before you. Finely disciplined units of Runic soldiers maneuvre in cadence step through the pass, allowing them to maintain a wedge formation. The Karnak irregulars soon lose formation and enter battle as a disorganised mob.
You stumble exhausted from the battlefield. Cairbre is rallying surviving Karnak warriors to him.
This seems to be an empty cave.
Cairbre thanks you for your assistance. 'Let me present you with this token of thanks from the Karnak people,' he says handing you a fine shield. 'This shield has a noble heritage, use it well.'

Cairbre says 'We have a problem. One of our greatest strategists has been captured by the Runics. Rumours have it that he is being held in their salt mines far to the north. They put both their worst criminals and captured enemies to work there.'

He continues: 'The only way to get to him to free him is to get captured by the Runics and be shipped to the mines. It would be impossible to battle our way that far without a massive force being sent against us. '

'However, a small group could get inside the mines and escape with him. His cunning is so great that I am sure he will find a way out.' Cairbre shrugs and spreads his hands. 'Its the best plan we could come up with'. Will you do it?
Yes
'Fair enough', Cairbre says, 'if you change your mind you know where to find me'.

'Excellent', Cairbre says, 'go to the gatehouse on the other side of the pass. Engage them in battle and lose. The pass guards never kill defeated foes. Instead they lock them in the mines.  There you can find the strategist, Penhaligon. Good luck.'
Karnak soldiers approach you. They see you are not Runics and pass by.
Refugees flee to the west clutching their meagre belongings.
Some stealthy figures disappear into the thick underbrush.
Some Runic infiltrators must have made it past the Karnak patrols. They attack you as soon as they see you to hide their incursion.
Byrm awaits you.
Byrm looks up expectantly. 'Nothing yet, eh, keep trying, please.' He says and turns away.

You show the hunter's note to Byrm. He reads it and turns to you. 'It seems the hunters were briefly kept with a Selkie. The Selkies were our ancient allies but we have not had contact with them in living memory. Until now.'

'The Selkie told the hunters that he came through another entrance to the Laerg caves. If you find the Selkie - give them this token - and hopefully they will remember us Knockerkin'. Byrm returns to his musings.
The mighty Ent crashes to the ground, lifeless. Even the death of a single Ent brings this ancient race of forest tenders closer to extinction.
You stumble across a battle in progress between some Laerg and some very strange looking blubbery creatures. The Laerg see you and direct their attacks against you as well.
The blubbery creatures silently limp towards the river and dive in. In mid leap they turn into grey seals. They disappear beneath the greenish water.
Registration point. Sadly, you cannot pass this point without registering.
A dark passage leads into the rock face.
You search along the rockface and find a thin aperture through which you can squeeze. The smuggler was right. The tunnel leads out beyond the mountains.
A sign over the bridge says 'Welcome to Tre Mordin'.

'I have been waiting here to see her once more. She ran off when I called to her. Why, I don't know. I guess I have waited here too long. I had better return to my home. Maybe you will see her, better for you if you don't.' He says dejectedly.
'Oh, by the way - I saw a huge bear or something near the lake fishing with his claws. Be careful it was a real monster'. He walks off.
The fragile structures falls to bits with a clatter.  The noise summons an enormous bear from the lakeshore. The bear looks at the destroyed structure and howls with rage. It attacks!
The bear collapses to its haunches on the rocky lakeshore. Blood pours from its wounds into the lake. The water starts to churn and boil as the blood spreads out to turn the lake crimson.
You turn back to the bear but instead find a beautiful raven haired woman lying on the lakeshore. Her wounds match those suffered by the bear. The bear is nowhere to be seen.
An enormous man stands in front of his hut chopping wood with massive blows. His bare chest is bristled with old scars.

His stops and stares at you. He seems to lift his nose in the air and take a deep breath. A bestial growl escapes his lips. 'You have the blood of my daughter upon you, I will tear you limb from limb'. He transforms into a bear and attacks you.

'Greetings', growls the man, 'we don't get too many visitors round these parts.' He winks with his one of his golden eyes and grins unnaturally large canines at you.  'They call me Greyclaw. Will you join me for some fish stew?'

You join Greyclaw in his hut. Inside you find a beautiful raven haired woman dishing out some fine smelling fish stew. 'This is my daughter, Dianecht, fine looking isn't she,' Greyclaw says proudly, then growls menacingly, 'alright, stop staring.'
After a fine meal Greyclaw pulls out some tobac weed and lights his pipe. He offers to pass the pipe around. 'Want some, it brings on good dreams?' Greyclaw says.
Uncomfortable with the vibes coming off Greyclaw you make your excuses and leave.
Greyclaw sits on his porch smoking his pipe. He seems lost in his dreams.

You all take a big toke off of the pipe and settle back in your chairs. A sense of relaxation and drowsiness overtake you. You dream of a small family of bears, a mated couple and a young cub. They fish for rainbow trout on the banks of a large lake.
You come across a pile of stones placed delicately into the semblance of a human shape.
Nothing happens.
You feel a sense of well being.
Hordes of the strange furry creatures line the battlements of this stone fort. The gates open and they rush forth to attack.
As you enter the gates you notice groups of humanoids huddled fearfully together moving slowly away from you. A lone figure emerges from the large stone fort and haughtily approaches you.

As the humanoid draws near, you realize she is a female of her kind, and from the tiara like object on her head she appears to be royalty. She looks at you angrily and says, 'what is the meaning of this unprovoked attack upon Groat land.'
An elaborate but weathered sign depicting a red dragon hangs over this large white inn. Enter?
'Just a simple old man', he winks. 'I'm not some retired wizard if that was what you were hoping for'.

You call her bluff and show her the papers found at the Silverband. 'There has not been a Groat king in twenty generations, the line runs from mother to daughter. This is a fake and not a very well researched one at that.'
The old man bids you farewell.
You don't have the gold. Embarrased you walk away from the disappointed innkeeper.
'Well fought,' Cairbre gasps. 'Lets retire to the stronghold.'
Cairbre instructs you to return when you have found something. He returns to his battle maps.
'You made it out of the salt mines!' Cairbre exclaims. 'To be honest I was not certain I would ever see you again. Please take Penhaligon to my father in Carclew.'
'You never found Penhaligon?', Cairbre gapes. 'Then all hope is lost'. He sits back in his chair. 'Please search the mines again, my spy network is adamant that he is there.'
'I have nothing further for you here, it is Cairbre at the pass who needs your impressive talents'. Godolphin says.
'I heard you were on a mission for Cairbre. Something to do with my comrade Penhaligon. Perhaps you should complete it.' Godolphin suggests forcefully.
Leave the cave?

Penhaligon greets Godolphin as an old brother-in-arms. 'Its been too long, old friend', Penhaligon says. 'Yes', Godolphin agrees and turns to you 'thank you friends. Again you have shown yourselves true friends of Karnak.'
You begin to head to your private quarters to stock up on provisions when a loud clanging startles you. The sentry tower bells are ringing. You race to the high tower of Godolphin's manor.

A lone dragon soars gracefully above the manor. There appears to be an armoured man on its back. Godolphin has appeared. 'A Dragonrider', he says quietly. 'I have heard rumours about them. An elite force answerable directly to the Runic Emperor.'

'Now that we have our master strategist', he claps Pengaligon good naturedly, 'we shall launch our counterstrike and drive the Runics from these lands.' The two begin to discuss logistics for the campaign.

'It does not make sense for the emperor to send such a valuable unit to fight us. We have nothing worth fighting for. Perhaps we have something that the Runics desire greatly - but are unaware of ourselves.'

'We can't make our attack with them controlling the skies. You are the only ones who have proven yourself strong enough to vanquish such a foe. The only way to defeat the dragonriders would be to attack them at rest before they mount up. '

'He returns to feed information to his masters... Seek out our agent, Kynyaf. He is spying for us in the Runic city, and frequents the local inn. He should have valuable insights into how to defeat the dragonriders.'
'Tell Kynyaf 'Durdala Dywy' which means "thank you" in the old tongue, and he will know to trust you. May Arn lend you strength for this expedition.' With that Godolphin climbs down the ladder.

Two water sprites are skipping rocks by this pool. 'Stone to break stone but leave water alone' one says to the other. It then skips a rock into the pool. The rock bounces off a wet stone, skips a space of water then bounces off another stone.
Godolphin stands here, wielding his trusty claymore.
You investigate the area.
The tinner looks unhappy. 'I can scrounge up 200 gold for the directions if you insist.' He says weakly.
You give the tinner directions and he rushes off excitedly.
Godolphin regards you 'We are waiting for word that the Dragonriders are no more. Until that happens we will be unable to mount our attack. Remember: Durdala Dywy.'
'You found Penhaligon.'
You find the smuggler's passageway.
'Go away, foreign scum', cry some sentries as they shoot over your heads.
You brandish your Godolphin emblem and the sentries open the gate.
A large sign proclaims to the world: 'Ryn Guildhall'.

Black rocks appear in the churning water ahead of the ship. It's too late to take evasive maneuvres. Suddenly a horrific splintering noise erupts as the ship's hull is ruptured. You are thrown into the freezing water.
The remains of a ship lie scattered here. It must have been smashed against the rocks.
A sandy grotto cuts into the cliffside. Enter?
A large cave leads into the mountains. Enter?

You approach an enormous tree. Owl-hoots call back and forth. You find yourself encircled by several hundred pointy eared archers who rise from their tree cover as one.  Warriors pour forth from the elevated platforms running along the tree.
A squat tower is set in a small grove in this forest of ancient oak trees. A tranquil garden surrounds the base of the tower. Enter?

A ruined castle stands atop a small hill. Its glory is all but faded and ivy stretchs along its crumbling walls. It is clearly occupied however, as many there many recent tracks leading up the causeway. Enter?
You step foot upon the mystic island.

You enter a grand looking hall which calls itself a university. It consists of empty rooms filled with chairs. You are about to leave when a scholarly looking individual walks up to you. 'How fortuitous, I was just looking for someone to assist me.'
A sign outside this building describes it as the city library. Enter?
A large sign outside this stone building describes it as the financial centre. Enter?
A huge Runic market takes up space here.
A statue commerorating the valiant efforts of the Runic Legions stands in the middle of this fountain.
The Temple of the Sacred Runes stands here.  They offer services to all but their prices tend to increase for those who they deem 'barbarian'. This includes you.
You walk up to what looks like a normal dwelling house. Knock on the door?
The Runic Light Cavalry are garrisoned here. A full light brigade consisting of five hundred well armed troops and their steeds live here. You think it would be best not to make trouble with them.
A large tunnel leads to the north. A chilling wind whistles through the tunnel. Head north?
A log cabin lies abandoned here. Entering it you see it has been looted and trashed. Nothing of value remains in here.
Beginning script ships crashs.

You come upon a crude fortification. Lumber and rocks have been placed in a pile to form a rough wall. From atop of the wall a hail of darts lands among you. This is followed by a frenzied attack by humanoids.
You clamber over the debris and continue.

Fresh air at last. You have arrived at a high plateau among the mountains. The view is breathtaking but your attention is centered upon the rough stone fort in front of you. A small keep, flanked by two squat towers stand beyond a wall.

'I sent a diplomatic envoy to the Karnaks to enlist their aid against the Runic invaders but they have yet to return. I am not surprised now. You Karnaks are a bunch of bloodthirsty berzerkers - the bulk of our menfolk are dead.'

'We will surely fall to the Runics now. I have no choice except to seal the tunnels. You had better leave now before you are stuck here forever.' Disturbed by this turn of events, you return to the passage and leave the mountain.
Tons of rocks have been heaved into the passage, sealing it permanently.
You enter a densely grown over and neglected valley. You feel a momentary surge of panic. A powerful premonition overtakes you. You feel certain that an awful fate awaits inside the cursed inn.

This is the mayor of Tre Garrick's office. It's the only building that isn't locked shut. The few townsfolk that you see wandering through this oddly quiet town cast you nervous glances and give you a wide berth. You enter.

The mayor sits at his desk. He jumps up as you enter. He is in a highly agitated state. 'Ah, noble adventurers ... have you come about the inn? Of course you have, there isn't anything here anymore since the curse fell upon the inn.'
A powerful compulsion to avoid this area forces you back.
The local druid lives here. He provides healing services for the area.
Creidhne the metal worker lives here.
Wealthy merchant lives here. Insider trader, capture on behalf of stock market.
An imposing private villa is located here. A large gate manned by well armed guards stands between you and exploring this place.
You have been at sea for weeks. Finally, a lighthouse beams out of the misty gloom to the north revealing a safe harbour. You are desperately low on supplies and gratefully head towards it.
It looks pretty rough ahead but the lighthouse indicates safe passage. You continue.
A group of tough looking characters guard  the door behind them. They are playing dice and casting mean glances around the room.
Set into the wall is a very sturdy door. The owners must be very security conscious as all counter measures have been taken against lockpickers and even magic.
You have interrupted a meeting of the Silverband. The large room is filled with rogues and hired armsmen. Alarmed by your intrusion, they draw weapons and attack.
You leave the Red Dragon inn.
Along with some obviously stolen jewelry and gems you find some notes. One details the expulsion of an assassin called Kynyaf for revealing Band secrets to outsiders.
The key found upon the man outside Ryn fits perfectly. The door swings open.
You take a moment to recover somewhat from your punishing ordeal.
Lacking the appropriate key, you move on.
A heavy locked door is set into the wall here. You won't be able to unlock it without alerting the smuggler nearby.
'Back off', one of them sneers, 'we don't like your kind around here.'
Stand your ground
Back off
The group stands as one. 'Looks like we get to earn our keep', one says menacingly as they advance toward you, weapons drawn.
The rest of the inn pointedly ignores your scuffle.
Now that you get a chance to look around, you see a large, well decorated room lined with desks and chests. The place gives the impression of a very organised and successful operation.
A rather tacky but ornate plaque reads 'Carclew Brothel, price of admision: 20 gold, enter one at a time'. Enter?
Who will enter?

Walking through the door, you realize too late that this is not quite what you expected of a brothel. That is, unless you expected several vicious looking characters to try to jump you as soon as you enter the room.
You hear a scream of terror from a woman to the east.
Another scream rings out. Its louder and is defintely coming from the south.
There is no woman in distress around the corner. Instead you find some very smug looking thieves with remarkable mimicry abilities. Needless to say they pounce on you.
A ladder leads down into the cellars.
Climb the ladder?
Back up
A ladder going up
A delicately crafted statue stands here. A plaque at the base reads 'In honour of Paltyr, the greatest thief of all time, and founding father of the Silverband'.
Upon closer inspection, you notice a small groove into which you could place an object.
An impressive looking locked chest stands before you. The Silverband have anti-magicked their locks. They have a deeply held belief in the old fashioned way of lockpicking.
Nothing that you possess seems remotely similar in shape to the groove so you move on.
The Silverband Emblem fits perfectly. You hear a movement of stone upon stone nearby.
Leave the building?
Some fine weapons rest against this weapons rack.

A note sits prominently on top of some otherwise uninteresting papers. It outlines a clandestine alliance formed between a 'Groat King' and the Runic Empire. There is also a map detailing the location of a secret Groat stronghold.

'I had given up hope of finding allies to join us against the Laerg. Please find the Selkies, they were a very shy and secretive race, and are probably far more loathe to deal with strangers in these dark times.'

'Show them this ruby and they will know you are an emissary of the Knockers. My great grandfather received it as a gift from the Selkies long ago. Perhaps they will join us against the Laerg. Otherwise, I fear we will not hold out much longer.' He sits.
The Selkies growl as you approach and disappear among the rocks. You are unable to follow them.

You hold the ruby given to you by the Knockers aloft. The Selkies stir into action when they catch sight of it. One moves to a large rock and knocks upon it. An opening appears in the rock and the Selkie motions for you to follow him inside.
They eye your possessions hungrily but do not make a move against you.
'One of my trusted armsmen, Teutates, will be posted in the Inn. Seek him out after your investigation.' Godolphin bids you farewell and heads north to Ryn.
A heavily armed man sits alone at this table. He wears the emblem of Lord Godolphin. He nods as you pass by.

You tell Godolphin's armsman, Teutates, about the Groat stronghold. He seems shocked. 'We knew the Silverband were getting in with the Runics ... but to find out there is a hostile force within our borders...'
He instructs you to investigate the stronghold and report back to Goldophin in Ryn if you discover anything. He takes his leave of the inn.

Before you can speak, he introduces himself. 'The name's Teutates. I know why you are here, the thieves have practically taken over the place ... their headquarters must be in here somewhere. I'll keep an eye on the exit... make sure no one leaves.'
Some thieves and armsmen are in here, counting loot and arguing with each other. As you open the door they draw their weapons and attack.

The namesake of this inn stands before you: The statue of a majestic red dragon rearing up on its claws and baring its fangs. The main room of the inn lies beyond to the south. A friendly looking innkeeper tends bar in the centre.
What was once an attractive pub garden has become an overgrown nest of weeds. A network of alleys extends both east and west.
You search through some uninteresting papers and ledgers detailing the day to day running of the inn.
You set off a lightning trap. Electric energy pulses from the chest to strike your party.
Thieves make the jump on you!
A rat scurries past you.
You followed the Selkie far below the surface through an exceptionally damp tunnel. Crude stoneworks appear before you. The Selkies move towards the gates.

Selkie guards lining the stoneworks exchange angry guttural snarls with the Selkies that accompany you. Clearly they are not happy at the thought of strangers entering the halls. The exchange ends as you again loft the ruby. The gate opens.

Selkie males, females and pups play together noisily in this flooded cavern. As you approach the males start to line the shores as the pups dive below the surface. The females start to emit a low growl. You decide to leave. Quickly.
Your Selkie guide growls at you in barely comprehendible speech, 'you had better see the Bull. He will want to have words with you.' The Selkie gestures towards the east with his silky flipper.

An enormous Selkie basks along the smooth stones here. He turns his enormous, blubbery body as you approach. 'Bipeds', he growls, 'I never thought I would see the likes of you in my caves. What brings you here?'

You relate to him the situation in the Knocker caves and the Laerg problem. He nods his great whiskery head as you speak. 'When I was a pup, the bulls would speak of our ancient friends, the Knockerkin.'

'One tale spoke of a Knocker who found some lost pups and brought them back to us. We Selkin have not forgotten. However, we cannot leave our caves to join battle against these reptiles. Not only do we have to guard the lake entrance against the Laerg ..

'But we must guard the underground springs against a malevolent water spirit called the Loireag. As you can see, our flippers are tied... It is with great shame that I must refuse the Knockers our assistance.' His whiskers wilt.

A large cow beside the Bull growls. 'You are such a walrus brain. If these brave bipeds were to remove the threat of the Loireag, we could stop skulking under this lake. We fled our homes along the coast to escape the vile sea-witch, Loireag.

'Pups began disappearing in the underground lakes and we knew she had found us again.' The cow is trembling with rage now. 'Find her and end her life and we Selkies we will rise against the Laerg with you.' The Bull balefully nods in assent.
'Will you confront the Loireag?' the Bull growls.
'Fair enough, it's not your battle.'

'Very good', the cow growls, 'legend tells of a great sandcastle that the Loireag resides in. We know she lives along the coast west of the mountains. Rumour among the seafolk is that she is a water spirit cast out from the ocean for her evil ways.'

'Some kindly water spirits gave us this token when they heard of our plight. Supposedly it is necessary to defeat her. Take it. I don't know what it does ... you will have to figure that out for yourselves. Return to us when she is vanquished.'

The Bull awaits you. 'You defeated the Loireag. All of the seafolk are celebrating this day. A great evil has been removed from the waters. Now we can move against the Laerg.' The cow speaks next 'We have been planning in your absence.'

'We have known the Laerg for generations. They have been content to reside in their subterranean lairs until recently. Now they make concerted attacks with such organisation that we can only surmise they have a new leadership structure directing them.'

'Our plan is to mount a force of Selkie and Knockers against the Laerg to draw them out of their strongholds beneath the mountains. This will give you the opportunity to enter their lair and remove whatever is organising them.'

'Anyone powerful enough to defeat the Loireag can dispatch whoever is behind the Laerg. Our scout will bring you to the Laerg stronghold through our secret mountain paths. From there it will be up to you. Most of the Laerg should be on the surface.'

The Selkie scout ushers you from the Selkie caves and through a network of tight tunnels and paths. From a high cliff you see a host of Laerg waiting before a massive mountain. They move off to the east. The Selkie guides you towards the Laerg caves.

The Selkies brings you the gates of the Laerg stronghold. He whispers 'I shall join my people fighting on the surface, good luck, there will no doubt be some guards left behind.' He then quickly scampers away.

As you move towards the entrance of the Laerg stronghold you see a great battle taking place before the mountain. Hordes of Laerg engage outnumbered Selkie and Knocker units. You return to the cave before you are spotted.
As you leave the Laerg stronghold you see lines of dispirited Laerg soldiers returning. Many look wounded and weary. They barely acknowledge your presence and file past you into the caves.
A small group of Laerg have been left to guard the gates. They attack as the see you approach.
You enter the Laerg stronghold.
A group of Laerg guards wait here, sulking because they were left out of the great battle. Your entrance makes their day.
There isn't much of interest in here.
A group of young Laerg play here. They are boldly chasing each other and pretending to be warriors. They quickly scamper into tiny holes when they notice you however.
This large cavern seems to be the main garrison of the stronghold. There is enough room for thousands of Laerg to ready themselves for battle in here. Thankfully, they are not here at present.
Rows of burrows line this cave network. It seems to completely deserted however.
There do not appear to be any Laerg in these caves thankfully. The burrows along the cave walls look like they could hold hundreds of thousands.
A lone Laerg sits here on his scaly rump. He seems completely insane and mutters something archaic to do with a great serpent that lives deep in the caves. He's no threat so you leave him be.
A big Laerg turns to you as you open the door. He directs his underlings to attack, crying 'protect the prissss'nerss'.
This door is locked with a crude Laerg mechanism. So crude in fact it is easily overcome.
Beyond the door you see several chained individuals. A Selkie and a Knocker are here and also oddly there is a man who looks like a Karnak.

The Selkie and Knocker are overjoyed at your presence. They explain that they were captured by the Laerg while on scouting expeditions. You explain the situation and they decide to join their kin in the battle on the surface. They leave.

The man turns to you 'I can't believe what I got myself into here. I never believed in monsters until I was captured by those walking reptiles. I worked for the Smuggler's Guild in Ryn and was looking for their abandoned outpost on the coast.'

'Its clear now why the outpost was abandoned. They never mentioned these creatures to me', he says bitterly. I used the old smugglers path through the mountains north of here, near the source of the river. Use it to get back to Karnak land.' He departs.

You approach what looks like the central meeting place of the Laerg. A large Laerg wearing some kind of badge of office has been nailed to a stone in the centre of a cleared area. His left foot has been chewed off. The meaning of this is lost to you.
Some Laerg are wandering through the caves. Upon seeing you they attack!
Some angry looking serpents rear their heads above the water and attack.
An angry looking serpent rears its head above the surface and attacks.
Several young dragons are here fighting over a half eaten serpent. At your approach they forget the serpent and attack.
A loud growl emanates from the cave before you. Brownish scales as thick as plate mail litter the floor. The creature that awaits you must be enormous.

A huge earth coloured dragon sits before you in a nest made of bones. Statues of fleeing humanoids line the walls, their faces frozen in fear. The dragon speaks in a voice that shakes the cave walls 'Tasty morsels come to feed me, hmmm...'

'I grow so tired of serpents and Laerg. Their meat is so tough, but you look like juicy mammals.' He slavers at the thought. 'I told the Laerg to bring me the seals and the little hairy men but you will certainly do.'
Hungrily, the dragon rears to its full height and attacks. Two of its brood join the fight.

You search along the cave. Unfortunately it seems that this type of dragon is not the treasure collecting sort. However, you find sort interesting things among the bones and statues of the dragon's previous victims.
A tunnel leads deep into the bowels of the earth here. Enormous heat exudes from this hole. The very earth seems to churn below you.
You realize you would not be able to survive in that heat and back away from the hole.
A crude stone building lies before you. Behind it a dark lagoon stretchs off beyond your sight.
A crude stone doorway stands before you. It lies open.
The exit lies before you.
A lever sits here, embedded into the wall. Pull it?
A Laerg guard unit waits here. Upon seeing you they attack.
Two powerful Laerg guard this room. Each holds the leash of a ferocious looking reptile. As you open the door, the guards unleash the beasts and advance.
This is a large room with a sizeable wooden table in the middle of it. A group of Laerg are gathered around it eating what looks like fish and eels. They spring up as you enter the room and charge.
The Bank of New Caster
A Laerg shaman sleeps soundly in this room. Do you wish to wake him?
A barrel of rotten fish and chopped up eels.
The large cavern narrows to a small tunnel leading out into a large underground lagoon.  Enter?
The tunnel leads into a long cavern.
You descend into a small room. Pits line the floor each filled with a pool of revolting smelling ichor. The stuff seems to pulsate as if alive.
You walk into the tower and climb down a ladder to what looks like a former storage room.
A ladder descends into the darkness.
A ladder leads up.
Rough stone stairs lead down into the darkness.
Take the stairs?
Back up
Stairs lead up.
A starved and wretched looking Laerg shaman stands chained against the wall. He looks stunned to see you. 'How did you get in here', he hisses. 'I thought they had come to feed me to the great wyrm.'
Talk to the Laerg
Kill him
Nothing easier than killing a chained Laerg.

'Thank you', the Laerg hisses, 'they locked me in here for daring to question the wisssdom of the great wyrm. I usssed to be the High Ssshaman until I sspoke out against the sacrifices that the great wyrm was demanding of my people.'

'The wyrm wass gradually taking over all asspects of Laerg life. He ordered the Ssshamen to kill and sssacrifice our own people, our own offsspring. We had to invade other landsss to collect victims to hisss neverending hunger.'

'I decided to sspeak out against the wyrm when he ordered uss to perform experimentss on our own people to change them into mindlesss monsterss. For that I wass thrown in here and a new High Sshaman sselected. One asss bloodthirsty as the wyrm itsself.'

'Perhapsss you are oness to free uss of this wyrm ... but I think not. The wyrm iss unsstoppable. Besst you return to the ssurface.' The shaman thanks you again for freeing him and walks out of the cell.
A row of cells line the walls of this corridor. They appear to be empty.
A vain Laerg? You would not have thought it possible.
A ladder leads down into a very humid opening.
There is a ladder leading up at the back of this small cave.
This appears to be the High Shaman's personal pool. There is nothing here.
Upon careful inspection you notice that this torch is far more worn than the others. Pull it?
A hallway of doors stretches before you.
The High Shaman is here, apparently hiding. Realizing his plight, he makes a last desperate attack.
This cave leads up back into the Laerg building. Take it?
Stairs lead down into a dark cavern. Climb?
You enter a long cavern. You hear low growls  from the east.
Tall reptiles lunge at you from the dark, their wicked teeth glistening with poisonous venom.
Perched atop a ledge lies a perfectly round and smooth stone. Its surface seems to swim under the torchlight. Clearly the dragon valued it so you grab it for yourselves.
A grisly sight lies before you. Around a great stone by the side of the lagoon lies chained the skeletons of what looks like various races: Knockers, Selkies, Laerg and perhaps humans as well.

Their condition hints that they were devoured ferociously by something that shattered bones with its jaws. Deep claw marks are gouged into the stone surface. Nervously, you glance toward the lagoon. For the moment all is quiet.
A candle fills this cave with revolting, greasy smoke. Take it?
You leave the lagoon barge.

The Selkie Bull awaits you. He is heavily wounded but full of vitality. You tell him about the defeat of the dragon. 'Well done, Selkie-friend, our battle with the Laerg cost us dearly, and I am relieved to discover it was not in vain.'

'Sadly, most of our young bulls died in the fighting. We shall close our lairs for some time to recover. You may be the last to see one of our race for many years. Take this gift to remember us by. There is precious little that the sea does not know...'
The great Bull escorts you the surface, waves a great flipper and growls in farewell. He closes the stone entranceway.
Selkies fish among the dark waters here. They combine their chores with constant playing and splashing.
Piles of fish lie here on the smooth stones. The smell is overpowering and forces you back.
Some powerful Laerg chargers are kept penned up in here. They rush you when they smell you are not Laerg.

Penhaligon inspects the river flowing into the cave thoughtully. He says 'this underground lake must be the source of a river above ground, if we grab some wood and float ourselves to the surface we should be free of these infernal caves.'
You are surrounded by the devastation of war. Bodies of Knockers, Selkie and Laerg lie in great heaps. The carrion eaters have already descended. A powerful stench urges you to move along.
You hear something approaching you. If you withdraw you might be able to avoid whatever it is. Investigate?
Selkie guards hold the gate against you.
Selkie guards, eyeing the Knocker ruby, allow you passage.

A guardsmen informs you this is the town stockade. Behind him an ogre of a man watchs you behind locked bars. The guard nods at him, 'this drunken fool practically lives here. He loves nothing better then to drink and brawl.'
A well dressed man says 'Welcome to the bank of Ryn'.

'Welcome to the Tinner's Guild', the man says nonchalantly, 'we don't get too much interest in the Guild since the tin mines became unworkable. We mined out the one south of Carclew and then moved on to another one across the bay near the lakes.'

'But something happened. We disturbed some kind of spirit and it chased us out of the mine. No one has dared venture back since. Sadly, most of the Guild gave up mining after that and took to less honourable professions.'
'If you find the mine you'll see what I mean'. He returns to moping around doing nothing.
A bold sign reads 'Smugglers Guild'.
A man hails to you. 'Welcome to the Smugglers Guild, business is going very well. I expect you are here to join?', he asks expectantly.

'Of course you have. Now contrary to what you might have heard, smuggling is an ancient and honourable profession. Karnak smugglers are the finest in the known world.' He says proudly. 'Naturally our entry requirements are quite strict.'

'In order to join you must complete two missions to prove your courage and guile. Your first mission is to find our abandoned smuggling post over the mountains southeast of Carclew. Return when you have found it.'

'Well done, you found poor Fundy'. He says, 'I suspected he must be dead, but it is still sad news. As a fully fledged guild member you may now go downstairs and use the guild hall.' He points to the heavy door set into the eastern wall.
A sign on the door reads 'Welcome to the Ryn Guildhall'
Under the trapdoor, a ladder leads down into the gloom. Climb it?

'You found the abandoned smuggling post. Well done, now you must do the Guild a favour. One of our members has not reported back in some time. His name is Fundy and he was last heard to be searching for a path in the mountains north of Tre Garrick.'
'Find him or what's left of him and report back to me.' He turns away.
The half eaten body of a Karnak man lies here. His name is etched onto his cloak, it reads 'Fundy'. He was carrying some fine items.
Occupied with the body of Fundy as you are you don't notice the mountain cats until they pounce.
A horde of Laerg are gathered here. You retreat before they see you.
An empty cave.
Leave the Guildhall?
An individual who sums up the word 'seedy' gestures down the hallway and says 'Hey, check out the local brothel, it's a knockout' before ambling away.
Some drunken mercenaries attempt to relieve you of your possessions.
Godolphin greets you. 'Yes, I know about the Groat compound, my armsman told me. Please investigate it, my work here in Ryn continues to occupy me.' Goldolphin turns away.
The smuggler says 'nothing huh? Keep trying. We certainly can't allow just anyone to join. And if you can't even perform this simple task, well ...' He shrugs and looks away.
'Hmm, come back when you grow a backbone'. Cairbre turns his back on you.

Runic guards line the battlements of this impressive gate. 'You there, the pass is closed, back away.' They cry. 'Why don't you come out here and make us you sons of whores', you respond. That did it. The Runics open the gate and charge.

Wave after wave of Runic defenders charge forward to pummel you into submission. You awake; bound on horse drawn carts. Runic guards escort you to an imposing looking fortress near a mountainside. You pass the fortress and are carted through some gate.

Grim faced guards lift you off the carts and drag you into through a dark tunnel. Salt residue covers the floor and the walls. You are pushed into a large cell and untied. Several guards with spears hold them to your throats as this is done.

Godolphin is looking very pleased. 'We heard about your defeat of the Dragonriders. Word of such a deed carries through the land with great speed. Envoys from the Runic merchants came to us and have pledged to cease hostilities.'

'We have agreed to peace. We Karnaks shall keep our land and the Runics shall keep the land beyond the passes. Trade routes have opened once more. It seems they were after our precious tin, what little of it we have left.'

'I shall call on your services no longer, but I am sure that there are others who will call upon you. Rowan, the druid, for example seems to be harping on about something. Again, thank you.' Godolphin returns to running his small fiefdom.
Lord Godolphin greets you warmly. He seems preoccupied with various affairs of running his fiefdom and you take your leave. Of course as honoured guests you may always use your room.
Cairbre greets you. 'Well met again, my friends.' You briefly sup with him and then take your leave.

'You may keep your tawdry possessions,' a grinning guard says, 'without them you'd soon be hacked apart by the other prisoners here. We lock the scum of the empire in these pits and forget about them. Enjoy your new home. You won't last the night.'
'And don't bother trying to escape. The gates cannot be opened from the inside and a full battalion is barracked in the fortress outside.' The guards depart and you look around.

Four huge men approach you. They are pale from lack of sunlight and heavily scarred from constant fighting. 'What have we got here', one says looking at your possession, 'new meat, you're gonna learn from the start who rules these pits.' They attack.
There are other prisoners in this large room. They back away from you and ignore the incident.
The entrance to the pits stands before you. It remains locked no matter what you try.
Rotting food lines the base of this pit. It looks like the guards throw food in here from a chimney above. The chimney is unscalable.
Two Pit prisoners are waiting to jump you behind this door. 'Thats them', one says as they lunge for you.
A crude message has been scratched onto this heavy door. 'Leave yer salt blocks and you'll get yer food.'

Behind the door a group of ugly mean looking prisoners lounge around amid barrels of salt. They smell like animals it's difficult for you to stay in the same room as them. One lazily gestures to the corner, 'leave your salt over there.'

When you do nothing he scrutinizes you. 'Hey, wheres yer salt? I don't recognize your ugly faces - you look like new meat.' He taps the others and states 'looks like we got new meat here boys, time for an initiation.' The other grin viciously.
As they advance toward you,  you realize now would be a good time for extreme violence as you doubt your 'initiation' would involve sharing tea and crumpets with them.
They smell even worse in death. You search the room and find only barrels of salt. What a waste of time.

You enter a large room full of rough furniture and pathetic sickly looking prisoners. They look pale, underfed and devoid of hope. All eyes turn to the door when you enter. You see fear in their eyes, which lifts as they focus upon you.

A sickly looking old man approaches you. 'You must be new here, choose a cell and get to work. There's plenty left, nobody lives here too long. As for food - you don't get fed unless you scrape up enough salt blocks.'
'Trade the salt for food with the big men in the hallway. They control access to the food. Don't try messing with them, they beat that crazy Karnak up pretty good when he tried to get to the food.'
You explain to the old man that you dispatched the gang. He rushs to tell the others and they hobble past you down the hall.
The ugly men sleep in here on the floor like the animals they have become.
Beyond this door is the entrance to the salt mines. Realizing there is nothing there for you, you close the door.

A battered man lies here. At first you think he might be dead, but an eyelid cracks open and he slowly rises. 'Come to finish me off have you, well you'll see I won't go out without a fight'. He rises to his feet and enters a battle stance.

Realizing this must be Penhaligon, you explain your recent exploits to him. After some food and water from your supplies he seems more steady on his feet. 'Hail and well met, a friend of Godolphin is a friend of mine.'
'The beating I took at the hands of those brutes who hoard the food was a blessing from Arn in disguise. As I lay here quietly, I heard strange noises coming from the walls.'

'I have been scraping at this wall for some time, waiting for my strength to return, but as no one would feed me I grew gradually weaker and weaker. But I could hear movement beyond the wall and possibily some kind of speech.'

'I heard legends among the older prisoners that the salt pits were once occupied by an ancient underground race that fled the overwhelming numbers of the Runics. We can't escape through the main gate but maybe this race has carved tunnels out of here.'

'I am sure something moves beyond this wall. With a little more digging we could break  through.' Left with no alternative you dig through the wall where Penhaligon indicates. Eventually a crawlspace is made.'
As you dig the tunnel, a portion of the floor gives way. Casting a torch down reveals a larger tunnel beneath you.
Climb down
Stay in the Pits
A room of full of badly constructed beds smelling of unwashed bodies and mildew stands before you.
A few prisoners lie in here on their beds. They refuse to open their eyes when you try to rouse them and wheeze horribly. You assume this is what happens to you after too much time in the salt mines.
There is a row of rough beds lined up against the wall in this room.
The strange rock being shatters into tiny, sharp fragments.
Looks like this cave is your only possible exit. You hear the distant roar of a waterfall. Surely this lake is the source of a river above ground.

Left with little choice but to try it you bundle some stout mushroom stems together to form flotation bundles. Knowing that this will either take you to the surface or to some dead end in which you'll be hopelessly stuck, you jump in.

The water is freezing and smells strongly of musty earth. You float along the river as it gradually coarses its way through the rock. You travel in near darkness and constantly scrape against the walls.
After an age sunlight suddently blinds you just before you are thrown over a small waterfall into a lake. Reaching the surface you see the mountain from which you just exited looming above you.
A pair of large dirty humans must have heard you and come to investigate. You attempt to speak to them but they don't understand and attack you savagely.

As you draw near the hideous plant in centre of this cavern leads out a shrill cry. You cover your ears in pain. Your mind turns hazy the pain is so extreme. Huge shapes rush from the eastern tunnel and attack you.

The creatures have made a kind of rough lair in this large cave. Piling mushrooms into mounds to sleep on is the best their limited intelligence could come up with. Still, its their home and they they fight to the death to protect it.
After searching their lice ridden bodies you examine the room. There is little of interest except for a fine ring hidden among some piled stones.
There is a huge underground lake here. The lake empties noisily into a large hole in the western wall. Other than that there is nothing here.
You stumble upon some snakes feasting upon the corpse of a giant shaggy human. They turn to you for fresh blood.
A Runic guard shouts out to you. 'These gates are closed to the likes of you, back away.' Hundreds of crossbows train upon you. You back away.
Nothing here but an empty cave.
You hear the faint noises of someone or something moving ahead. Perhaps if you moved very stealthily you could catch a glimpse of whoever was making the sound.

You tell Byrm of your battle with the Earth Dragon. He nods sagely 'you have done very well. On behalf of the Knockerkin I thank you. Please accept this ancient stone as a token of my appreciation. I have been its warder for many years.'
'But something tells me that you will have need of it to fight a greater evil.' He hands you a small ion stone and leaves to tend the Knockers wounded in the great battle.
You tell Byrm of your encounter with the Selkies. 'You are doing well my young friends, but the Laerg continue to harass us. Perhaps there is something more you should be doing.' He turns away.
Runic guards let you pass.
Byrm turns to you 'the Selkies, my friends, they are who you should be looking for'. He turns away.
You stumble upon some shark faced humanoids combing the beach. They amble towards you.
You have stumbled upon a Reef Grimal lair. Hordes of them pour out and attack you.
In the back of the cave you find their treasure trove. It consists of items either washed up on the beach or perhaps taken from stranded ships.
You pass through the sand dunes and see a opening in the dark rocks ahead.
Rocky cliffs surround you and sand dunes cover the eastern part of the beach. To the west a small lake has formed against the cliffs. A trail heads north up into the mountains.
The dune erupts around you as huge sand coloured crabs uncover themselves and scuttle towards you.
What the took it be a rock suddenly lurchs towards you pincers raised.
Giant black crab shells litter the ground. Great claw and fang marks score the shells. Clearly some enormous creature feeds off the giant crabs. Perhaps it lives in the cave to the east.

You have learned that sand creatures tend to burrow under the sand and attack from below. You prod a loose section of sand and a huge reptilian head appears. It looks very annoyed that its ambush was ruined and moves towards you.

Sadly, you still haven't learned that sand creatures tend to burrow into the sand and attack from below. Huge wings flap sand into your face blinding you. Before you can regain your vision a huge sand dragon attacks.
Amid some treasure in the back of the cave you find a skeleton wearing armour and a ring of superb craftmanship.
Clearing the tight rock tunnels you see a bizarre sight in front of you. An enormous sandcastle has been sculpted in the middle of a sandy lake.
The sandcastle looms above you. Flakes of sand fall off of it as you scrape it with a blade. An entrance lies ahead.
Enter?
There is a pile of stones at your feet.

The skipping rock hits the stone to your northwest, then bounces up to richochet off the north wall. It travels southwest to richochet off the west wall, then bounces on a stone to the south east. It continues southeast and bounces off another stone.
It then smashes into the statue.
The skipping rock bounces for a time before coming to rest in the water with a mighty splash. The chilling water drenchs your party.
You pick up another skipping rock.
The water is freezing. You quickly back up.

You come to a water filled room. It is unnaturally cold here. Stones stand in the water with no clear pattern. In the south wall of the room an alcove contains the statue of a webbed man. Two piles of skipping rocks lie on the stones.
You hear the scratching of enormous sandblocks moving.

A large coffer stands here, decorated with scenes from the ocean. It appears to be made from coral. Inside is a small sandcastle which looks like a scale model of the building you stand in. Beside it is a pendant.
Upon closer examination the pendant seems to flow as if filled with water. It smells strongly of the sea.
When you try to remove the pendant it instantly rematerialises inside the coffer. It isn't going anywhere.

The token give to you by the Selkies begins to glow in the presence of this pendant. The pendant starts to transform before your eyes. It loses the sense of fluidity and gradually turns to a greyish dull stone consistency. It now smells like rotten fish.
Somewhere high above you, you hear an agonzied shriek. You return the putrid smelling pendant to its coffer and close the lid.
The sound of slithering brings your attention to the darkness at the end of the hall. You sense a malevolent presence. Chilling water floods toward you.
The flood chills you to the bone.
The horrible woman mockingly gestures for you to advance towards her.

The hideous sea hag bellows at you in a voice like a crashing wave. The water moves on her command to form solid ice. You looks very satisfied with her trick. You cannot force your way through it no matter what you try.

The water reachs out to grab your ankles as if alive but fails to take hold. Upon seeing this the woman shrieks in frustration. 'So its true, my tie to the ocean has been severed. I shall destroy you for this.' She gestures and giant black crabs appear.
You move to engage the Loireag.

As the Loireag is dealt her deathblow she melts into a pool of water. A booming voice rings out, 'Loireag, you shall return to the depths to face my justice. Your days of evil upon the land are over.'

The castle begins to shake. The roar of a huge wave grows louder and louder. Just before the sound becomes deafening you find yourself upon the beach. It has been swept clean except for a shield. The ocean has reclaimed its own.
The contents of the chest are now yours to plunder.
Trap detected.
Trap disabled.
There doesn't seem to be a trap.
Lock picked successfully.
Ouch, you set off a poison needle.
The door opens.
A locked door stands before you.
That doesn't seem to work.
You failed to pick the lock.
Beyond this door lies the private quarters of the innkeeper.
The shaman's have a sitting room in here.

You look in the mirror and a glamour overwhelms you. You are back in your home town after years of adventuring. You rap on your grandmother's door. She opens the door and regards you. You proudly brandish the mystic sword you found in the lich's lair.

She regards you silently. You look beyond her, 'where are my brothers?' you hear yourself ask. 'They died in the war', she says simply, 'years ago. You should have been there to protect them; instead you chose to leave us to pursue your empty dreams.'
'Get away from my house', she rasps, 'you are dead to me.' She slams the door. You know this isn't your memory. The glamour fades and a bright red 'H' is left on the mirror.

You look in the mirror and a glamour overwhelms you. Your party walks through Tre Garrick hunting down and butchering the local townsfolk. Men, women and children fall to your blades and magic. Finally you stand alone surrounded by corpses.
You know this isn't your memory. The glamour fades and a bright red 'E' is left on the mirror.

As you open the door an image forms. A child walks toward the bed. The ghostly body of a woman lies upon the bed. 'Mommy, mommy, I hurt myself'. The woman is nonresponsive. 'I hurt myself real bad', the child whines. The woman raises her head slightly.

Her eyes open a crack. She looks at the child and then closes them and rests her head. The child turns toward you. She has clawed her eyes out. They rest in her hand. She opens her mouth to speak but before she can the image fades.
There is definitely something warped about this inn. A bright red 'M' appears on the far wall.

As you open the door an image forms. Through the snow a group of adventurers are tracking a snow white wolf. The wolf appears on a ledge ready to defend its territory. It howls before jumping down to attack the group.

They hack it to pieces and then skin its coat. The snow is stained red. Red footprints trail off after the departing party. Other wolves gradually gather around the dead wolf and lift their snouts together to howl.
The image fades leaving in its wake a bright red 'A'  on the far wall.

As you open the door an image forms. A party of human warriors shrieks war cries and rides into an orc village. Orc villagers attempt to stave off the attack but are quickly overwhelmed. There are no orc warriors present to fight off the attacks.

The orc females and young are round up and slain. The image fades and is replaced by another. A party of orc warriors shrieks war cries and rides into a human village. The villagers attempt to stave off the attack but are quickly overwhelmed.

There are no warriors present to fight off the attacks. The village females and young are round up and slain. The images repeat themselves several times. You get the idea. Finally a bright red 'S' appears on the wall.
A heavy wooden door stands before you. The image of a large mouth appears in the door. A sardonic expression plays across its lips. 'What have you learned?', it says.
The mouth fades and the door opens.
The mouth says 'no' and disappears.

A man is shackled to the wall. His wild eyes turn to you as you open the door. 'Kill me, please, kill me. I can't take this anymore. The visions ...' His eyes roll back in his head and he slumps in the chains. He fades into nothingness.
A bright red 'R' appears against the far wall.
An old man sits alone beside a roaring fire. He turns as your open the door. 'Would you like to know real despair?' he asks grimly. 'Well I'll tell you.'

'You don't actually exist. Your childhood memories are fake. Your present is totally controlled by an entity who couldn't care less if you lived or died. You have no future either. You are trapped in an endless loop. Soon the entity will move on ...'

'... to other pursuits and you will be obliterated. Your triumphs are meaningless, your relationships with others are simulated and you yourselves are nothing more than just pointless numbers and letters.'

Mercifully his rant fades away. You know you exist. Simply because your fate lies in the hands of greater beings does not make you an automaton - simply mortal. At least that's what you tell yourself. A bright red 'F' appears on the far wall.

You gaze into the mirror in this room. A glamour overcomes you. You are very young. You stand in the common area of the dwelling where you grew up. The furniture is enormous compared to your small size. The front door suddenly bursts open.

Your father rushes into the room. 'They're coming', he shouts, fear in his voice. He gestures to you, 'hide the child in the cellar' he shouts. You are whisked up in your mother's arms and put in a dark room. Above you a trapdoor shuts with a bang.

The sound of heavy furniture being placed over the trap door follows. You are alone in the dark. The damp smell of earth and mildew surround you. Roots from the tree you enjoyed climbing have penetrated the rough walls and scrape against you.
Above you a loud crash erupts followed by boots tramping into the room. The clash of arms is brief. Your father lets out a scream but it is brutally cut short. A loud thump hits the floor above you.'

Your mother starts screaming and doesn't stop for several minutes. Her screams abruptly stop. The silence is deafening. Footsteps cross the room. You press against the earth, willing yourself to sink into it; to merge into the soft earth like a worm.
The earth begins to grip your wrists and ankles. Fear rises like a lump into your throat. The trap door above slowly creaks open.
Light from above floods in. You close your eyes in pain. Rough hands grab you and drag you upstairs. You keep your eyes tight shut. You are dragged outside. You open your eyes.

Your mother and father stand before you. Your entire clan is assembled here, in a ring around you. They look at you with a mix of sadness and contempt. Your father speaks gruffly 'you failed the only test that matters. You are not welcome here anymore.'
Your clan escorts you to the edge of the village. They leave without a word. Noone looks back as they stalk away. You realize that now you are one of the kinless. The rest of the story you know.
A bright red 'A' appears on a worm that crawls across your foot.
A small child stands at the end of this hall. He seems to be waiting for you. He beckons to you. 'Come closer', he chimes in a high pitched voice.
'closer ...'
'closer ...'
The small child stands directly before you. At this range you notice his eyes are blood red and feral. The child laughs and claps his hands. An apparition falls from the ceiling and attacks.
The figure falls to the ground. Only then do you see the thin wires attaching it to the ceiling. The child laughs in delight and runs around the corner.

The child stands here. 'I hope you enjoyed my images and toys' he says, a huge grin cracking his face. 'It took me an awfully long time to think them up, although you provided some excellent memories yourself.'
'But the game must end here, sadly. I haven't designed another level yet. Sorry'. The child's body collapses and a ghostly apparition bursts forth and launches itself at you.

The apparition fades away into oblivion. The child lies on the floor. His breathing is strained. Cautiously, you examine him. His eyes have returned to normal and he looks like any typical Karnak child. His eyes blink open and he looks at you.
'Who are you? Where's my daddy?', he says weakly. 'Would you please take me home?' he asks pitifully.

'Oh thank you', he beams. You carry the child through the inn without incident and follow his directions to a house in the north part of Tre Garrick. Instead of directing you into the house the child directs you to a small garden around the back.

A small grave stands amid some violets. 'My daddy says my mommy lives here now, but I want her back. You saved me from the horrid building. You can do anything. Wake her up so we can be together again.'
Raise the woman
Leave the child

You begin to intone the ancient incantations of raising the dead. The child stops you 'thank you, your intentions were enough. Clearly you temper your strength with compassion. You are a credit to the forces of Good.' The boy begins to transform.

'A very good reason to knock you out of the war before you grow too powerful' growls the demonic being before you. 'I am the Child of Night and your bedtime story ends here.' The grave erupts like a giant scab as a horde of lesser demons pour forth.
You suddenly find yourself back in the corridor, as if you had never left. However, the feeling of dread has lifted from the inn.

The child wails in anguish. He runs off around the house and out of sight. You are left alone with the cold grave. You turn to leave and find yourself in the inn as if you had never moved. You are alone.
The child rises to his feet and rushes past you down the hall. His footsteps fade into silence.
You are unable to leave the inn. The circle has begun and it must be completed.

You leave the accursed inn and breath fresh air again. Walking back into the centre of town you notice your surroundings have altered somewhat. The buildings seem decayed and rotten. The cobblestones at your feet have come away from the road.

The most alarming change is the townsfolk however. They shamble about with vacant eyes. Their skin hangs in strips from their skeletal bodies. A crowd forms around you. Festering tongues lick swollen lips as they advance hungrily upon you.

As the last body drops to the ground the scene changes. You are surrounded by the bodies of the townsfolk of Tre Garrick. The mayor lies dead at your feet. Survivors of your massacre flee through the gates, clutching their belongings.
Your hear the wicked laughter of a small child fade away and then utter silence. The town is now deserted.

'If it is fame and riches you seek the Inn has plenty. It was once the grandest establishment in the land until a shadow passed over the town. Something evil lurks there now, please free us of this curse.' He says. You leave, the door locks behind you.
You enter the cursed inn.
The inn is deserted but otherwise normal. However, you can't help but feel a sense of dread and fear permeating the building.
Cautiously, you climb the stairs.
