You descend the stairs.
The inn is deserted.
The lighthouse is deserted. Perhaps thats because the light is only tended after dusk.
A retired sailor greets you. Caswal - wants his anchor back.

Some bodies have washed up along the shore of this small lake. They are small and furry with feline features. They seem to have been stripped of their possessions. Close inspection reveals blackened tongues - a telltale sign of death by poison.
These must be the Groat emissaries the Queen spoke of.
The hole leads down into dark water. Simplistic fishing poles lie against the rack beside it. Barrels of salted fish stand against the wall. You now have a good understanding of the Laerg diet.
Some bored looking Laerg stand guard in this hallway. They jump at the chance to engage in their favourite sport: combat.

A Shaman is berating some enormous and grotesque looking creatures in this room. They cringe at his voice. He stops when he sees you and claps his clawed hands, 'Exsscellent, a live tessst of the creashhions.'
Upon closer inspection of these grotesque creatures you notice that they resemble Laerg but are much larger with heads full of teeth.

This is either a torture chamber or some madman's workshop. Barrels full of blood, gore and scales stand against the west wall. A table with blood encrusted manacles stands against the far wall. A dead Laerg lies strapped to the table.

His face is a grimace of agony. One of his legs has swelled up to an unbelievable size. Hard ridges have grown along his shoulders. To add insult to injury someone has drawn 'Reject - dispose' in red on his leathery chest.

You open the door to see a very irritated Laerg wearing a blood smeared smock before you. 'Consstant interruptshhions,' he snarls, 'I will ssssilencce you for good'. He attacks. Another Laerg in the room joins him.
There some vials full of strong smell liquid here.
Amid some indecipherable papers full of anatomical drawings and scribbled notes you find a journal.

The journal relates the history of Laerg research into attempting to purify their race by combining it with what is described as the offspring of the Great Wyrm. The Laerg have discovered that they can use some toxic substance to achieve this.

The Great Wyrm directed the Laerg to do this. The rest of the journal goes on and on about the glorious beauty and wonder of this Great Wyrm and its eternal wisdom and how the duty of the Shamans is to obey its every whim.
Horribly mishapen skeletons and skulls dot the floor of this room. This must be where failed experiments are dumped.
Some of the hideously deformed Laerg are in here training with spiked clubs. They particularly enjoy smashing rocks and other objects. As you walk in they assume you are more objects to be smashed.
Too bad enhancing intelligence was not one of the priorities of the Laerg researchers.

A group of powerful looking Laerg guard this hallway. A Shaman wearing a huge collection of gaudy jewelry sees you and rushes to the south and through a doorway. The rest advance upon you croaking 'protect the High Ssshaman'
The door to the south slams shut.

You enter a lavishly decorated room. From the plush carpet to the decorated candle holders in the corners you can tell the Laerg who lives here is trying to adopt an air of civility. The room is deserted.
This looks like the lair of the shark faced beasts you met. It is deserted.
Hidden in a false bottom of a barrel of soiled Laerg laundry (words cannot describe what this is like) you find a fine collection of jewelry.
The chest of drawers contains some extremely vulgar clothes that you can't imagine a Laerg would wear. Some of the robes look interesting though.

Amid some papers detailing the day to day running of Laerg religious life cover you find a treatise on the natural superiority of the Laerg race. Chosen by the Great Wyrm because of this superiority they are destined to rule the world.

The Laerg will swarm across the surface subjugating all races and peoples. All those who deny the leadership of the Great Wyrm will be cast into a lake of fire. The Great Wyrm will reward the faithful with eternal life and incredible power.
In other words, it's the usual megalomaniac claptrap.

Some of the books on the shelves include: recipes for Selkie stew and Knocker pie, several books of Laerg history with pages torn out, a tome on the history of the Laerg shamans with the final chapter removed, and a well thumbed book on Laerg jewelry.
You walk through a secret tunnel.
Some Laerg beasts lounge around in this damp room. They sniff the air as you enter. Realizing you are not Laerg they attack.
He wakes with a start and stares at you. His reptilian eyes are wide with shock and his tongue nervously darts in and out of his mouth. He jumps out of bed and attacks.
Hidden under his bed you find a staff with radiates power.
A magnificent statue of a dark earth coloured dragon stands at the head of this room. Mats for kneeling in prayer lie before it. The room is deserted.
A sturdy looking door stands here.
Some Laerg guards wait on the other side of the door.
A family of griffons live in this high cave. They are enraged that you would enter their territory. They swoop upon you.
A hunting pack of giant spiders have made their lair here.
Exit the manorhouse?

Rows of statues line this stately hall. A carpet of superb craftmanship lines the tiled floor. Several vacant eyed townsfolk wander listlessly through the hall. One statue lies in pieces against the north wall as if struck by a blow of incredible force.

A finely gilded throne dominates this deserted room. Obvious signs of recent violence are scattered throughout. The charred remains of armoured guards lie around the throne. Some intense heat must have struck them, welding armour to flesh.
A well groomed garden stands here. The garden is showing recent signs of neglect however. The neatly trimmed bushes are beginning to lose their precise lines.
Some fine robes are hung on this rack.
Some food is stored here, still reasonably fresh. Some fine bottles of wine to accompany them are also here.
This room is a shambles. Some incredible force was directed against the southwest wall shattering half of the table and reducing its target to a burnt husk in the corner.
What looks like the common dining hall is now a deserted shambles. Chairs are overthrown, cutlery and crockery are scattered along the long wooden tables and on the floor.
Some miscellanous equipment has been left here.
The manor's kitchen stands in here. It was apparently hastily abandoned. Some now rock hard bread dough lies atop a tabletop. Pots full of cold stew hang over the braziers.

The owner of this manor must have had refinement and a taste for the finer things in life. A small but elegant bathing pool stands in the centre of this room. Complex murals line the walls and rich mosaics line the bottom of the pool.
A pile of mundane papers stand atop the bureau. A half written letter catchs your eye and you read it. It is addressed to Lord Godolphin of Carclew.

'Lord Godolphin, I have always held your advice in the highest of regard. However, I must respectfully dissent from the path that you have chosen. Granted, there is much about the Runics that calls for caution and care.'

'We know little about them and what designs, if any, they have for our land. This is why I propose we trade with them and learn as much as we can through peaceful means. They seem interested only in trade and commerce, not blood and invasion.'

'I have spoken at length with the Guildmasters of Ryn on this matter. They are in agreement with myself. Only through peaceful trade relations with the Runics can the fear that leads to pointless war be averted.'

'You are a puissant warrior, but this situation requires diplomacy not battle. The Guildmasters and myself are in agreement. If your son's stronghold continues to block trade through the eastern passes we shall be forced to use the secret passes ...

' ... to reach the Runic city. Join us in this endeavour and cease your provocations of the Runics. We should be pleased to have them as neighbours. I need not remind you that they quickly dispatched the Orcs who used to hold power in that region.'

'I am thankful that that brutal people have been scattered and a civilized race stands in their place. Heed my counsel, Godolphin, the sword is not the answer. I meet with Runic trade agents on the morrow and shall inform you of the outcome. Mordin'

The possessions of whomever was staying in this guest room are still here. Some notes and ledgers reveal that the occupant was a Runic trade agent recently arrived to meet with the Laird to discuss opening up trade routes.

This room has been completely smashed. All the furniture in the room seems to have been burnt to a cinder except for a sturdy looking metal trunk in the corner. The stone floor in the south of the room has been melted by some incredible force.
Inside the trunk you find some potions and scrolls and a journal relating the experimentation of what you assume was the Lord's wizard.
You deduce that the wizard was experimenting with control of lightning and energy. The last journal entry refers to attempting to summon some mysterious entity to assist in this goal.
A locked chest stands before you.
The chest opens.
Inside the chest you find the Lord's treasury and a brass key.
Descend the stairs?
Ascend the stairs?
A ladder descends into the stone floor. Climb?
A ladder leads up. Climb?
Carefully hidden in the intricate wood carving of this sarcophagus is a key hole.
Try as you might the lock will not budge without the proper key.
Using the Lord's key you open the casket. Inside you find a skeleton wearing magnifent armour, gauntlets and a fine helm. Do you touch the items?
You feel a presence in the room. Something tugs at your minds as if your very thoughts are being probed. As quickly as it arrived the presence dissipates without explanation.
The hidden passage leads to a cramped room containing only a simple wooden sarcophagus and an airhole in the ceiling.
A heavy stone sarcophagus rests here. It is engraved with the names of former heads of the Mordin family.
Some of the glowing daemons are gathered down here. They attack upon seeing you.
Some daemons are waiting beyond this door. They move purposely toward you.

A large holding pen stands in the back of what is clearly the manor's dungeon. A collection of townsfolk, some Karnak armsmen and a man in blue armour stand behind metal bars. The bars seem to be humming with energy.
A townsman who seems tired and fearful but with his wits about him sees you and cries 'Careful, the bars are trapped'.
The humming bars stand before you. On the other side the prisoners watch and wait expectantly. They can offer no advice on how to remove the bars.
The electrical energy strikes the humming bars and the humming desists. You may now pass the bars.
That has no effect.
A group of worried townsmen rush past you as soon as the barrier is removed. They are frantic with fear and claw at each other to make it out of the dungeons.

Two weary looking Karnak armsmen stand here. 'Thank you for the timely rescue,' one says, 'I don't know what those winged horrors were, but they were slowly escorting groups of us upstairs to do Arn knows what.'
'Our Lord is dead and our town laid waste by these beings. We shall travel to Carclew and swear fealty to Godolphin if he takes us in. There is nothing for us here now.' They stalk off.

A man in blue armour stands here apart from the others. 'Greetings and thank you for my deliverance', he says with a stiff formality. 'I cannot explain what took place in this town. I arrived last night as part of an escort of some trade agents.'

'They and the rest of the troop were taken by these strange beasts upstairs. With your permission I shall make my report to the prefecture in New Caster.' You assume this must be a Runic soldier. Do you allow him to leave?
'Thank you', he says formally and leaves the dungeon.
'Very well,' the Runic says wearily, 'I have my duty to uphold'. He lashs out at you.

Most of the books on this bookshelf are concerned with gardening. One book relates the rather uninteresting history of Tre Mordin: long ago a great warrior of legend, Teague, the founder of the Mordin family, pacified the area and built a settlement.

Over time, people flocked to the safety of the settlement and a thriving town eventually developed. Tre Mordin means 'Place of Mordin' or 'Farmstead of Mordin' in the old language. The rest of the collection is even less interesting.

A book on the history of the Mordin family lies on the shelf. One reference attracts your attention. The first Mordin was a great warrior who was blessed with a suit of armour upon completing some quest apparently set by Arn, the moon goddess.
Some fine wines are kept locked in here.
The Lord's armour stands here. It is in fine condition and looks like it hasn't seen action in some time.
Some antique jewelry has been locked in here.
Hidden underneath a chest of drawers full of the Lord's finely woven clothes, a small lever is set into the stone. Pull it?
As you cross the threshold of this richly decorated door you see several large daemons hovering around a strongly pulsating symbol drawn in the centre of a luxurious room.
The daemons look to the the largest of them, a savage looking daemon who is so bright with pulsating energy that it hurts to look at him. He nods and the daemons engage you.
As the last of the daemons implodes into raw energy the symbol on the floor ceases to glow. It slowly fades away into nothingness, leaving a burnt mark in the middle of the stone floor.
The daemon's essence is released from its earthly body in a blast of energy.

An enormous room lies beyond this door. The east side of the room is taken up by rows of beds which look like they have been dragged into this room. Still bodies lie chained to the beds. The room is alive with current.

The hair on your head starts to rise. A pulsating symbol drawn with care into the smooth marble tiles is surrounded by large winged daemons. They gather protectively around the symbol when they see you. Silently they move to intercept you.

The figures on the beds are alive but have the same vacant, glassy eyed look you are now used to. When you cut them loose they simply walk off around the room without purpose. Sadly, they are beyond your help.
Some of the daemons are gathered in this room watching the townsfolk wander through. They notice immediately that you do not fit in among the zombie-like townsfolk and attack.
Some polearms rest against this weapons rack.
Some glowing daemons are gathered in here. They cackle to each other in voices like static.
This weapons rack contains bows and quivers of arrows for the guardsmen. There are no guardsmen stationed here though.
A row of halberds line this weapons rack.
The shattered remains of a statue lie around you. The pieces seem charred by some great heat.
A procession of vacant eyed townsfolk stream past you. They take no notice of you.

You come across a grisly scene inside this large meeting hall. It looks like some townsfolk gathered behind furniture which had been piled into a large bulwark. Scorch marks on the furniture reveal that it caught on fire.
From the condition of the bodies you assume that the smoke from the fire suffocated them.  There is nothing in the building to reveal who or what started the fire however.

The frost giant savant regards you. 'The Riders lie defeated but their mounts continue to pose a serious threat. Perhaps seeking help from a dragon to defeat another is the answer. Seek the Winter Dragon over the ice floes.' He turns away.
A large inn named "The Seventh Rune" stands before you. Enter?

A villainous looking character lounges at this table. Several hired thugs sit nearby. He seems to be ignoring you, but you get the idea that he has estimated to the ounce the amount of coinage you possess.
The guardsmen glance at the ferry ticket and allow you to pass.
The dock is heavily guarded by Runic infantry. A guard crisply informs you that without the proper paper work you will not be able to use the ferry for troop transport.
The sinister looking character in the corner murmurs to you without taking his eyes off of the Runics in the far side of the bar 'what do you want, stranger?'

He seems satisfied and quietly says ' ... 'bout time someone made contact with me. Can't talk here. Meet at my house at the far north of town. Don't walk out with me.' He casually gets up, pays the innkeeper and strolls out of the inn.
You respond:
He looks at you strangely and returns to his cup of ale.
A young boy answers the door. He looks past you into the street. Quietly he swings the door open. Kynyaf appears behind him and ushers you inside. He bolts the door and brings you into his study.

'This is the first contact I have had with Karnak agents in months.  Tell me what's going on.' He says. You bring him up to date on the Karnak-Runic struggle. He muses it over. 'Yes, I can be of assistance.'

'I have been unable to scout the area because it is so heavily patrolled. However, I know that the bulk of the Dragonriders are currently up in the northern mountains finishing off some new Runic conquest.'

'Rumour has it that they will be returning here soon to direct their attention against us Karnaks. The Runic troops speak of them in awe. They perform a dual role: scouting from the air, making sneak attacks impossible; and heavy assault.'

'You'll have to attack them in the north before they return. Otherwise they will barrack in the midst of the Runic garrisons and will be able to mount up before being attacked.  Once airborne they are invincible.'

'Take this ferry ticket. It's a damn fine forgery. You will need it to cross the Tamar to get to the northern passes. Good luck. I won't be able to help you further. I am shutting down operations for a time.'
A tunnel leads back to the south. Head south?
You wander through the northern passes and return to the warm south.

A stone tower stands in this bleak winter landscape. The door to the tower is massive and not of Runic design. However, the Runic standard flies above it and some cold and miserable looking Runic guards stand on duty. They immediately attack.
A hungry pack of arctic wolves rushes from the deep forest cover and surprises you.

An enormous tower stands in the middle of this frozen valley. The scale of the features of the tower indicate that it was designed for massive individuals. Noone stands guard around the huge doorway. Enter?
In the entrance hallway stands a large scale but intricate ice sculpture depicting the region around the valley. A beautifully crafted dragon is shown looming over a lake to the west of the tower.
Down the hall a drunken Runic dressed in impressive looking armour is attempting to push a massive barrel. He sees you and snaps 'don't just stand around you ... help me with this.'
Help him?

The Runic actually looks stunned. He shakes his head and then menacingly stalks towards you (his slight stagger ruins the effect somewhat). Drawing himself up to his full height he says quietly 'I assume I heard you wrong, could you repeat yourself?'

The Runic is obviously torn between the pleasure of killing you and the hassle of pushing the massive barrel. Laziness overcomes belligerance and he relazes. 'Follow me with that barrel, scum, the other 'Riders are thirsty.'

Pushing the huge barrel you follow the Runic into a large chamber. Everything is giant scale in here. A massive chair has been smashed and now forms a bonfire. A squad of heavily armed men stand around it trying to warm themselves.

'Excellent, more rum', one cries as he sees the barrel rolling in. 'those giants make a passable batch.' The 'Riders smash a hole in the barrel and begin filling their tankards. None of them take any notice of you; servants are invisible to these types.
What is your plan of attack?
They couldn't care less. Not a one of them listens to you.
They take notice of that. Servants certainly do not speak in such a manner. The Runics mannerisms change and they behave as if they are seeing you for the first time.

Their surprise turns quickly to anticipation as generations of decadence has instilled in these men the inability to back down from a drinking contest, even when duty and common sense suggest otherwise.

Unfortunately, the 'Riders also possess an incredible tolerance for alcohol. After several hours of trying to get them drunker then yourselves you merely accomplish the opposite result. Inevitably a drunken brawl results with both sides worse for wear.
The Dragonriders lie at your feet. Half of the job is done. Now you need to dispatch their mounts.
The Dragonriders draw weapons and respond. They seem a bit unsteady but are still deadly.

You search the room. Unfortunately, the Dragonriders did not bring anything with them other than their weapons and equipment. Along the walls are hung several valuable works of art, all too massive to move.

This chest contains something of note. Among some superbly designed but giant sized arms and armour you discover a sword of exquisite workmanship. Although the weapon could be a short sword by giant standards, it makes a fine two handed blade.

A group of frost giants and wolves stand guard in this pass. A particularly large giant approaches you. Other frost giants watch the skies. The giant speaks in a deep rumble of a voice 'So you have come to try to finish us off.'

'At least you have the courage to fight us on the ground. Your friends who cast fire from the sky killed my wife ... killed my child.' The giant starts to shake with rage. The wolves growl, sensing his blood rage.
Your response?

The giant considers this. He confers with several of the other giants. Some grumble angrily at what he says but gradually relent. He returns to you: 'an enemy of those that took our homes is our friend.'

'If you mean harm to those that cast fire from the sky then you should speak to the Savant beside the lake. There is a cave to the north of here, follow it west to a lake where you should find the Savant's hut.' The giants let you pass.
One giant blows a horn as the wolves circle around you. They attack.
More giants and wolves approach from the north having heard the horn.

Frost giants flanked by wolves guard this narrow canyon. They have heard rumour of your defeat of the Dragonriders and talk excitedly about returning to their tower. One gestures for you to speak to someone to the north and west.
The Runic goes berzerk at this affront to his considerable dignity. 'You have found one', he says and attacks.

A frost giant savant sits alone in the rough hut. He gazes across the frozen lake to the north. He barely turns as you walk into his abode. 'I have been expecting you', he states simply and gazes once more across the ice.

'Beautiful, is it not?' he states pointing to the ice. Shapes appear and twirl as the perpetual northern twilight catchs the wind blasted snow. You sit and stare as recognizable objects flit in and out of snow clouds and ice gloom.

'The ice speaks if you but listen', the ancient giant says. You watch the ice as adventurers clearly recognizable as yourselves storm a great tower. In the mountains above the tower a huge white dragon circles blasting icy frost from its giant maw.

The images fade. The giants turns to you 'the ice has never misled me. This is a strong portent. The very land cries out against these invaders who bring fire and destruction. The dragon you saw lives in a cave further down the lake. Best seek him out.'

The Savant congratulates you on your defeat of the dragon riders, explaining that he saw the image of the battle in the ice. 'It was a good deed that you performed. Our race would have been no more if you had not stepped in. My thanks.'
Some giant sized abandoned structures stand here. They have been blasted from above.

You enter a frozen cave. Silver scales and great claw rents in the tundra clearly indicate that this is the lair of a dragon. You are not surprised when a great scaly head appears out of the blackness.

Nine beautiful ice carvings of emerald dragons encased in ice lie atop the lookout platform of the tower. Intricate runes are etched along their scales. The mounts of the dragon riders have been neutralised now as well.

The dragon regards you fiercely and then softens up. 'Hello little children, it has been a long time since your parents have allowed you to visit. Why aren't they with you? They didn't allow you to walk the ice by yourselves, did they?'
You speak with the Winter dragon.
'Thats nice children'. A great claw pats you on the head.

'Children, it is best not to joke about a dragon being enslaved. No true dragon would allow a human to ride upon its back.' You insist that it is true. 'Wait here and I will take a look'. The mighty dragon flies off.

... and returns several minutes later. 'I spotted several dragons sleeping atop your tower. They reeked of humans.' The dragons seethes with indignation. You explain that the dragons were used to drive the giants from their homes.

The dragon is infuriated by this. 'Children, wait here, I shall freeze these domesticated vermin in their sleep. Then you can return to riding sleighs down mountains and throwing snowballs.' The dragon flies off again for a longer time.

The dragon returns looking exhausted. 'The deed is done, children. Now run along and play ... and tell your parents to visit me more often. Its lonely now that my brood has grown up and flown away.' The dragon settles in for a deep sleep.
The winter dragon is fast asleep. Ice pellets stream from her nostrils as she snores.
What was once the lookout platform on top of the tower is now inhabited by nine large sleeping dragons. Strange runes are etched into their emerald coloured scales. Do you approach them?
You think that waking up a group of sleeping dragons is a good idea. Your approach wakes them up and they angrily attack you.

They have no treasure unfortunately. Not only is this not their lair but domesticated dragons do not possess the hoarding instinct. However, without their breeding stock the Dragonriders are effectively finished as a presence in these lands.
An ancient ice dragon lives in this cave. She is fast asleep and has covered in the entrance in impenetrable ice sheets.
The Savant nods at you and returns to gazing out across the frozen lake.
'And you found the sacred sword of Ymir', he seems troubled for a moment. 'You are going to return it to its rightful owners, aren't you?'
'Thank you', says the Savant. 'Let me give you this in return'. He hands you a potion and returns to gazing out across the ice.
The Savant watches you sadly as you make off with the sword. He then slowly walks out towards the ice and is gone.
The Savant makes no attempt to defend himself as he is cut down.
You have stumbled upon the lair of a clan of yeti. They are starving and rush upon you as a group.
Amid some coins and jewelry lies the skeleton of a human male. Some interesting items are near him.
A serpent suddenly rears its head from the ice and attacks, taking you by surprise.
The dragon's horde is quite small by dragon standards. Plunder is quite scarce up in the frozen north apparently.

A book concerning Runes catchs your attention. It would seem that the Runic empire once consisted of nomadic tribes that wandered the vast continent to the south. One of the tribes discovered seven sacred Runes and began to worship them as sacred idols.
'Welcome to my magic shop, would you like to see my inventory?'
'Welcome to my shop. I specialise in defensive equipment, would you like to see my inventory?'
'My name is Totle and I am professor of Jurisprudence here at the University. I require the assistance of some students to do some field research for me. Would you be so kind?' he says.

'Wonderful', he chirps, 'I am representing a captain of the light cavalry accused of murdering a convoy of wine merchants and plundering their wares. Apparently, he was caught leaving the scene of the crime by several members of the heavy cavalry.'

'The leader of the heavy cavalry who has given evidence against him is called Slaine. He, like all of the heavy horse, is one of the Rune blessed and so his evidence is given great weight by the courts. The plundered wine has never been found.'

'The accused, Palthus, is not Rune blessed and so further physical evidence is needed to prove his innocence. He is being held in the prefecture. Please speak to him and find what evidence you can to mount his defence.'
Totle is working at a desk overflowing with books and papers. 'No evidence yet? Keep trying' he says.
A prefect looks at you suspiciously. 'Can I help you, citizen?'
'Perhaps you should loiter somewhere else'.

You explain to the prefect that you are here to see Palthus on behalf of Professor Totle. The prefect seems satisfied and calls for the prisoner to be brought up. An unarmed but dangerous looking man is escorted to you. You explain your purpose.

He nods calmly and says 'theres not much you can do. It is Slaine's word against mine and my word is meaningless against his. There was always petty rivalry between the light and heavy horse, as is usual and even encouraged throughout the legions.'

'But the heavy horse started taking things too far. They are drawn from the ranks of the pure strain Runics while the light horse are drawn from the many nations and peoples that have been conquered by the Runic empire.'

'The heavy horse considered themselves naturally superior as a result. However, the increasing popularity of the light horse with the common people has been unbearable for them. I suspect that Slaine's hand is behind this, his pride knows no bounds.'

'I would search carefully near where I allegedly attacked the merchant convoy. Perhaps there is some evidence there that might shed light on Slaine's treachery.' He thanks you and the prefects return him to his cell.
The prefect says 'You don't have any business here. Please remove yourselves. You think I keep this big cudgel for smashing walnuts, do you?'
The prefecture of the city of New Caster stands before you. The central administration runs the city from this centre while the prefects police the streets. Would like to enter?
'Welcome to the Bank of Newcaster. Please feel free to use our banking services.'

A heavily armed Runic guard looks you over. 'You look like a capable group. The Bank has a problem. Its very sensitive and we would rather not call upon the Prefecture to solve it. They can be somewhat indelicate at times. Would you assist us?'
'Good', says the guard, 'a wealthy and influential trader named Hulain has defaulted on a loan owed to the Bank. He is using his personal connections to prevent us from foreclosing on his property.'

'The bank would make it worth your while if you spoke to this man and impressed upon him the need to repay his debts. The law does sanction the use of force but lets keep this between ourselves. The Bank is eager to keep this matter quiet.'

'The trader has a large house just inside the gates of the northern residential zone. Our agent will meet you there and take care of any 'cleaning up' operations. Pay is 1000 gold. Report back to me here. Again, not a word to anyone.'
The guard says 'please return when the deed is done.'
'Well done', says the guard, 'here is your reward and I would like to thank you on behalf of the Bank. I hope that merchant wasn't too much trouble.'
Empty.

A group of Runic roadbuilders stand here arguing in this temporary shelter. They are unable to agree on whether to curve the road around the moutain or attempt to dig a tunnel through it to maintain a straight line. You leave them to it.
A broken wagon lies abandoned near the west end of this bridge. It looks like someone tried to push it in the river and then gave up.
You move on.
You search the area carefully for clues regarding the plundered wagon but are unable to find anything.
The ground around the mouth of the river has been churned into mud by many hoof and foot prints.
There doesn't seem to be anything here of interest so you move on.
Searching carefully amid the prints you find a broken barrel stained with wine. Embedded in the barrel is a small piece of metal which you hold up to examine very carefully.
The Runic Heavy Horse is garrisoned here. An entire heavy brigade of five hundred well armed troops and their steeds live here. You think it would be best not to make trouble with them.
The crest of the Heavy Horse is proudly displayed above the gates. Three eagles in flight.
The crest of the Light Horse is proudly displayed above the gates. A rampant griffon.

An entire legion of Runic heavy infantry are garrisoned here: five thousand men. Squads of legionnaires practice their formations with unnerving precision. You have never seen troops move with such coordinated precision.

Runic squad leaders shout angrily to auxiliary infantry troops consisting of conscripted orcs. The orcs seem unable to grasp the precision required of them. Their formations are laughable. The Runic squad leaders are not amused however.

Beyond the fortress you see the entrance gates to the dread salt mines. Rather than risk engaging an entire legion of troops you move away, but not before noticing the Fifth Legion's standard emblazoned proudly above the gates of the fortress.
You move on.

You compare the crest of the Heavy Horse to the ripped piece of metal and there is a match. The ripped piece of metal is clearly from a shield employed by the Heavy Horse. Your investigation has not gone unnoticed however.

A troop of cavalry leaves the fortress and surrounds you. The captain narrows his eyes when he sees you are examining the crest carefully. 'Attack the intruders', he cries and the troop instinctively obeys.

You are not completely surprised to see that the captain's shield is missing a section which corresponds to the piece in your possession. It seems you have the needed evidence. Totle would be eager to share this news.
The Heavy Horse is garrisoned here. Feeling that you might be persona non grata with this arrogant troop you move along.

You show the piece of Slaine's shield to Totle and inform him of the battle with the Heavy Horse. He is very excited. 'I shall take this evidence to the Prefecture and secure the release of Palthus.  Meet me at the gates to the Prefecture.' He leaves.
free

Palthus and Totle stand here shaking hands. Both turn as you approach. Palthus thanks for all that you did. He hands you a quiver. 'Please take this and accept my gratitude, I picked it up on a campaign on the eastern frontier many years ago.'
Palthus takes his leave of you, obviously relieved to be in the open air again. 'I hope we meet again' are his departing words. Totle congratulates you and returns to his studies.

Runic guards stand attentively at this gatehouse. 'The gate is closed', one says as you approach, 'it seems some orcs have organised themselves into a viable force. These gates will not open until the area is pacified. Begone'
Runic guards watch you approach the gates. 'There's not much orc rebel activity these days for some reason. It's safe to pass.' They say.
The griffons have collected some shiny articles in their nests.

You have wandered into a fierce battle between two groups. The group to the west are large with wolflike features. The group to the east look distantly related to valley elves. Both groups are so caught up in their melee that they attack you as well.

A group of vicious looking humanoids with doglike features are gathered here around what looks like recent booty. They are arguing among themselves in their guttural language. When they see you they rush to the attack.

Some humanoids have set up camp in this cave. A group of them are arguing over some recent booty they have managed to get their claws on.  They turn at your approach and move to engage you, hoping to add you to their collection.

An ancient megalith stands here on this windy point. Strange script has been carved into it. The script is so weathered as to be illegible. However, the distinct image of a single rose can be made out.

The white rose of the Fir'bolgs starts to hum. Delicate petals are blown onto the sea. The thick sea mist begins to clear and an island appears. A wooden bridge of arcane design stretchs out towards the island.
You pass through the gates of this fairly large Runic city. Groups of people from many different parts of the farflung Runic empire crowd the streets. Noone pays you any particular attention.

The residential district stretchs out before you. Identical stone houses are built tightly together in typical Runic fashion throughout the empire. Some rude shacks lie to the east in what appears to be the less desirable end of town.
Dark Druid's tower.

At their head is a proud looking female who addresses you. 'Who are you to enter Fir'bolg land without permission?' she asks. 'To compensate my people I shall require you to perform a task for us. If you do not you shall be killed. Which shall it be?'
Perform task
Fight

'Good', she says. 'We fir'bolg once proudly ruled this entire region. Wave after wave of human invaders pushed us back into the mountains. Now our new home is threatened by a depraved group of evildoers who call themselves "The Seven."'

'They have managed to bully some local orcs into a ragtag army and we fear an invasion. We require you to eliminate the seven leaders. The orcs will disperse without leadership. They have precious little brains of their own.'

'The Seven hole up in abandoned fortress in the valley to the east. The northeast pass is manned by a sizeable body of orcs. We shall provide a force to engage them at the pass and draw out their troops. You enter the fortress and remove the Seven.'

'After you have prepared yourself for battle go to the northeast. You will be met by a troop of our stout archers who will assist you in storming their defences. Return to me when the Seven are no more and you will be well rewarded.' She withdraws.

You tell the Fir'bolg queen of your defeat of the Seven. She rewards with treasure and a single white rose. 'Take this white rose on your journeys. It acts as a key should you find another Fir'bolg settlement.' The queen says.
The Fir'bolg gather expectantly around you. When they hear that the Seven are still in operation they return to their tree tops.
The Fir'bolg queen gazes at you levelly. 'Very well, on your head be the consequences.' At her signal the archers let loose their shafts peppering you with arrows.

The Fir'bolg attack en masse. You notice that there are considerably less of them than you were led you to believe. Some crafty magic or trick must have given them the illusion of greater numbers. Still, there are enough ...
You ransack the Fir'bolg tree house and find some treasure. A odd white rose is housed in what you assume is the Fir'bolg queen's private chambers.
You thank the queen and take your leave of the Fir'bolg.
The Fir'bolg greet you politely but keep their distance.
Felled logs have been piled into a rough defensive bulwark. Orcs in dark armour stand on the other side, watching you.
Storm the bulwark?
The orcs gleefully pour forth to engulf you.
Grim looking Fir'bolg gather behind you. The orcs see the host before the bulwark and scramble over it, eager for battle. They were never much on defence, orcs. You are engulfed.
A squat ugly fortification is carved from one of the dark igneous mesas. A lurid skull grins from the centre of the evil building. Enter?
As you enter the dark forest you hear a eerie horn sound far off.

A strange glamour takes hold of you. You feel an irresistable urge to race wildly through the forest and set upon what beasts have the misfortune to cross your path. Eventually you come across a clearing.

A mighty hunter with a brace of antlers arising from his head stands above the carcasses of several recently killed deer. Other huntsman are gathered nearby. They begin to tear into the still warm flesh of the deer. Hot blood steams from their lips.

The Huntsman seems satisfied and blows the horn again. Powerless to resist you follow the hunters through the forest savagely attacking anything that crosses your path. After each kill you tear into the victims flesh with your teeth and hands.
You wake several hours later on the edge of the forest, covered in blood. The compulsion has lifted.
Teague's Helm of Silence enables you to resist the fey effects of the Huntsman's horn. You proceed into the forest.

The huntsmen have encircled a unicorn in this glade. The unicorn is lathered in sweat but defiantly swings its deadly horn about, keeping the huntsmen at bay. The huntsmen see you and savagely attack. The unicorn takes this opportunity to charge them.
The bodies of the huntsmen sink into the mossy forest floor until nothing is left of their destructive presence. The unicorn, heavily wounded but still alive meets your gaze levelly.

Its wanders over to a clump of moss on the spot where the horned huntsman lay. Digging its horn in the moss it flicks an object from the ground which falls at your feet. The unicorn then trots off into the thick forest.

A manuscript detailing the history of the smugglers guild reveals that the smugglers are former merchants who turned to their current profession when the Eastern passes were closed by the war with the Runics.
Leave the giant's tower?
Climb the stairs?
Some well made weapons and equipment rest against this rack. Unfortunately their size prohibits you from wearing or using them.
Several massive barrels of rum stand here. You can barely lift them.

'When pressed, the envoys admitted that with the demise of the Dragonriders their local leader was forced to listen to the merchant's calls for peace. The military were so demoralised that they put up little resistance.'
Several of Godolphin's trusted aides are set up in this manor. They greet you warmly but have nothing useful to say.
Some rough huts have been put together in the midst of these apple trees. They seem occupied. 'Who are you, what do you want in this accursed place?' a weak voice calls out. You explain yourself.

'All because of the arrogance of one wizard called Gwyddno. He brought some ancient cauldron here to further his studies. At first it was a boon to our healing magic. But in truth it brought our worst nightmares to life.' He says meaningfully.

'Rumour has it Gwyddno brought the thing back from one of his expeditions and began experimenting with its powers in the ancient forest on the west of the island. All I know is that the forest sickened and a hideous creature rose from the depths.'

'The creature spawned more like it and attacked the city, killing us as we slept. A group of us hid in what was the city gardens. These apple trees seem to deter the creatures for some reason. It seems only fitting as they were the symbol of the city.'

'Gwyddno had a tower along a high mountain trail to the west. But we daren't venture there. The creatures massacred us last time we tried to face them. If you can destroy these creatures please return here and save us.' The Fir'bolg returns to his hut.
'Know that you can rest here safely among the apple trees.' The Fir'bolg says.

Some hideous creatures have removed the top of this ancient stone tomb. It seems whatever lay inside became very unhappy with this desecration. Three undead warriors arise from the grave and attack the creatures.
You find an impressive spear in the tomb.

Several hideous creatures are digging into the soft earth of the swampy forest. You notice them pick up small green worms and gather them almost tenderly in their powerful claws. They turn at your approach, place the worms to the ground and attack.
The worms crawl back into the earth. You notice that tracks lead from the hole to the west. It looks as if some heavy object has been dragged from here.

You open the door and see a shocking sight. A massive creature that looks like it consists of lichen is huddled over a cauldron which is glowing with a sickly green light. It is feeding small worms into the cauldron, crooning to itself.
It sees you and barks an order to several of the hideous fellspawn that are gathered around it. The creatures rush to protect the massive beast.
The massive swamp beast and its remaining minions attack.
The swamp creatures putrefy into foul smelling slime.

You approach the cauldron. The green light slowly fades to nothingness. The cauldron is made of a heavy metal and appears to be of ancient design. It depicts the renowned healer Cerredwhen ministering to the wounded.
Leave the tower?
You enter a remarkably clean and orderly tavern. It looks recently built, with marble fittings and pillars covering the central dance floor. None of the patrons look in the mood for dancing however.
A sign reads 'Prefecture jail - no unauthorised visitors'.
A sign reads 'Bounty Hunter Division'.

You enter the main hall of the prefecture. The Praetor of the city stands before his official seat. He is engrossed in what appears to be a heated discussion between some military types and a group of merchants.

The Praetor stands here listening to a prefect. 'The prefects are more than adequate to find your son my lord, we don't require the assistance of some merchants to perform such a task.' A merchant retorts 'you weren't capable of guarding the boy.'

'You have shown your incompetence all too clearly.' The merchant continues. The prefect grits his teeth and responds 'this is a security matter and is of no concern of yours. Return to peddling your baubles and stop wasting the Praetor's time.'

The merchant retorts 'it is a trade matter when your attempts to enforce security closes all trade routes.' The Praetor speaks 'enough, this is getting us nowhere, my son has been taken from my own personal quarters', he glowers at the prefect.

'I want an immediate investigation, but not by the prefecture, as I suspect the kidnappers must have had inside help.' The prefect starts to object but is silenced by the Praetor. 'And not by any merchant's mercenaries either.'
'The investigators must be aligned to neither faction so that I may have full faith in them.' The merchant and the prefect seem unhappy with this idea. Do you wish to volunteer your services?

You explain that you are a band of adventurers seeking work. The Praetor seems satisfied with this if not completely trusting. He directs the prefect to escort you through his chambers to investigate the crime scene, but not to interfere with you.
The prefect points to the door on the eastern wall. 'That way to the scene of the crime.' The prefect says grudgingly all the time watching you like a hawk.
A locked door.
The Praetor's personal quarters. Comfortable but spartan. Searching the floor and the furniture you come up with nothing to explain the disappearance of the boy.
The bedroom of the Praetor's son. You search but cannot find any clues in here.
You step out onto the Praetor's personal balcony. You see the impressive city stretch out below you to the north. Four high towers are perched atop the four corners of the high city walls.

Some scratching in the smooth marble floor attracts your attention. A deep gouge has been made in the stone and another against the short wall surrounding the balcony. Leaning over the edge you see a piece of black metal wedged into an arrow slit.

You reach for and pull up the object. It is clearly a grappling hook. The prefect becomes excited 'see, clear evidence of Karnak spies ... wait here, I will summon the Praetor.' As he leaves you examine the grappling hook carefully.

It consists of dull black iron and has simple designs on it with which you are not familiar. The Praetor enters the balcony with the prefect. He examine the hook. 'Why are you convinced this is a Karnak device?' he asks the prefect.

The prefect responds 'who else would perform such a cowardly act my lord.' 'Thats not good enough', replies the Praetor. 'Search the city and uncover what you can about this device. The librarian might be a good place to start.' The Praetor suggests.

You ask the librarian to examine the grappling hook. 'Never seen the like' he responds. 'Definitely not Runic. Doesn't look Karnak either, they take great pride in their metalwork and this is clumsy. The kind of thing an orc would make.'
'Maybe you should go to the north part of town and ask the orcs?'. The librarian muses.
A rough looking orc blacksmith toils here. One glance at his product indicates his standards leave much to be desired.
Thinking better of buying any of his shoddy merchandise you move on.

You ask the orc about the grappling hook. The sight of the thing makes him nervous and he stammers he has never seen it before. You suggest to him that he might prefer to make a statement to the prefects. This seems to do the trick.

'Alright, I don't want those evil cutthroats asking me questions. We Orcs have been the scapegoats for every problem since they conquered us. Some orcs with a strange dialect came to me a few days back and bought the hook. Real nasty types.'

'I had never set eyes on them before. I didn't asked what they wanted it for. Why would I? If they're still here - they're probably holed up somewhere in this district - they would stand out anywhere else. Just keep my name out of this, I got a family.'
The orc returns to his toil and tries to ignore your presence.
This shack looks decrepid by even orc standards. Someone appears to be watching you from a window. Enter the shack?
Searching under the boxes reveals a trapdoor. Open it?
Climb the ladder?
Whoever is hiding out down here heard the trapdoor and prepared an ambush. Figures rush at you.

A faint voice cries out from the dark: 'Who's there?' You explain that you are searching for the Praetor's son. 'Thats me, thank the Runes, help me up.' The boy tries to rise to his feet. 'I've been there for days. What did I ever do to them?' he wails.
The boy introduces himself as Semius. He is too weak to walk and must be carried.
Searching the body of the head orc you find a crumpled note. It reads 'Take the Praetor's son and hold him until further instructions arrive. Fail and you will be nailed to a tree. Mojril.'
Leave the shack?

The Praetor sees his son and thanks you. 'You have my thanks, noble adventurers.' You tell him of the orcs and the note. 'This is news indeed. I know of this Mojril, I have placed a bounty on his head. Perhaps he took it personally?'
He takes his exhausted child from you. 'Let me reward you for your job well done.' The prefects look less than pleased. It seems you have made friends here as well as enemies.
The stairs are so wet and slippery that you tumble down them and fall into a water filled room. There is movement around you under the water. Something is surrounding you ...
The heavy doors of the castle open onto the sun baked sand.

The rock then bounces off a wall and continues travelling, landing on another stone. It then bounces and lands heavily in the water, making a splash. The sprites sigh dejectedly. Then turn and see you. Frightened, they dive into the pool and disappear.
The criminals' loot is kept in this chest.
Leave the manorhouse?
A locked door.
These chambers have been set aside for your use.
You can store what you like in this chest except items with magical charges.
Godolphin's private quarters.

A group of orcs are eating noisily at one end of the table. A densely muscled humanoid of unknown race sits with them, arguing with a heavily armed and armoured orc. Upon your intrusion, the orc turns to his companion and says:
Orc archers are stationed along this parapet ready to pick off any intruders.
Arrows hail down on you from a nearby guard tower.
A squad of orc guards holds the base of this tower.
Climb the ladder?
The barrels seem to be covering some stairs. It seems as though the orcs wanted to prevent any access to this area. Clear the barrels?
Sounds like a lot of commotion on the other side of this door. Do you wish to proceed?

A group of orcs are lounging around in here waiting for orders. They are occupying themselves in typical orcish fashion: sharpening blades, playing dice, arguing, sleeping etc. As you enter they draw weapons and advance.
Several orcs guard this room. It is clear even to their simplistic minds that you are not invited guests.
Raised voices and deep guttural growls indicate that a sizable number of humanoids are beyond this door. Enter?

Entering the room you see a faded throne room that must have been quite magnificent in days of yore. Its current occupants are a group of fierce dog faced humanoids squaring off against a group of tough looking humans. A robed wizard sits in the throne.

The wizard notices you at the door. 'Eliminate them Garanhir', he shouts, pointing at you. The two factions move as one to deal with you. Before you are engulfed you see the wizard disappear in a blinding flash.

You hear shouting behind you. More armed troops arrive to engage you. They are led by a monstrous lizard man, who rips at his own flesh in a blood frenzy crying out 'Guttur rend, Guttur cut, Guttur drink blood of fools.'
A locked heavy door.
The iron key found on the mighty warrior Garanhir unlocks this door.
The door won't budge.

You discover a net covering the floor. If you had stepped on it you would have been strung up from the ceiling. You spring it and several eager looking trolls barge into the room. They look incensed that their net trap failed. They take it out on you.

You fail to detect a net trap along the floor. You trigger it and the less agile among you are caught in it as it springs towards the ceiling. Eager trolls burst from the far door, delighted that their trap worked. They attack.

You enter the ruined castle and step into a courtyard. It is faded and crumbling but evidently still in use. Two squat guard towers stand before you to either side. You see movement along the parapets. Orc archers emerge, draw string and watch you.
You exit the castle.
As the Demon Lord's earthly body falls to the floor, his demonic minions wink out of existence.

A hideous little troll is laughing wickedly as two other trolls strap a struggling fir'bolg to a torture rack. Seeing you enter, the little troll takes out a vicious looking whip and walks towards you, flanked by the larger trolls.
The fir'bolg struggles free of the poorly tied ropes. 'A timely entrance, good friends. I fear my fate at the hands of the misshapen ones would have been less than pleasant. Gwydion is my name.'
He ferrets out a fine bow from the troll's bags. 'I'm an archer, as you might have surmised and I would be honoured to assist you in your noble venture.' May I join you?
An ornate chest stands here. Attempt to open it?
You notice there is something wrong with the floor the chest rests upon. You prod it and the empty chest disappears into a spiked pit. Well spotted.

You fail to notice that the floor upon which the chests sits is triggered to fall when you step upon it. You fall heavily into a spiked pit. The chest shatters and reveals nothing. To make matters worse the spikes are coated with hemlock.
A spiked pit opens beneath you. You float safely above the spiked pit. The chest shatters and unfortunately is empty.
Put a bunch of trolls in what were once pleasant quarters and this is the result. This room smells foul and is covered in grime and decay.

Two humans are arguing violently in this richly decorated but faded central hall. A large red demon stands patiently near them, a smug expression on its face. One of the humans, dressed in long brown wizard's robes notices you.

He waves his hands in an incantation and prepares to engage you. The room fills with winged demons who move toward you. The large demon automatically moves to protect the wizard. The other human, dressed in ornate robes, flees through to the south.

You open the door and see the man who fled on his knees. He appears to be beseeching a large grey skull which rests upon a pedestal. A thin voice hisses from the skull 'I know, you fool, they're right behind you. If you survive, return to Skullkeep.'
'Yes Gremyr,' he says reverently. He then leaps to his feet and snaps his fingers. Four powerful looking guards plod slowly towards you from the shadowy corners. The man grimly moves to attack you.
The skull has fallen silent.
Nothing seems to be open the peculiar lock on this sturdy chest.
The key found on the priest fits perfectly in this chest.
Several books on demonology sit on the shelves amid the rotting remains of ancient tomes. Touch them?
Weak light peeks through a thin aperture in the wall.
What do you want to do?
Assuming a vaporous form you slip through the tiny aperture and discover the wizard's treasure.
You hastily return to the wizard's chamber before your vaporous form dissipates.
In this dark room a large pentagram has been etched in salt along the floor. Other than a unsettling otherworldly smell, it is empty.
The crumbling statue of a wizard protector of the Tuatha de Danaan stands here. A plaque reads 'Amathaon'. The Danaan must have been the people who originally inhabited this forsaken place.
A crumbling statue of a female Tuatha de Danaan Ranger stands here. A plaque reads 'Lady Arianrhod'.  The Danaan must have been the people who originally inhabited this forsaken place.

A weathered barrow stands here along side this ancient lake. It has clearly not been tended in years. Once proud trees stand withered and bent and you have to clear brambles from the entrance. A sign reads 'Cruaich Meor'. Enter the barrow?
Leave the barrow?
A sturdy coffin lies before you. A strong aura of magic radiates from the large copper gilded object. Open it?
A dark room can be seen before you. In the centre of the room lies a copper casket. Enter?
As you enter the room a hideous beast leaps from the ceiling directly above you, bellowing a shriek. It surprises you.
Several shambling shapes step out of the gloom having heard the commotion of battle.
A skeleton crumbles to dust as you open the coffin lid. A silver scroll case which was clutched by a skeletal hand opens to reveal a sheet of paper. A strange musical instrument sits by his side.
Several shambling shapes step out of the gloom and attack.

As you near the twin pedestals you feel a warmth surround you. You faintly detect the unique odour of forest moss in addition to strange sounds like light footsteps on leaves all around you. A probing sensation starts to nag at your minds.

A faint voice speaks to you 'Your purpose I sense. Aid you shall have, younglings. Orc-cousins shall not witness our grand truth however.' The voice is replaced by the soft and mournful strumming of a harp in an unfamiliar style of music.
Something materialises in front of you on the pedestals. The strange sensation leaves you.

You enter a large meeting hall. It has been cleaned up and looks heavily used. Currently it stands empty. A name has been chiselled into seven of the eight chairs as follows: Kevardhu, Terksch, Guttur, Garanhir, Mojril, Nguthgz and Darvik.
The eighth chair has only an 'S' carved into it.
The strange faery that live at the bottom of this well are infuriated that you would enter their lair. They swarm around you, hissing.
A group of the fey creatures leap at you from above.
A pile of shiny objects are located here. The Korrigan must gather around and gaze upon them adoringly.
A large metal object seems to have slipped into the deep murky water. You only noticed it because of a peculiar glow surrounding the object.
Enhanced by waterworld enchantments you are able to swim down and collect the item. Its a mighty blade!
If you dangle a rope down the well you could probably descend safely. Do so?

The Gnolls obviously tried to expand their cave structure until they came across a vein of some metallic mineral and stopped. They now use the hole as a refuse pit. A piece of the mineral ore lies in front of you. Pick it up?
The prospector eyes the chunk of tin you found in the Gnoll's cave. 'Tin ... Where did you find that?' he asks excitedly.
You reply

'Wait 'til I tell the lads', he chuckles as he rushes off. He gets to the door and quickly stops. 'Oh, in return I shall appoint you honourary members of the Guild.' He hurriedly makes some grand gestures in the air.

'There', he says and pulls out some things from a shelf and puts them on a table before you. He then darts off. On the table in front of you is a large mining tool and a ridiculous metal cap with a candle attached to its top.
A depressed looking prospector stands here.

'No more tin.' He says shaking his head. 'No more tin. I am sure as Arn not ever going back to that one down south.' Any attempt to change the topic of conversation with this individual away from the fact that there is 'no more tin' fails totally.
A message has been carved into beaten bronze here. 'The Acolytes Path: The true disciple will know which is the correct path. Step through.'
A horde of treasure lies before you. Gather it up?

The shrill voice rings in your head. 'Monetary wealth and physical possessions distract you from your tasks. They provide meaningless entanglement. They are naught compared to the glory of the Grey God.' You are thrown backwards.
A small tree stands here. Silvery acorns adorn its branches. Take one?
The shrill voice rings in your head. 'The natural world brings only disease and chaos. It must be cleansed and purified.' You feel ill.
You look into the mirror and see a reflection of the dark room behind you. You are nowhere to be seen. Step through?
A shrill voice rings in your mind 'Yes, for truly we are nothing ... before walking the dark paths of the Grey God.'
You look into the mirror and see absolute nothingness. Step through?

A shrill voice rings in your mind 'Do not presume that you understand the perfection of oblivion, foolish acolyte. Your presumption does not come without cost.' Lightning springs from the mirror to strike at you.
A shrill voice rings in your mind 'Yes, the agony of the flame builds strength, cleansing the weakness of our corporeal selves.'
A shrill voice rings in your mind 'Water, the life-giver, is a poison that weakens the pure of form.'
Burning ...
A shrill voice rings in your mind 'Those that seek to choose the easiest path deserve nothing but my comtempt.'
You look into the mirror and see a reflection of yourselves. Step through?

A shrill voice rings in your mind 'No, acolyte. You enter the service of the Grey God as nothing; as no one. Your past is erased. Sever all ties to those not sworn to Oblivion, for their lot is chaos.'
You wade through the icy cool yet soothing water.
You step onto the curiously smooth stone. Two large but closed eyes float in place in front of you.
The eyes spring open. Feral orbs regard you carefully.
After several seconds, an expression of contempt fills the eyes. Nothing seems to happen, but the eyes watch your every move.
The eyes seem to focus on the Pendant of the Grey God in your possession. A great door materialises in the far wall, as if an illusion has been lifted. The eyes continue to watch you.

Opening the door reveals a dusty room beyond. Large windows reveal a breathtaking view of the surrounding mountains. Unlike the rest of the castle this room has been left untouched by its present inhabitants for some reason.
This ancient loom is beautifully crafted and covered in mystical Sidhe script. You fiddle with the ancient loom and try to make it operational. However as you have no thread there isn't much point.
Whatever magic was holding the animated tree together dissipates and the trunk explodes in a shower of jagged wooden thorns.
Shadowgaunt castle
A large group of guards is garrisoned in this entrance hallway. Upon seeing you they draw steel and advance.
The portcullis at the far end of the room slams down, closing off that corridor.
The door opens to reveal a neglected looking corridor ending in a simple door. Thin apertures line the walls.
As you step into the corridor the door behind you springs shut with a loud bang.
Archers appear at the apertures and start peppering you with arrows. The tiny size of the apertures makes counter attacking impossible.
The archers await you in the next room. The design of this corridor gives them a tactical advantage. They are free to move while you are bunched into the tight corridor, causing entanglement.
A collection of soldiers and robed priests are gathered in here waiting to dispatch you. As you open the door they attack.
There appears to be a lot of noise coming from this room. There is clearly a great number of people on the other side of this door. Enter?
The chest is empty.

Against the far wall of this room stand three crude statues. They seem pitted and scored as if having been struck by projectives. Broken arrows litter the floor. This seems to be a rudimentary archery range.
Against the far wall of this room stand three crude statues. They seem warped, charred and chipped as if having been struck by magical forces. This seems to be a practice area for wielders of magic.
A lever is set into the far wall here. There is nothing accompanying the lever to explain its purpose. Pull it?
The floor beneath you gives way and you land heavily in a spiked pit.

Beyond the door lies a huge auditorium filled with dozens of seats facing a raised dias. A figure on the far dias is lecturing to a multitude of robed individuals who seem totally focused upon him. You take this opportunity to listen to his speech.

After several minutes of droning on about the power and splendour of the Grey God the lecturer catches your attention '... and those that are deemed worthy shall journey to his tower and stand before his baleful gaze.
The skull idol is completely nonfunctional.
A sheet of writing has been left under several books on the desk. The books contain unintelligle diagrams and appear to be describing something called 'Astronomy'. You read the paper.
You put the piece of paper back under the books.

One book catches your eye: a worn piece of propaganda entitled 'Why the Laerg will conquer the world.' Briefly it states that the Laerg have such a high rate of population growth, being reptilian, that they will soon overwhelm all other races.
This large room is a dining area. Large wooden tables and chairs fill the room. Armed guards and several robed figures fill the chairs. They notice you and prepare for battle.
The melee has drawn several squads of guards to the area.

'And lo He shall smite those who are weak and those are unsure of their loyalty. Those that are deemed worthy shall journey through His tests towards His sacred instrument: the Altar of Skulls. There they shall be granted eternal life in His service.'

Four unusual statutes line the walls of this small room. The statues depict exotic looking warhounds. As you move forward the eyes of the statues seem to train upon you. The statutes begin to blur and in their place stands four suddenly alive warhounds.
The hounds allowed the defenders of this area time to prepare themselves for your arrival. A line of heavily armoured guards multi-tiered room. As you open the door they move toward you.
You enter a shadowy hall of pillars.
Digging into the earth you find a large flat stone. Lifting it reveals an old ladder leading down. It's dark but the ladder seems to be made of bone. Climb the ladder?
Someone was watching the battle from through the door in the northeast corner. They slam the door shut.
A strange contraption stands here. A barrel is tied by stout ropes to a platform in the sunken sand. This whole sandy platform is saturated with foul smelling water.

Inside the chest you find a small diary written in a rough script. You read it and determine that it belongs to Garanhir, the leader of a group of Nordman mercenaries. He writes long tedious passages about how he misses the northern ice floes etc.

A horrific sight greets you as you approach what at first looks like a forest. Rows of warped trees exude a smell of corruption from the grisly fruit that hangs from their boughs. Dozens of men lie hanged from their necks, their feet swaying listlessly.
Sunlight peaks through the end of this tight squeeze. Enter?
You claw your way through overgrown brambles to emerge on the surface.
A plaque reads 'Prepare yourself for the Hall of Shadows.'
Any attempt to enter the forest is blocked by the trees which seem to move to cover every likely looking path. Eventually you give in and back away from this nightmarish corruption of nature.

A text describes the details of a Shadow magic spell entitled 'Summon Shade'. It involves boiling down the fat of human beings to form the tallow for a candle. The shadows that are formed from this lit candle can be controlled by the Shadow Mage.
Three large braziers stand along this wall. They are thick with dried wax. The wax, although decades old, continues to exude an unpleasant odour.

A book on Blood Magic discusses the possibility of animating various mundane objects and filling them with a basic sentience... perhaps enough to enable them to be effective guards who animate upon a specific trigger.
As you sort through the treasure you hear the scraping of stone against stone behind you. The red statuettes have automated with the opening of the chest and now move toward you with deadly purpose.

An ordinary looking grey stone sits on an altar in this dank room. The aura of pure evil it radiates is far from ordinary however. Ideas begin to trickle into your head. Why not use your power to overthrow the Karnak leaders and enslave the population?

An interesting tome entitled 'The Malylakron' catchs your eye. It is so ancient and faded that it is barely legible. It discusses the legend of a stone that reputedly has the ability to compel those of an evil persuasion to be drawn towards it.

Three small crimson statues surround you. As you enter this area they start to hum. Stubby arms begin to emerge from the statues and vacant eyes appear on the smooth surface. The monstrosities lumber toward you.

Better yet ... why not kill the entire population to prevent them from stealing your possessions. You remember their covetous glances ... their jealousy as you solved problems they were too weak to handle themselves.
Gradually your willpower overcomes the malevolence of the stone and you smash it to pieces to escape its intense pull. The Malylakron lies in pieces on the floor. You feel much more benign suddenly.
Careful searching reveals that one of these books is fake. Tilting the book forward reveals a secret door.
The rancid odour of dried herbs and other reagents indicates that this must be a laboratory of sorts.
A heavily thumbed folio on the subject of contact and digestible poisons lies on this bookshelf. The author's approach to poisoning techniques is highly avant garde.
Several potions, unguents and stoppered vials lie haphazardly across this table. You are not sure which potions have been brewed successfully and which are an early death waiting to be imbibed.
The chest contains several rare reagents used in the prepation of potions. Some gems to be powdered and various other valuable sorcerous equipment.

As you approach the chest the two crimson statues flanking the door begin to hum. Stubby arms begin to emerge from the statues and vacant eyes appear on the smooth surface. The monstrosities lumber toward you.
You help yourself to the possession's of the occupant of this room.
Some interesting pieces of jewelry are kept locked away here.
The High Prelate's possessions lie in this chest.

A large number of individuals are feasting in this hall. Some are armoured, others are clad in robes. All turn at your intrusion and spring to the attack. They are led by one who has the look of the irretrievably damned.
That most unholy of abominations stands before you: the Altar of Skulls. It stands in the centre of a strange formation of scarlet statues.
Sadly, lacking the proper items there is nothing that you can do here.
Do you wish to attempt to raise the spirit of Ossian at this time?
By placing Ossian's torc inside of the Cauldron you attempt to resurrect the long dead Bard. The torc fades to nothingness as a ghostly apparition forms in front of you.

The spirit of Ossian watchs you impatiently. Unfortunately, as you do not possess the Lay, he waits in vain. Perhaps if you possessed the Lay you could request him to counteract his songspell as Rowan advised. Sadly, you wasted this opportunity.

The spirit of Ossian seems to detect your purpose and wordlessly reachs for the songspell. His image appears to be singing yet no sound emerges. You begin to feel the tell-tale pulse of powerful magic around you.

Unfortunately, the magic appears to have triggered some sort of defensive mechanism. The statues begin to transform into creatures you have not encountered before. They move toward the altar perhaps to silence Ossian who has not finished his songspell.

As the battle dies down, you notice that Ossian appears to have stopped singing. A low rumbling sound far off shakes the underground shrine. Rocks begin falling from the ceiling. Before you are crushed to death, Ossian gestures and you are teleported.
You are on back on the surface.

The stone of the tower transforms into a sickly and feral eye that gazes upon you. Rage fills the eye and you are thrown backwards by an unseen force, slamming against the rough stone of the tight canyon.
The force acting upon continues and you are thrown bodily out of the canyon. Rocks topple from the walls of the canyon and you realize the canyon is now hopelessly blocked by debris.
You pass the strange tower safely.
Leave the tower?

A man stands in the centre of this ivy carpeted room. He introduces himself as Rowan the Druid. He says: 'I am glad that you are here. It is an honour to meet adventurers such as yourselves. In my youth I too wandered the land seeking adventure.'

'The land is in need of adventurers. Sadly, the common folk of this region are blind to the coming darkness. Instead they waste their resources on fighting among themselves. Perhaps that is exactly what the darkness desires.'

'In any event, there is much I must tell you. But first the wasteful war that wages between the Karnaks and the Runics must be ended, one way or another.' Soil from his recent gardening endeavours falls from his hands as he gestures.

'My counsel of peace has been rejected by my bloodthirsty kin. Should you meet with success in ending this war, return with haste to me and I shall enlighten you with news of the true darkness that threatens to engulf this land.'
Rowan the Druid looks at you. 'Sadly, with the present climate of confusion because of this war I am unable to proceed with my plans. Please return when the war has ended.'
A stone guardian stands motionless before this door. At your approach he animates and performs his sole function: defending the door.
Rowan engages you in conversation regarding the above topics.
Something stirs on the peripherary of your vision ... but then fades when you look more carefully.
Rowan waits expectantly.
You light the lamp of human fat and place it atop the central brazier. It flares up and a revolting smell fills the dark room. Odd shadows dance among the pillars as the lamp burns.
You don't have the lamp of human fat and cannot continue.

The shadows begin to move purposefully toward the lit candle, encircling it and yourself. The shadows wait expectantly for some command. Unfortunately, untrained as you are in the necromantic arts you are unable to control them.
The light from the brazier reveals a hidden passageway.
A map has been left here. It details a secret route used by the smugglers to access the Runic City.

The smuggler's guildmaster is pleased to see you. 'We heard about the end of the war. I don't know how but I suspect you were involved. You have my thanks. We have already made contact with the Runic merchants and trade will resume.'

You read a story about the great hero, Teague. It seems that Teague was to fight against a horde of vicious humanoids called the Camaar. The Camaar used to march into battle playing fey battle music which would cause those listening to flee.

Teague had some Fomorians fashion him a helm which could block out all sound. Equipped with this device Teague managed to successfully defeat the Camaar horde. He then crossed over the southern mountains and was never heard of again. Not much of a story.
Upon the death of the villainous Druid, his novices redouble their attack.

As you open the door you see the distinctive red robe of the wizard near a fire place. He is burning documents. He sees you and rushes to the back of the room and out of sight. A female voice cries out to him to hurry up.
The two seem to have vanished. Then you see the open trap door behind the barrels.
You douse the flame and quickly snatch the smouldering paper from the fire before it roars up again. There is one simple word written upon the paper. It says 'Fenris'.
Two elegant saddles are kept locked away in this chest. Each bears the name of a horse: 'Dexter' and 'Sinister'.
A strange and oppressively low ceilinged room stands before you. Walls of shimmering stand between you and the far side.  A mouth appears in the skull to your right. It speaks: 'what is the pattern?'
The skull speaks again: 'there is no pattern of course. For such is chaos. All symbols are mine. All loyalties, all races, all factions belong to me in the end'.

You come to a dank room with a very low and somewhat convex ceiling. You can almost sense the weight of the earth poised to collapse through the stone above you. Amid the darkness you can make out the shattered remains of now recognizable statuettes.

A corpse hangs from a makeshift gallows in this wreched room. Noone deserves such a lonely death ... to swing listlessly so far from the surface, unable to fly toward's Arn's light. You move toward the corpse. It speaks...

'Stay thy hand ... I live yet ... in a sense. My body may lie here, but my soul hath been taken from me and placed in a suit of living armour. I came here to destroy the abomination known as the Grey One but instead my soul has become a weapon...'
A murky corridor stretchs out before you. Six lifeless figures line the corridor three abreast. At your approach they spring to life and attack.
Two closed eyes hang in space above what looks like an offering bowl made of some dark stone.

'A weapon in the employ of the Grey One's unholiest of disciples: Clur'can. Know that you must destroy the unholy creation hidden behind the far wall. It will fight with the decades of cunning and battle skills that once I could call my own.'

'Slay it and let me know peace once more. Make sure all of it's brethren are dispatched. For only then can you safely call upon Clur'can. Be wary of him, the Grey One has granted him great power over the dead ... some say he himself is dead ...'
Enter the base of the tower?

In the shadows a mighty suit of armour stands to attention. Despite its vast size, the monstrous being steps lithely holding a mighty axe in both arms. Other smaller shapes materialise out of the shadows to engage you.
The figure hanging from the gallows barely raises his eyes to you. He nods silently, a look of resolution on his face. The body is broken but the fight lives on.
The figure hangs limply now. Perhaps in peace.  Perhaps in another place of torment. It is not for you to know.
The eyes crack open, revealing the feral yellow slits you have experienced in the past. The eyes regard you and then close.
The feral eyes glare smugly at you and close. You hear the sound of stone moving.
