A rock thrusts through the lava to form a step.
The use of cold based magic in a room full of lava results a scalding cloud of steam.
The room has been de-magicked against exactly that spell.
An odd lever is set into the wall here. Pull it?
Something happened ... but what?

This mystical loom is clearly not of Runic design. It is carved in Sidhe script. It must have been transported here at great expense. The transportation must have taken its toll as the loom is now devoid of magic. You find some interesting thread though.

The pyromantic couple has sealed themselves in what could be their secret channeling room. Two large braziers fill the small unventilated room with acrid smoke and incredible heat - causing eyes to water and throats to dry up.

As you stumble through the haze of heat you see the pyromancers complete their summoning spell. A massive red dragon pops into existence near them. It is enraged by being contained under the ground and becomes berserk, breaking the summoning link.

You scan the room for the occupants of the statues but they are nowhere in sight. Suddenly, you make out shapes through the gloom to your right and left. They were hiding in alcoves on either side of the door. The Angreden gain the initiative.
A simple lever is set into the floor. Pull it?
A portcullis falls from the ceiling trapping you in this confined space.
Only brute strength will shift this massive contraption.  Who will try?
Success! With Herculean effort, the portcullis is slowly and painfully thrust back into its perch.
Your efforts were in vain.
Your dwarven party member suddenly calls for the party to stop, explaining that they have detected a significant slope in the stone hallway ahead.
An old dwarven trick has been stolen here, that of creating an optical illusion whereby the hall looks flat but in fact is a steep slope. Do you venture out onto the smooth steps?

The smooth stones ahead look flat but are in fact part of an old dwarven optical illusion.  Unfortunately, you don't have a dwarf with you to warn you about this... The party tumbles down a steep slope into a dank room.
The prisoners locked up behind these bars call out to you: 'Let us out!'. Let them out?
They repay you by attacking. They might have been locked up for some transgression, but they know where their loyalties lie.

Some unfortunate villagers are locked in here. They are being held for some unknown purpose. When asked they are unable to share any useful information with you. They gratefully take their leave of this place.
You hear a noise. There appears to be something in the barrel. Open it?

To your surprise you find an unconscious woman in the barrel, trussed up hand and foot. You revive her and she introduces herself as Vesta, Warrior-Captain of Porthenys. 'Thank you for this timely rescue. I feel a bit foolish having been captured.'

A Runic prefect approachs you. 'You must be the squad hired for the foreclosure operation ... you don't exactly blend in here, do you?' He looks pretty shifty for a prefect, and he doesn't quite fit his uniform. 'Are you ready to proceed?'

'Good. The guards will let us in without much fuss. Noone dares question the prefects in these parts. We can then have a quiet word with Hulain. I am sure he will be compliant. These merchants rarely show any back bone when confronted directly.'
The 'prefect' who you assume must be an agent for the Bank approaches the gates. As predicted, the guards quickly open the gates and you enter the lavish villa.

The bank's agent proceeds to march up to the front door. He is carrying a large manuscript of papers which he brandishes like a weapon. The door opens and an imposing man dressed in crimson swirling robes stands before the agent.
He doesn't look particularly like a merchant... more like a ...
... those sorcerers who specialise in fire magic...
Pyromancer ... that's it. The merchant glares at you and rushs into his villa, slamming the door.

It seems the Bank's agent has become a heap of ashes along with his writ of foreclosure. A voice from the villa calls out 'guards, remove these vermin.' Armed guards stream out from the gatehouses and engage you.
An imposing private villa stands here. Someone seems to have had some sort of disagreement with the guards however. Enter?
Leave the villa?
This low wooden building must be the stables. It has that characteristic pungent odour.
Several impressive looking horses live in these stalls.
Watch your step.
A small grazing space for the horses has been set up inside the walls of the villa. A tool shed occupies the far corner.

A faded piece of paper with the seal of the Bank of New Caster lies here. The document appears to have been part of an earlier attempt at foreclosure. By the looks of the charred skeleton adjacent it looks as though the foreclosure did not go well.
A huge pile of ash lies at the bottom of this pit.
Most cellars are cold and damp but this cellar seems unnaturally warm and dry.
Some rare vintages are kept tucked away back here. Take them?
A large squad of the merchant's guards have gathered in here to pounce upon you.
A bunch of off-duty guards are dozing in here. Wake them?
More guards have gathered on this landing to finish you off.
A stout wooden chest stands here. Open it?

Just before opening it, you detect a trap and step back. Your sudden motion causes the trap to trigger. The false floor around the chest gives way causing the chest to plummet down into a pit of flame. Close.
You fail to detect the false floor upon which the chest sits. Opening the chest triggers the floor to fall into a pit of flame. Those that fail to leap out of the way are burned.
You float above what would have been a very nasty trap. The false floor beneath the chest gives way and the chest plummets into a fiery pit. The chest is incinerated.
A magnificent dining room table dominates this long room. An impressive collection of silverware is laid atop the table. The room is otherwise empty. Do you wish to to grab the silverware?
You leave the small cave.
Enter the cave?

An odd island breaks up the river here. What looks like a burial cairn lies in the middle of the island. As you attempt to approach the cairn, an irresistable compulsion to leave the island forces you back.
Godolphin greets you 'I am sorry that Penhaligon is not with you. However, the war must go on. You must have the greatness of legends to have survived my son's odd plan to break into a prison.'

Godolphin continues, 'In any event my advisors and myself have agreed that the time is ripe for a large push against the Runic positions through the eastern passes. Your prison break will be causing them to waste resources searching for you.'
'We will discuss it in greater detail later. Why don't you get some much needed rest?' Godolphin returns his attention to some maps of the passes.
Owww....

Luckily you are intelligent to realize that this underground river is your only possible exit from these deep caves. You will need to create some kind of flotation device to float yourself to the surface.
The stone of the tower transforms into a sickly and feral eye that gazes upon you. The eye contorts with rage and you are thrown backsward by an unseen force.
You hear the awful screeching of the serpents as they search blindly for prey. Keep paddling?
A quaint cottage is set in this idyllic forest grove. Melodious notes ring from the skillful strumming of a master musician's harp. You feel at peace.

'Cerredwhen was a master healer in days of yore. He would travel the lands for no purpose other than to bring relief to the suffering and cure the afflicted. His deeds were so great in fact that the goddess Arn, bathed in moonlight gave him a gift.'

'She bestowed upon him the Cauldron which is said to have great healing properties. The Cauldron is rumoured to have the power to raise the dead. Cerredwhen was known to have raised several worthy individuals who died before their alloted time was up.'

'Ossian, whose torc you possess, is one such worthy person. I can feel the purity of his life essence humming in that torc. I propose to raise Ossian with the Cauldron to aid us. His body is long lost to this world and only the Cauldron can raise him.'

'Ossian's songspell ended the war against the Shadowgaunt but is now working against us. Mighty watch towers were built by the Sidhe to warn of the rising of the Grey God. However, He corrupted the magic of these towers and now hides behind them.'

'We are powerless to stop the tide of corruption He has unleashed. Only Ossian has the power to reverse his own songspell. This is a bardic matter so we need the counsel of bards. Seek out Llywarch who lives to the south, he will know more.'

As you near the cottage you see a bard of obvious talent playing a harp. Listening in rapture to him is a woman of almost unearthly beauty. At your approach she turns and casts a withering glance at your rude intrusion.
'How dare you intrude upon our privacy!' she exclaims. Embarrassed, you feel compelled to leave. You note however, that the bard didn't even seem to notice your presence much less stop his playing.
Your musician character informs you that there was definitely something amiss concerning the bard and how he played, but are unable to explain why.

'Llywarch', you cry out. At the mention of his name the bard abrupty stops his frantic strumming. He looks dazed and exhausted and crumples to the ground. The beautiful woman is overcome with fury and casts baleful yellow eyes upon you.
'A curse upon you - you have no idea what powers you interfere with. I shall come to you in your dreams. You shall know true misery before your short lives end in darkness and pain.'

Llywarch stirs. 'At last she is gone. And I am free. He looks at his worn hands;  bleeding from his enforced playing. I did not know she was a Quickling, they told stories about them in the College of Bards when I was a lad. But I thought them myth.'

You inform Llywarch of Rowan's intentions regarding Ossian. At the mention of Ossian he looks shocked 'She came to me after I composed a ballad for Ossian. I shall never play that tune again. But let me tell you about Ossian, for I have learnt much.'

'Ossian lived in the wooded valleys of the Tuatha de Danaan far to the north. I visited the ruined castle that they abandoned decades ago to further my research but found nothing. However, I have tracked his final resting place.'

'After the great battle with the Nameless One, the weary Danaan gathered their dead and retreated from the world. They built a great tomb in a secluded valley and set one of their watch towers to guard it. '

'Rumour has it that the great songspell that Ossian used against the Nameless One was placed in his tomb. I tried to enter the tomb but the watch tower sensed my presence and hurled from my feet. I was almost killed by falling rocks as I fled.'

'If what Rowan says is true, you must retrieve this songspell for Ossian to reverse his magic. We must hurry to this watch tower. I feel that my destiny will be fulfilled there.' Allow Llywarch to join your party?
Then let us proceed with haste. The tower of which I speak lies not far to the northeast of Rowan's wood.

'An offer of friendship coldly rejected is unbecoming of such fine adventurers. Consider yourselves very lucky that you will be given a further chance to walk the true path', Llywarch says mystically and enters his small cottage.
Llywarch regards the blocked canyon. 'An impressive illusion isn't it.' He says, 'but we bards are the masters of illusion.' He plays a few notes on his harp and the stones melt away.
Llywarch urges you forward toward the tower. His eyes seem to gleam with some wild fervour.
Llywarch cautions you to stand back. He strides toward the tower calling out 'tell the young bards of my deed ... I want my tales to be included in the stories sung by campfires.'

Llywarch walks with purpose up to the tower. The yellow eye erupts like an open sore across the smooth stone of the crumbling tower. It blasts him with its power. Llywarch lets out a single note of pure unadulterated sound from his tortured lungs.
Llywarch crumples up like dried parchment and falls to the ground. The eye of the tower stares fixedly at the spot where he lay ... Its power extinguished.
'Yes, it is vital to our plans. Llywarch the bard should know more. I am but a druid, who am I to guide our hand when it comes to bardic matters?'

You relate the tale of Llywarch and the Watch Tower. 'It was his gaes to fall in that matter.' Rowan says sagely. 'He had known his fate for years but he would not hesitate nor choose a different path. Let not his sacrifice be in vain.'

'A young druid has reported to me that he has had contact with the fabled centaurs. They ride the plains far to the east. Within their lands, which they will not allow any strangers to pass, is said to be a shrine to the Grey God.'

'It is located in the broken and blighted city of Yr Coreag, where once the Bone Shavers built their accursed monuments to the Grey God. It is at that shrine, where the Grey God first walked the earth, where Ossian must recant his songspell.'

'When the time is right, remember to use the Cauldron to raise Ossian from his life essence which resides in his Torc. His spirit is so lost he will only have moments to complete his spell before he returns to his eternal sleep.'

'Ossian's song spell should reverse the time freeze on the Shadowgaunt's lands and cripple the corrupted Danaan watch towers. Then we move against what remains of the Grey God's forces and finish this for good.'
'Yes, seek the Cauldron. I sent a young druid to speak to the Fir'bolg. But he has not returned. I hope he has not been lost to us.'
'Ossian's Torc must be found. As he was a great hero amongst his people, the Tuatha de Danaan, perhaps his torc will be found in their lands to the north.'

'Sadly even druids are not above treading the dark path. The Gallowgaes was a vile magical practice long since forgotten by righteous druids. It is forbidden knowledge and I feel uncomfortable even speaking of it. I apologize for bringing it up.'

'So that vile practice once again blights the land. It must be the work of Baille, who was cast out from the circle of druids years ago for his experiments against nature. One so cruel as he would inevitably seek out the Grey God and serve him.'

'Find the Ents who live in the forests of Boscawen. They are wary of people but will speak with you if you sit and wait patiently in the grove of Alder trees in the middle of the forest. They will know what steps to take to counter Baille.'
'There must be a purpose for the gallowgaes. Baille must be protecting something from those who would oppose the Grey God. For that reason we must find out what it is he hides.'
You come to a peaceful grove of alder trees.  You can't help but feel watched. Searching the area reveals no source for this odd feeling however.

You patiently wait in the grove as Rowan instructed you. Over the course of many hours you discern the gradual movement of the alders around you. Slowly a circle of trees forms around you. Suddenly one of the alders begins to speak in a deep monotone.
'Long it has been since a youngling has come to speak with us ... And longer still that any understood the need for patience ...' He muses quietly for several moments. 'Why have you come to us?'
You explain about the gallowgaes. The alders rustle with agitation.

'Short lived as you are, you will never fully comprehend the tragedy you have brought word of. An entire forest which grew over the course of centuries has died in the making of this evil magic. Their souls are enslaved and their trunks animated.'

'This Baille creature has planted the seed and he shall know the full fury of ents 'ere his roots ever take hold.' The alder trees begin to pull their roots from the earth and lumber ungainly about. Their size is awe inspiring. So is their wrath...
'Proceed with haste to the gallowgaes, younglings, and we shall reduce this Baille to a mossy stump.' The furious Ents march off toward the blighted forest.

As you approach the odd forest an Alder rumbles 'So this is all that remains of Llengelly forest. There shall be a reckoning...' With that the ents begin furiously smashing at the dead trees. They roar war cries which not been heard in centuries.
But the animated trees are not defenceless. They pull out their twisted roots and soon you find yourselves drawn deep into the sickly forest - engulfed in a battle of living trees.

You are surrounded by shattered wood and fallen branches. In the distance you see a tower which grotesquely mirrors Rowan's own. From the tower pours forth a number of hooded figures who summon more animated trees from the forest.

An Alder points to the tower and rumbles 'seek the base of the tower, they will have dug paths under the earth to corrupt the very roots of the forest. Quickly. Meanwhile we shall fend off these blighted trees.'
Left with little option you rush through an opening among the animated trees which the ents pummel open and rush into the tower.
Exit the cellar?
Through the gloom you make hooded figures accompanied by strange mushroom-like creatures. The hooded figures turn at your approach and attack in a frenzy. The strange creatures follow their lead.

Having dispatched the guardians. You examine what was being guarded. Small stones that glitter chaotically in the light are lumped around the roots of the trees above in an intricate pattern. Disrupt the pattern?
Whatever power these stones had seems to have depleted. The roots slowly begin to draw back up into the earth.
Leave the tower?

You peer out the door and realize that Baille's trees are still animated. They continue to rise from the ground after being pummeled by the ents. The ents by contrast, do not rise once they have been struck down. Perhaps you did not find all the roots.

A much diminished force of ents continues to smash at the now unanimated trees. Their fury continues to overwhelm them. They notice you have left the squat tower and begin smashing at it with their gnarly fists.

The tower is reduced to rubble in less than a minute. The alders begin to calm down and their roots start to delve into the ground. One speaks to you 'you have the friendship of the trees for what you done. We shall stay here and regrow the forest.'

'Bring the battle to the Treeblighter and those craven fools who would follow him into oblivion. Strip the bark from them and leave their wood to rot in the twilight. Take this and remember the power of treekind.' The alder becomes still.
A force of armed men and humanoids watch you from the battlements of this gatehouse. They recognize that you are not of their ranks and rashly flood out to engage you in battle.
An ancient cairn stands here. It has been carved from the rocky canyon that surrounds it. A dark and foul smelling entrance leads down into the darkness. Enter?

You burst into the tower only to be confronted with a score of druids led by a particularly loathsome individual who could only be Baille. Dressed like Rowan but with the mannerisms of one close to insanity, Baille leads his force against you.
You immediately notice a trap door leading down in the corner of the room.
Overcome by the twisted druids you awake to find yourselves hanging from a tree. Your soul is slowly drained from you as the wasting stones gurgle merrily and you begin a descent into oblivion.
You open the door to an unholy scene. A withered corpse radiating immense power towers above its empty crypt. Its turns to you, its eye sockets glowing with a sickening yellow light.

It rasps 'I am pleased that you could make it this far. I have much to thank you for. You have released my glorious Master from his slumber and I can once again direct his troops to rid the earth of vermin such as yourselves.'

'You cannot know how I railed in my unlife as I waited for my Master's living followers to regain their senses. But you have seen to that very effectively. The Shadowgaunt host shall pour forth and I can at last raise Yr Coreag to its former glory.'

'It would be churlish of me not to grant you the greatest gift that the Boneshavers taught me - your lifeless forms shall join me in the dirt nap and know true joy in the service of the Master.' Skeletal forms rise from piles of bones to join him.

You open the door to see the High Prelate on his knees beseeching the wall in front of him. Two large eyes face him but do not seem to move. Whatever the fiend was about to do, you evidently interrupted him.
He rushs to the far wall and presses a hidden button. A horrific sentience casts its attention this way.
A tight passage leads back into the Skull Keep. Follow it?
Climb the ladder?

At last you catch up to Gremyr. He appears exhausted from his flight. As you move to engage, you notice with horror that his shadow moves away from him and blocks your path. This is repeated several times until a group of living shadows surrounds him.

Gremyr pants 'Now you will feel the true power of the Master - shadow magic - nothing can stand against it.' Only now do you finally hear the stealthy footpads of the group of Defenders who followed you into the dark passage.

'I had sought to find out why so many of my city's folk had wandered off to this place. I suspected that these cultists were recruiting my soldiers to sap our strength and so I wandered here to pretend to join their ranks and discover their secret.'

'I managed to fool the underlings, but their priests saw through my deception and had me cast down here to die a slow death. I don't know who these folk are nor their plans for my doomed town. With your leave I shall join you and aid you in your quest.'

'You have the Cauldron. Wondrous news. Perhaps now those swamp beasts will die off and we can rebuild this city. Please take that thing away from this island as soon as possible. Would that I could reward you for your valour, but alas we have nothing.'

Fir'bolg children peer out of the shack and stare with wide eyes at their devasted city home. A generation turned into refugees by the heavy cauldron you hold in your hands. You tell them about the Fir'bolg settlement on the mainland.

A ring of Centaurs has surrounded you. Ironhoof leads them and addresses you: 'well met again noble friends. For two-legs you seem remarkably interesting. Do tell me what Sidhe magic you have been up to.' You relate your recent history to him.

'I don't pretend to understand such things. We centaurs have always been too strong to bother with magic and the like. Enough of this idle chatter too. Rest and we shall sally forth to find out what glorious danger awaits us 'cross the mountains.'
Sally forth
Decline

'Very well, I am old enough to realise that the wise warrior takes time to prepare against a particularly deadly foe. Meet us at out camps along the shores of Lake Circle when you are ready to ride.' With that the troop of centaurs canter off.

'Ahhh, I long to lead our mighty cavalry against the cursed ratfaces. I just hope some are left alive to adorn my blade and soften the footfalls of my polished hooves.' Before he embarks on too much pageantry you set off and the Centaurs follow.
An orc stands here watching you carefully. 'I suppose you're wanting to escape. I can get you out of here, but it will cost you. You interested?'.
Leave the Skull Keep?
Boxes full of greenish glittery stones are stacked here. The stones give off a weak glow. Take them?
Upon contact with flesh a nasty cloud of putrid gas fills the room.
Enter the cave?

Suddenly you are surrounded by a group of large equines. As they clear the low branches of the trees you see that they have the torso and features of humans but the bodies of horses. You recognize them as the legendary beings known as Centaurs.

'Halt', one of them says. 'You dare enter the forbidden lands of the Centaur?' he asks you pointedly. Drawing his sword he rears in the air. The other centaurs encircle you. From the noise of hoofs around you surmise that they are here in strength.

'Thou will accompany myself to our outpost or I shall be forced to separate thine head from thine puny body and drag thy corpse along the high plains for mine own amusement. What sayest thou?' The Centaur demands of you sternly.
Comply
Resist
The Centaur's face breaks into a wicked grin. 'I had hoped you would say that.' He hails to his comrades to 'have at them'. Wave upon wave of centaurs engage you.

The Centaurs escort you to a clearing, all the while watching your every move. In the clearing a large tent has been erected. From within it a large grizzled Centaur emerges. He is even sterner than your lead escort.
'What foolish worms have you brought to annoy me with', he demands of your escort. He turns to you 'Get thyselves hence from these lands or face mine wrath. ' He rears up before you.

Another Centaur hurdles a stump and roars into the clearing, brushing aside other Centaurs who grimace at him sourly. 'Rein thyself in Greyflanks, I bring word from the old man - they are to be brought to him at once ... unharmed by the likes of you.'

The grizzled Centaur, Greyflanks, does not seem to take this command very well. With lightning speed he spins on his forelegs and lands a massive blow to the chest of the newcomer. The other Centaur crashes to the ground but deftly rises, blade in hand.

He speaks calmly but with barely disguised menace to Greyflanks. 'Perhaps I spoke out of turn, wouldst thou relinquish thine authority over these here foreigners. Or shall I invoke the Code.' At this the Centaurs begin to murmur amongst themselves.

Greyflanks considers this, his tail thrashing and his eyes ablaze with fury. After a brief silence he storms into his tent. Crashing sounds resound from within. The newly arrived Centaur addresses you. 'Follow me with haste before more blood is shed.'

You have learned not to anger these proud beings and accede to his demand. The Centaur leads you from the forest and brings you at a steady Canter to a lake surrounded by tents. Hundreds of Centaurs race about. You had best watch yourself.

The passageway ends abruptly at this point. Several pale and exhausted slaves are taking a break, their pickaxes by their sides. At your approach they rush to pick up the pickaxes and start hacking at the wall.

You explain that their enslavement is over. They stare at you blankly and return to their work. You take a pickaxe from one and point to the open air. Stunned, they drop their equipment and stumble to freedom.
A low stone passage has been dug into the mountainside. You have walked by it had you not noticed the tracks leading to and from it.

You are escorted under heavy guard to the edge of the forest. 'Avoid these woods if thoust value thine lives, miscreants.' One utters, waving his blade for emphasis. With that, the Centaurs canter off into the trees.
Centaurs surround you. One addresses you 'One wouldst have thought we had impressed our displeasure upon thee concerning foreigners in these here woods. Take thyself hence or be put to the sword.'

Centaurs surround you once more. 'It is they', one shouts to his comrades. A Centaur approachs. 'A scout hast reported most peculiars happenings in the lands of those wretched humans. Thou wilt explain thyselves to mine superior.'

You are passed through an ever increasing chain of command as sentries demand to know the reasons for your presence. They are clearly not a race of trusting individuals. Finally you arrive in the tent of what you assume must be the premier Centaur.

An old but fierce Centaur he is. He addresses you with more restraint than his kin. 'Greetings and well met my small friends. My appellation wouldst be Ironhoofs. And you hadst better be me telling a canny tale or you'll know well how I earned my name.'
'Take thyselves hence from these woods.'
Among the dusty notes you see a bound grimoire. It is entitled simply 'Amathaon'. You begin to read it.

An ancient butler greets you at the door. 'I have prepared a room for you at the behest of his Lordship. It is located to the southeast of the this, the great hall. I do hope it is to your liking.' He rasps.
This small room is laid out like a luxurious child's bedroom. A large window takes up much of the left wall.
You peer out the window. A pleasant grassy meadow lies beneath.
Whatever was trying to get in the room seems to be gone. Or has it? Perhaps you are just jumping at shadows? An bright red 'E' appears where once the window stood.
Lightning flashs... It looks like something is trying to get in the window.
A powerful wave of energy knocks you backwards.
Wheee....
Some useful magic aides are kept in this chest.

Two impossibly high towers reach to the skies above you. They are made from a pale smooth stone. A cluster of thorns bonds the two together. Whoever built this strange building must have had an incredible knowledge of both stonework and plantlife. Enter?

A prefect looks at you 'Here's who tops our most wanted list. We pay gold for the apprehension of these criminals. Dead or alive. But we only pay out if you bring proof. There are enough braggarts wasting our time as it is.'
Amid some equipment you find the Battle Standard of the Runic Sixth Legion.

'Word on the streets is that he's a contract killer working for one of the merchants. No one can find his hideout though. Can't very well search all the merchant's fine homes without any leads. They'd have you busted down to dock detail.'

'Claims to be the rightful ruler of all Orckind. Just a troublemaker really. No one could organise those orcs, much less get one to do a proper days work. Whingers I call 'em. They used to live in total savagery until we taught them a thing or two.'

'They say he just walked off one night. Noone knows why. He was an accomplished Centurion in one of the toughest Legions. Came from high blood too. He stole the Battle Standard of the Legion. Disgraceful. And for that all of the Sixth want him dead.'

'Seems like a matter for the legions. They must be having trouble if they have posted a bounty. We prefects have enough trouble running the city without doing the legion's work for them. And they act like lords amighty when they come to town n'all.'

Amid some scrolls you find an interesting book concerning 'The Eighth Rune.' It details the worship by the Runics of seven Sacred Runes. A persecuted minority also secretly worship an eighth rune, which is rumoured to be a source of great fire magic.
An angry looking man glares at you as you enter this secret room. 'Come to take me, have you? You'll find that I'm no easy prey.' With that he launches himself at you.
You look around the room. It smells rank in here. The strange man must have been hiding out down here for some time.
As you stand in the centre of this odd group of stone platforms you feel some form of sentience enter the room. A melancholy voice, full of self pity, echoes throughout the damp room.

'Who enters my shrine after such a long absence. My worshippers are no more. Taken from me by a mad and jealous God.' You feel a strange sensation fill your heads. 'You are not of my people. But you oppose the mad God. For that I am pleased.'
'Would you oppose Him? ... Would see him cast down and his followers scattered to the wind? ...
'Then answer me this riddle. Who were my people?'

'That is correct. It pleases me that they are still remembered in these lands. I shall aid you in your struggle, for it pleases me to do so. Take this mighty hammer and smite the mad God with it. I have embued it with the last vestiges of my power.'

'It shall not destroy him. But it will deprive him of godly invulnerability for a short time. Use that time well. Cast him back into darkness where he belongs. Go, and do not waste this gift on lesser beings. For it shall work but once.'
'I shall not assist the ignorant. You are on your own.'
You enter a strange shrine in the back of the cave.
You leave the shrine.
You leave the cave.
You find a worn diary amid some faded papers. Read it?
A long tunnel leads to the north. Frozen air blasts out of it. Head through the tunnel?
Searching the wreck reveals a scroll tucked snugly into a waterproof tube. You crack open the scroll and read its contents. It appears to be the captain's log of whatever ill fated ship this was.
The captain's log contains the usual nautical information except for the last entry which catches your eye.

Captain's log, Day 54. I have come to regret this mission on behalf of my secretive proprietors. Transporting this strange rock which seems so important to them - but yet which they were unwilling to transport themselves despite their capable fleet.

Now I suspect why they were loath to be alone on a ship with it. The crew has definitely changed. Mates with whom I have sailed the endless seas now turn against me, and against each other. A wave of paranoia and hatred has overtaken us.

I lock my quarters at night and sleep with a blade at hand. I have never felt the need to do this, even in pirate infested waters. I am sure this rock is to blame. I even tried to throw it overboard, but was unable to even touch it without flinching.

Tonight, when most of the crew sleeps, I shall beach the ship along the rough shore to the north. If I survive, I shall head out alone and move as far as I can from both this vile rock and those strange men who could desire such a thing.
May Arn forgive me for whatever part I have played in this evil. This will be my final entry.
Leave the grotto?
A long dead corpse lies here, moldy and foul smelling from the damp atmosphere in this grotto. Searching his body reveals a map and some items.
Stepping back from the corpse you notice that you are not alone. Vicious shark faced humanoids have wandered into the area to see what the noise is about. Without warning they attack.
You dig for a time before realising that the earth has compacted itself too densely. You are forced to give up.
The earth is no match for your onslaught. You find a large chest containing a sizable quantity of gold and gems.
Your treasure hunting has attracted the attention of the shark faced denizens of this grotto. They encircle you and attack.
Some sharkfaced humanoids spot you and attack.
Enter the cave?
Leave the damp cave?
A crude wooden bridge barely supports your weight as you cross a small underground river. It looks like the cave network has been severely flooded.
It looks like something has chewed through the rock walls and caused an underground lake, or perhaps the sea, to flood the caverns.
Several rocky beings creatures propel themselves towards you. Huge slathering jaws erupt from their stony surface. Hungrily they attack.
The rock has been chewed away from the end of this tunnel revealing some valuable stones.
The source of the chewed rocks reveals itself. Several boulders seem to come alive at your presence and launch themselves at you. One of them is enormous.
It looks like you have cleared the flooded mines of the strange rock creatures. With the the destruction of the largest one, they will probably be unable to reproduce further.
You leave the tower.

A letter rests on this desk. It reads: 'Jredlol, chief stonemason, know that we must abandon our most beautiful creation, the ivory towers, and build dwellings in the caves. We must take refuge from the coming storm and rebuild after it has passed.'

'Of course the first thing that must be carved from our brother stones must be a new shrine to Domnu. Follow these preliminary drawings. We have driven the red claws from the cave networks, but design reinforced entrances should they return.'
You take the architectural drawings.

A heavily armed Defender awaits you in this secret room. He has gathered some of his cohorts to him for a final showdown. 'At them', he cries 'for the Master.' They engage you. You notice they are backed up by large canine featured humanoids.
Some gatesmen strike a brass gong as you pass but do not interfere with you.
Another gong is sounded as you pass these gates. The gatesmen appear to be looking everywhere but at you.
This squat church hasn't been kept up in recent weeks. Weeds grow around the entranceway and the doors hang open. There is no one inside.
Again the ominous gong sounds but no one approaches you much less looks at you directly.
You leave the building.
Enter the building?
Some vicious looking guards man these gates. They hold large warhounds on leashes. They demand of you your business.
'Begone', they say. And slam the gates.
They seem satisfied. 'You may pass'.

You enter a pleasant looking inn. It seems to be suffering hard times now, though. It is almost completely empty except for some surly looking armed men in the corner. The innkeeper gestures at you to approach him.
'Welcome my good friends', the innkeeper says expansively. 'We are all good friends here. Why don't you take a seat at our finest table and I shall bring you some fine mead. What do you say?'
'Good, I shall be with you in an instant.'

You take a seat at one of the rough tables. A serving girl approaches your table and brings mead. Clumsily, she spills some on you and attempts to wipe it off. 'A thousand apologies, my lord'. She says and scurries off through the door in the south wall.
A moment later you realize some of your gold is missing. Looking at the door through which she retreated you notice that it is ajar. It quickly shuts when you stare in its direction.
The serving girl awaits you beyond this door. She seems unafraid considering her crime.
'I am sorry for my desperate actions' she says, returning your gold. 'I needed to speak with you away from prying eyes. You have probably noticed that something is amiss in this once peaceful town.'

'Slavers have taken over the manor and hold the Thane a prisoner in his own house. It seems he is too cowardly to do anything to oppose these vile men. They have carted off whole families to some stronghold in the north. No one returns.'

'Those members of the guard that tried to resist the Slavers were put to the sword in the main square. Now no one has the will to oppose them. They will allow you in the manor if you tell them your business is 'slaves' for that is all that concerns them.

'Please free this town from their grip before we are all taken away.' She beseeches you. 'I had better return to serving the tables, remember what I said: 'slaves' is the only answer the guards want to hear at the manor gates.' With that she leaves.
A well maintained inn stands here calling itself 'The Stalwart Centaur.' Enter?
A weary merchant peddles his wares in this building.
He then plunges into the opening, laughing with villanous mirth.

You emerge from the stairwell onto the soaring precipace of the tower. A small grove of trees has been planted here. The trees are of considerable age and are still strong despite their decades of neglect by whoever planted them. It is very windy.

Unfortunately, the wind masks the sounds of wings. Suddenly from the clouds above you a group of blue dragons shriek down to their lair on which you are standing. Looks like a mated couple and their brood. They look hungry.
Some hapless victim of the dragons must have been flown here to be devoured. His belongings won't do him any good anymore.
A massive torch is set into the stony ground here. Combustible peat fills the upper brazier. Light it?
Light floods the cavern, revealing more than just stalagmites.
Trolls flood out of the caves to find out why they were summoned. They assume that eating you will be reason enough.
The light reveals some interesting items left by the trolls along the ground that you might missed in the dark.
A ragtag group of thugs, footpads and other undesirables tries to make the jump on you.
A cave entrance is revealed when some thick underbrush is pushed aside.
The tunnel ends at a tight canyon. A crude barricade has been set up to control traffic in this canyon.

A bunch of footpads and their warhounds watch you amble up to the barricade. A small ugly man shouts down to you 'Damn considerate of you to drop in. Just leave your gold and goods by the gate and we'll come and collect it.' He chortles.
Needless to say you deliver an altogether different gift to these miscreants.

What once was a pleasant cottage overlooking an idyllic lake has been turned into Scum central. Tain, the current leader of the Scum, has gathered his remaining forces around him, including some large warhounds.
He possesses just enough intelligence to realize the threat that you pose.  Mustering up what courage they can, the Scum attempt to engulf you.
You search the Scum dwelling for whatever ill-gotten loot they might have collected. Hidden under some half rotten floorboards you find their horde. Not much, times have been tough.
Some decomposing bodies have been stuffed into this tight crevice. They have been stripped of their valuables.

A rough bulwark has been placed at the entrance to this canyon. At your approach a small troll sitting atop it lets out a snarl and several larger trolls appear. They all look down at you. The small troll gestures to you and the trolls advance.
Some more trolls shamble over to see what all the commotion is about.

You stand before the gates of a recently constructed outpost. The efficient design and attention to detail indicates it is a Runic fortification. A dismounted Runic cavalryman calls to you politely. 'Sorry, no civilians allowed in the area, citizen'.
This area is crawling with trolls ... Some crawl towards you.

The remains of trolls, horses and other hapless creatures have been dumped here. Great score marks along the bones and  charring would indicate the presence of large and possibly fire breathing monsters in this valley.
As if you needed further evidence, the flapping of wings heralds the arrival of some smallish red dragons. You are standing in their food pit so you can hardly blame them for trying to eat you.
A mated pair of full grown red dragons and several other young alight near you. They are less than pleased at seeing you wiping off dragon blood off your weapons. They scream in rage and attack.

Palthus of the Runic Light Horse stops his inspection of a recently arrived half-century and approachs you. 'Hail my adventurous friends ...  welcome to the eastern front, land of trolls, trolls and more trolls. Will you share a cup of wine with me?'

'Good, for we have much to speak of.' You enter the barracks and share some fine Runic wine. 'Rank has its privileges.' Palthus says, looking pleased with himself. 'High Command must have wanted to silence me, sending me to this death zone.'

'But at least they promoted me to Lance Captain and gave me my first brigade. My orders are try to pacify the area. Unfortunately the place is crawling with trolls. We don't even have to root them out. They come to us, they love horseflesh it seems.'

'We lost a score of horses before we managed to build a suitable paddock for them. But still the trolls come, boundless in appetite. We even noticed some smaller ones who seemed to be directing them. If they have a command structure I would take it out.'

'Perhaps these smaller trolls are the key.' He jumps up excitedly. 'Would you capture one of them for me? My men are trained in the lance and trolls don't tend to talk much after being skewered. It is much to ask but I would consider it a great favour.'
'Of course, it is asking too much. Well, go in friendship and be on the alert for the trolls.' Palthus returns to his duties.
Runic light cavalry tend to their mounts. They nod at you but remain aloof.
'I knew you wouldn't let me down. Bring one of those ugly bastards back here and we'll talk some more.'

Palthus meets you. 'Boldly done, you have one. Lets take a look.' He takes the trussed up troll and chains him to a post. He kicks the brute awake and it snarls at him. 'Hmm, I had hoped that I would think of something before you returned. '
'Any ideas', says Palthus.

The troll's guttural snarls slowly transform into intelligible speech: 'miserable monkeys in metal mesh. Unhand it. Let it free. Give it horseflesh. Give it sweet horseflesh now. Horse shank roasted over fire. Sweet juices drip down chin. Hmmmm.'

Palthus kicks it and asks why the trolls are so aggressive. The troll looks stunned that he can understand. It says 'Horses, bring horse to lizards. Lizard full, lizard eat horse, no eat troll. Give troll horseflesh. Sweet, juicy. Now, juicy horseflesh.'

Palthus says 'So the trolls seem to be trying to appease some big lizards. They would have to be dragons or something equally terrifying to put that kind of fear into them.' He is interrupted by a loud tumult from outside.
You race outside to see a large force of trolls at the gates. Cavalrymen are racing to mount up and defend the gates. Palthus efficiently takes charge. You are engulfed in battle.

Palthus directs some cavalry units to mop up any remaining trolls in the vicinity, then turns to you 'Vicious bastards aren't they. Did you notice that the little ones don't regenerate? I thought that was typical of all trolls. Strange.'

'I think a scouting expedition is in order. We should ...'. He is interrupted by a frantic groom. 'Captain, Guineterax has been taken.' Palthus looks stunned. 'High Command will nail me to a tree for losing their pride breeding stallion.'

'I will lead a force into the heart of the troll lands. I have no choice. We must find the stallion, if it still lives.' Surrounding cavalrymen nod in agreement. Clearly, their mounts are seen more as comrades in arms than simple animals. 'Join us?'
'I am relieved. Lets mount up and ride.' You leave the garrison and head north through the gates.

You are alarmed to see a large company of heavy cavalry charge toward you from the west. 'Stand down, Palthus, you skirmishers are reassigned. Your failures have reached High Command.' The lead rider says haughtily. 'Impossible', replies Palthus.

'Take your men and begone,' Palthus shouts, 'we have no need of your aid.' The rival companies square off, the emnity between the two is manifest. 'I never offered assistance ... we remember your treachery against our brother Slaine.' They charge.

The heavy cavalry are driven off. Palthus says 'this rivalry which the High Command fosters so carefully will be the death of the Empire.' He shakes his head in frustration. 'Lets continue our journey east.'
You spot some trolls in the distance. They appear to be making their way toward the southwest. They spot you and attack. A small troll in the rear appears to be directing them.

You manage to capture the small troll who was knocked unconcious. You truss him up tightly. Palthus would be most interested in seeing your new 'friend' before it manages to escape its bonds. It would be best to hurry back to see him.
A large paddock full of horses has been set up here. Grooms and stablehands tend carefully to the horses. It looks like an efficient operation.
After the battle the cavalrymen spread out in long lines to prevent trolls getting past them and reaching the undefended horse paddock.

The cavalry are now widely dispersed through the plains. You see scattered skirmishes to the west and north. Palthus studies the bulwark in front of you. 'This must be their lair. We'll never manuevre the horses in those tight canyons.'

He looks at you sheepishly. 'Would you enter these caves and take a look around. We'd be hedged in and slaughtered in there.' Before you can respond Palthus is called off to assist some riders trapped between two large forces of trolls. You are alone.
'You found the stallion.' A forward scout calls excitedly. 'Follow me, lets find the Captain.'
Palthus looks at you with relief. He has gathered the exhausted remnants of his shattered company to him. 'Lets away to the garrison.' He calls and you head off.
You look over the bulwark and see light cavalrymen hard at work fending off attacks by ravenous trolls. Perhaps you should find the stallion before they are all killed.
A dark cave leads into the mountains. There has been a lot of activity here. The trails of countless trolls and even hoof prints mar the ground. Enter?

This cave is full of the small trolls. They huddle around a campfire and call to each other in guttural growls. Some terrified horses are tied up at the back of the cave. One notices you, and they attack with a fury.
Most of the horses are too weak and terrified to move. One fine looking stallion seems to have fared well from its ordeal however. You tether it and bring it with you.
Leave the troll cave?

You return to the garrison. 'We have been through much. The trolls are in disarray. I go now to report to High Command that the area is pacified. Perhaps we shall never see each other again. Take this battle lance to remember me by.' Palthus rides off.

Runic cavalrymen greet you warmly. They mention that Lance Captain Palthus is not here. They do however seem quite talkative and have dropped the familiar Runic attitude of rudeness toward foreigners.

They tell you that New Caster is but a small outpost in the Empire which spans a whole continent. They are miles from their homes which lie over the water to the south. In conversation with them you learn the following about their recent history.

This room is a horticulturist's nightmare. Black roses have grown to immense proportions and fill the room with their venomous thorns. Other strange plants dot the room. It would be death to attempt to scrape past the thorns.

The thorns seem to respond to the power of the alder Ent's gift to you. The room fills with a thick fragrance as the black roses begin to blossom. Their thorns fall to the ground and are replaced by beautiful pettles. You may now pass safely.
You brush against the black roses and receive a vicious cut from the venomous thorns.
A radiant shrine to some unknown deity rests here. A central resting place for some large artifact stands empty. Whatever was kept here has been removed.
A neglected building stands here. Rooting around inside reveals that this place is an abandoned Runic dockyard. Several abandoned galleys have been hauled onto the land. None are remotely seaworthy.
A large cave leads into the dark mountains. Enter?
Some vicious creatures lair in this cave. They bound out, leaping distances of 10' at a time. Savage claws dangle from mottled reddish fur. They are upon you.
Reddish beasts detach themselves from the shadows and are upon you.
A sign reads 'Porthenys.'

You step into a water channel dug into the tunnel. Ripples from your footsteps move along the channel and strike a tightly bound drum at the end of the channel. An eerie noise reverberates through the tunnel.
The drum sets off a spear trap!
A sign reads 'Leper - beware of contamination!'
'Oh, so you've come to steal my treasure is that it?'
A cry of rage is your only answer. A small figure leaps from the strange structure, in midair a bizarre transformation takes place. A large boar lands on the ground and charges you.
The dead boar shifts back into the form of a small harmless looking man.

'Alright, come up' says the man, lowering a stepladder. 'Don't be concerned about the leprosy, its not contagious, but don't spread that around, I can do without those meddlesome bandits poking around. The name's Ardon.' He shouts down.

You reach the small hovel set high in the tree's canopy. A small man with bandaged hands greets you. 'Greetings, please come and share some tea with me. In my youth I wandered the lands and met many strange beasts in the forests and mountains.'

'I even journeyed to the plains of the centaurs to the east, and ventured into the feline infested canyons in the west. I've seen griffons in the snow covered north and even some giant crabs along the southern shores.'

'One legend I heard talk of along the lonely roads ... was the tale of the Hunter and his mystic horn, which is rumoured to grant power over the beasts of the forest. My desire for that relic is so great that I would even trade my treasure for it.'
Ardon looks longingly at the Huntsman's horn. 'I will trade you my greatest, in fact only, possession for that horn.' What say you?

Ardon accepts the horn reverently and then almost forgetfully hands you an ancient tome. For an instant the images of eleven replicas of Ardon stretch out behind him in a line. The twelve images slowly turn into a blinding light and dissipate.
Ardon the leper sits here on a tree ledge humming tunelessly to himself. He greets you but has little of interest to say.

An ancient woman huddles by this river. She is labourously dragging a robe through the river. Over and over again. Blood seeps from the robe and flows down the river. No amount of cleaning by her stops the flow of blood. At your approach she looks up.

You notice a crowd forming around the busy streets. A celebration or some kind of procession seems to be occuring. Nudging into the crowd you see a young boy sitting on a chair held high by some men. The men and the boy look extremely pleased.

As the procession makes its way past you, you overhear some Runic citizens talking. 'The first child of the city to be called to the Runes ... a portentious day to be certain.' Another nods in agreement. The procession passes and the crowd dissipates.

A well armed Runic struts toward you in the street. His swagger conceals a liquid grace. A fine sword dances at his hip. He purposely bumps shoulders with you. 'Watch yourself, barbarian, or I'll have you flogged.' He states challengingly.
Take offence?

He seems very pleased. He looks around. There are no prefects in sight. You can't help but admire his form as he draws his blade and leaps to the attack with lightning fast reflexes. He gains the initiative.
You hear shouting down the streets. Citizens are calling for the prefects. Wisely, you make yourselves scarce.

A small pack of young Centaurs gallops past you. At the last minute the swerve as one and ride straight through you knocking down those not agile enough to leap away into the dust. They snicker as they pass and disappear out of sight.

A lone centaur approachs you. He rushes straight at you but stops and rears into the air before you. 'I'll not have the likes of you soil these lands whilst I draw breath.' He slurs. He is obviously exceptionally drunk. But still deadly. He is upon you.

A large number of centaurs have come to watch the melee. The clap hands to shoulders in salute of your victory. However, you are informed in no uncertain terms that you must now pay a death duty of 100 gold to the Centaur's widowed mare. Do you?
Wise decision. The Centaurs wander off. The matter is considered closed. One young Centaur takes the gold and heads off to inform the mare of her bereavement.

The Centaurs are shocked by your bad manners. It seems they commonly carry about bags of 100 gold with which to pay death duties. Being unable or unwilling to pay is unfathomable to them. They stalk off, ashamed to do you the honour of fighting you.
Your fencer character was impressed with the Runic's lightning fast draw. Incorporating the technique into their training, they gain a bonus to hit their target.
It's before or equal to 8.
It's after 8.

You stand before the inside gates of this well designed castle entrance. The double portcullis gates can easily trap unwanted guests in the kill zone you currently stand in. Bowmen walk along the crenellated walls sizing you up.
After a tense few moments the guards decide you are not a threat and open the portcullis.
The ground is disturbed here.

You come across a band of ruffians holed up here. Edging quietly towards them, you size them up: a motley group of poorly armed brigands, without the sense to post sentries or keep their voices down. Several bodies strewn about indicate a recent catch.
Attack?
The fools react with dismay as you plunge into their midst.
You search the bodies of the ruffian's victims. They look like merchants, but don't seem to have been carrying any wares. One of them is carrying a map etched with an unintelligible message.

You wait by the stone as indicated on the mysterious map. After a time you hear a rustling in the nearby copse of trees. A face appears at the edge of the trees. It whispers 'come into the trees, away from prying eyes.' You head into the copse.

'Did you bring the other message?' says the cloaked man before you. Then he looks at you strangely. A worried look crosses his face. Then realization. 'You're not the messenger - you must have killed him', he cries in anger and lunges at you.
Perplexed, you search his body. You find another map, again with an unintelligble message.
The town blacksmith works here. He appraises you. 'Inspect my fares if you please, fine travellers.'
The local healer resides here.
'But if you're looking for more exotic wares, you might want to inquire with the Thane. He loves to barter for new goods.'
You exit the castle.
A sturdily built castle looms before you. Enter?
A large and inviting looking inn stands here. The sign outside names it 'The White Hart.' Enter?
Exit the White Hart?
A statue stands here, hand extended.

You shake hands with the statue. The arm is loose and levers up and down. This seems to start some internal crank and a small scroll drops out of the statue's armpit and lands on the floor. Inside is yet another strange map.
Nothing seems to happen.

A large room lies beyond this door.  It is well decorated, with unusual statues flanking the walls. Snug looking chairs and bookshelves fill the room. The innkeeper must provide this room as a quiet spot for this guests. The room is empty.
A small bathing area lies beyond this door.
The cheery innkeeper greets you and asks what you'd be wanting.

A gallows stands here. A hangman's noose dangles in front of your eyes. A horrible compulsion to place the noose around your neck pulls at you. You feel an oily corruption seeping into you from the very rocks that form this cursed place.
Place the noose around your neck?
You dangle for a time, the noose tightening around your neck. An entrance appears before your eyes. As the entrance opens fully the rope snaps and you land safely.

The curse of the Bean Nighe manifests itself. Welts appear in your back, cracking the skin open and raw. It feels like whiplike blows are striking into you. You double over in pain. The wounds age and fester in a matter of minutes.

Her eyes are pools of rage. Her face contorts as she sets eyes upon you. 'Come to witness my suffering have you. Join me in it ... revel in it ... may you never know peace until I too have found it. I curse you.' She points at you and you feel her aura.

'The curse will visit you every three days hence until my spirit is laid to rest. Heed me not and die in agony. My remains were not laid to rest in my family's tomb. This wrong shall be righted before you know peace. Now go.'

A wise old Centaur lives in this tent. He is knowledgeable in the use of herbs and has even mastered some powerful healing magic. It is rumoured he learnt it while travelling through the lands of the Sidhe long ago.
A centaur blacksmith with biceps like boulders sweats in this smoky tent. He shows you his wares.
Seanchan, Wizard of Porthenys nods politely at you but with barely disguised indifference.
Seanchan, Wizard of Porthenys stares at you. 'You have the geas of the Bean Nighe about you. I can sense its powerful magic wrapped around you like a shroud. Would you know more?'

'Wise, for only with wisdom can the curse be lifted. The Bean Nighe is not a malicious spirit, but one that demands a specific wrong be righted before its curse is lifted. What did this spirit say to you before bestowing it's geas upon you?'

You inform the wizard about the vague tale told by the spirit about its body not being laid to rest satisfactorily. He shudders, 'that story strikes home. One of the Thane's Guard Sergeants lost his wife in childbirth a month past.'

'For some reason he demanded that she not be buried with her family in the hallowed island, even though this runs contrary to our traditions. When pressed he became incensed and no one mentions it now. He tends to bury his sorrows in the Hart now.'

'Clearly, you had better speak with him. The little I know of the Bean Nighe is that the geas will not be lifted until the specific demand has been met.' The wizard shrugs and speaks no more of the matter.

A greatly intoxicated and morose guardsman sits here. He stares blankly at the wooden table in front of him. Occasionally he reaches for a tankard, more often than not spilling cheap ale across the table. He takes no notice of you.

'I want to talk about your wife', you say bluntly. This shocks the guard from his torpor. Bloodshot piglike eyes barely focus upon you. 'How dare you soil her memory with your filthy mouth' he roars attempting to rise. He falls to the floor.

You sit at the table and wait for him to compose himself. He seems to realize he is making a fool of himself and quickly regains his seat to restore whatever dignity remains in him. You take this opportunity to tell him about the Bean Nighe.

His eyes widen. 'You're being punished too', he whispers and gingerly shows you his back. Painful infected welts crisscross his back. 'I started to suffer these periodic attacks after my wife died. I thought it was my grief, but there is something more.'

'She died in childbirth. Thoughts began to fill my head that she had been punished because the child was not mine. I felt it like it was a certainty, though that certainty has faded with time. I refused to bury her with honour, with her kinfolk.'

'Now I suspect that I was a fool. What will become of me?' He holds his head in self-pity. 'Where did you put her body?' you ask point blank. Quietly he draws you a map. He stands, a tranquil expression on his face. Without a word he stalks from the inn.
The ground is too hard.
You unearth a small body, wrapped in a dark bloodstained robe.
Bury the woman's remains in the family plot?
You feel as though something has been lifted from you.
This small island is hallowed ground. Several tomb stones dot the land. A large family plot stands before you.
You sup some fine honey flavoured ale.
You eat some excellent mutton and feel the better for it.
'No problem, just follow the door in the corner upstairs. Choose any room, we don't have any other guests.'
The innkeeper calls out to you 'thats for paying guests of the inn.'

A squat lighthouse stands here. A massive stone casts radiant light at the top of the tower. It must be visible for several miles off shore. The lighthouse seems deserted. It is covered in dust. A ladder leads up to the platform where the stone lies.
Climb up?
You reach the top of the lighthouse and regard the stone. Searing pain jolts you as the incredibly bright stone is unbearable at this distance. Hastily you retreat.

Much of the shelves contain books on the sea. One particularly well tended book is concerned with the Sea God, Manannan. On the inside cover is an unintelligible message:   tHrfetratHdtsnhpcahloolptSoyre
The sign reads 'Pengelly'.

You enter a communal hall. The Thane of Pengelly sits at the table surrounded by his guards. He looks pathetic. Drunk and barely coherent. He slurs softly to his men who turn away in embarrassment. They cannot meet your eyes.

'Don't bother us, ' says the guard witheringly. 'Go see the men off the throne room for your commodities.' He looks at you with disgust. He glances at his Thane who takes no notice. He regards his Thane with equal disgust if not more.

'Welcome to Pengelly, all is well.' Slurs the Thane. His accent combined with his drunkenness make him almost incoherent to you. He returns to his drinking. His guards shake their heads and look away from this wretched scene.

A guard stands beyond this door. 'You'll be wanting to see our stock will you.' He says,  more than a trace of contempt in his voice. 'Follow me.' He leads you into an inner courtyard. Cells line the perimeter. Perhaps they once held cattle.

But their present use is clear. Townsfolk have been herded into the cells and locked up. A man hangs from a makeshift gallow at the end of the courtyard. When you stare at him the guard says bitterly 'A warning for those that question the new ways.'

Some heavily armoured men emerge from the far wall and fill the courtyard. The guard stammers 'they're wanting to see your stock.' An armoured man laughs viciously, 'they can join them in servitude to the Master in that case.' They pounce upon you.

The Pengelly guard lets out a cry. More of the heavily armed men pour forth from the far wall. But a group of the Thanes men come charging from behind you. The two sides eye each other up. The Thane's men defiantly stand beside you.
The heavily armoured men laugh at the Pengelly guards. One gestures to the hanged man and says 'Eager to join your comrade are you? It will be our pleasure.' Violence ensues.

The entire household of the castle comes to witness the end of the hated slavers. They free their enslaved kin and knock down the grisly gallows. The Thanes men let out a cheer. The Thane is nowhere to be seen however.
'I didn't see their leader, Reismar', one says to you, 'he could still be about. Be careful, he is a deadly swordsman.' He turns to tend to his wounded comrades.
The Defenders have turned what used to be a storehouse into their makeshift office. Ledgers relating the shipments of slaves to the north fill the room.
Hidden behind some empty boxes you find a secret door.

You inform the Thane that Reismar, leader of the slavers, has breathed his last. The Thane regards you, barely comprehending what you say. It finally dawns on you. He has been broken by his ordeal. He is an empty shell of a man. You leave him to it.
The Thane sits here alone. He hasn't moved since last you saw him.

Word of the overthrow of the slavers has spread. Freed slaves tearfully hold their kin. Others search frantically for loved ones amid the crowd. Other wail in misery when they realize their loves one are gone. You are ignored in the tumult.

The innkeeper greets you warmly. 'Hail the saviours of Pengelly.' He pours some rounds and hands them to you. 'I never thought to see the end of those slaver vermin.' He says with hatred. 'Where is your serving girl?' you ask.
The innkeeper blurts out. 'What serving girl? My daughter used to assist me, months before ... the ... the young girls were taken first ... and ... ' He breaks down.
You see that the scars of the slavers will take long to heal, if ever... Your good humour dispelled, you take your leave of the inn. The door locks behind you. The lights of the inn go dark.
The merchants looks at you. 'You freed my son. May the Gods smile upon you. For you I shall trade at cost.'

Some groups of people are starting to clean up the church. You overhear that the place was closed down by the slavers. Now people are free to worship their chosen gods again and are taking advantage of it.
The guards of this gatehouse are prepared for you. They fire a clumsy catapult at you. A massive glob of flaming tar sails into the air.
And lands near you splashing you with the searing hot, sticking substance.
The guards then rush out to finish you off.
The Thane of Porthenys stands here.
The Thane greets you enthusiastically 'You rid these lands of the aptly named Scum. Well done. You have my thanks. Let me reward you.'
The Thane thanks you again and turns to discuss other matters with his wizard. You get the idea you are dismissed.
You hear some rustling noises. Sounds like something lies ahead. Retreat?
Strange forest creatures pounce upon you from the forest floor. Their camouflage is perfect for these woods and they gain the initiative.
Their booty is now your booty.
A group of large humanoids huddles around this campfire. They growl in guttural tones to one another. At your approach they rush to engage you.
The humanoids that reside in this cave have heard you coming. They pounce upon as you enter the cave.
A skull stands here, dull and lifeless.
The Thane's private quarters. They are slovenly with a slight smell of mold to them.
This looks like guards common area. It is deserted.
The Thane's throne room. Completely deserted.
A snowlogged hunting cabin stands here. It is terrible disrepair but shows signs of recent activity.
The local priest resides here. A whale bone shrine to Manannan, God of the Sea stands well tended before the house.
Nordman marines refuse access to their precious ships.
The Nordman mariner's hail in greeting to Hreidmar as you pass towards his ship Skidbladnir.

Some fierce looking Nordman guards man this rough stone gate. They call down to you in gruff voices 'what brings you sorry lot to the frozen north?' They laugh at your discomfort in these chilling lands. But they open the gates and let you pass.

You tell the priest of your quest on behalf of the prelate of Manannan. His eyes shine with religious fervour. 'To aid in such a quest, truly you are blessed.' He says benignly. 'Seek Hreidmar, only his ship Skidbladnir can make the necessary voyage.'

'Seek him in the valley of griffons to the east. Beware, it is a dangerous place as the griffon's are ravenous this time of year. He tends to make camp at an old hunting cabin along the frozen lake. Good luck.'
Manannan's priest blesses you and offers his services. For a reasonable fee of course.
The small community maintains a large central campfire at this spot.
A small shop with a marginal stock stands here. The shopkeeper looks at you hopefully.
The Helmsman shakes his head. 'If we go up there we'll not make it home before the storm hits. But it's your boat.'
The sea starts to churn. The Helmsman shouts above the tumult 'warm waters from the south make this part of the sea deadly, perhaps we should head north.'
'I rather you didn't root through my personal things upstairs if you don't mind.' Rowan says patiently.
A large gargoyle statue blocks the corridor. As you step foot into the corridor the statue automatically animates and swoops upon you.

You enter the lighthouse and find a temple inside. Two Kelpie flank a woman wearing shimmering robes. The Kelpie pointedly ignore you while the woman speaks, 'Only the wisest can enter here. Therefore I salute you.' She bows extravagantly.

'Clearly you are not of the faith. You must be resourceful adventurers in that case. The Sealord's mighty hand is clearly at work here. We have great need of such resourcefulness. Would you perform a task for the Sealord?'

'I am pleased. We have received word that a mighty artifact has washed ashore from the watery kingdom of the Sealord Manannan Himself. Unfortunately, mischievous sprites known as Korrigan found it first. We failed our Lord.' She says with shame.

'We know that the Korrigans prefer to live in wells dug by humans. They love shiny objects and spread rumours that wishs will be granted if folk drop coins in the well. They are not evil but their humour borders on the malicious.'

'Our agents wandered the lands, following rumours of these false 'wishing wells', but for naught. The only useful lead we discovered was that of a well far in the frozen north among the Nordman. Seek the local priest, he is of the faith.' She finishes.
'Seek the Korrigan's well. And may Manannan smile upon you.'
A remote lighthouse stands here. Waves crash against the rocks. Enter?
Leave the temple?

Her eyes light up upon sight of  Manannan's Favour. 'I see you already been of service to the Sealord. You carry a shield blessed by His own hand. I am very impressed. Word has spread of the removal of the vile spirit, the Loireag.' She says.

A collection of rich Runic merchants lounges about in this opulent room. They are dressed in fine clothing and feast upon exotic foods from the far corners of the vast Runic empire. One glances at you and gestures for you to approach, his mouth full.
A sign reads 'Merchant's Quarters.'

He swallows the morsel from the shank of lamb he was chewing on. 'You're not Runics but you look a cut above the other barbarians that people this land. I have made my riches from being able to judge people.'

'Should this wasteful war ever end between the Empire and the locals please come back and see me. I will have need of such as you. The locals probably won't warm too quickly to us Runics, but you can be my agent with these people.'
'That's all. Thanks for your time.' He waves you away dismissively.
The merchant's are very excited about the prospect of peace. Trade routes are being planned and there is much of talk of new exotic items to be bought and sold.
One particularly gluttonous merchant glances at you and hurriedly gestures to you to approach him. 'Good to see you my friends, would you consider being my agents in this land of Karnak?'

'Good. I need a steady supply of tin. I hear this land is rich in this metal. The Legions will pay well for weapons made from it. Please contact whoever you can to secure me a supply of it. Return to me if you have any success and I shall reward you.'
Your merchant employer asks where his tin is. When you explain that no trade route has been set up he waves you away angrily. 'Results, not excuses, is what I require.'
You discuss with the tinner the possibility of setting up a trade route with the Runic merchant. He seems very interested.
'We'd love to sell tin to the Runics. But we cannot as long as the tin mines are closed down due to those bizarre rock creatures.'

'Of course we can set up the trade route. Since you cleared the mines for us we have set up operations again. We shall start shipping tin to the Runic city right away.' He rushes around the room excitedly.
'Superb. The tin supply has started to flow from the Karnak lands. I stand to make a tidy profit. Let me express my thanks to you.' He you hands a huge sum of gold and returns to his scheming.
Light from above casts dim rays down here. Climb up the rope?
You come across what looks like a small abandoned village. A well stands in the middle.
Griffons flock down from neary cliffs and pounce hungrily upon you.
Inside the dark cave you find a pair of vicious looking serpents. They crawl towards you.
You enter the dark cave and interrupt a group of large snakes resting among the cold stones.
The butler politely informs you that no one is allowed inside the manorhouse until Lord Godolphin has been returned safely.

An armsman you recognize from Godolphin's manor rushes up to you. 'Have you seen Lord Godolphin recently.' He asks you hurriedly. When you respond in the negative he says 'He is missing. Blood was found in his room. He must have been taken.'
'Teutates, one of his trusted armsmen, is also missing. Please be on the lookout for either of them. We are scouring the lands.' He rushes off.

You enter the mayor's residence. A Karnak veteran who you recognize as Teutates stands here with the former mayor of Ryn. Several armsmen lounge around the room. Other men who are clearly Silverband enforcers regard with hatred. They charge.
The mayor's residence. Currently the deposed mayor is held here under house arrest.

Rolled up in a thick rug is an unconscious body. Unrolling it you discover Godolphin with a vicious bruise to his forehead. You revive him and he opens his eyes painfully. He regards you. 'How many times will I have to thank you for your timely aid?'

'I can't believe Teutates would betray me with these knaves. I heard them talk of taking me to the east. That didn't make sense to me. I guess we'll never know their true motives. I had better get back to the manor. Thanks again.' He staggers off.
You enter a valley of snowcovered forests encircled by high mountains.
Stretching out before you is a vast forest with dark, forbidding peaks in the distance.

Its a finely appointed inn. Rich marble tiles and fanciful decorations abound. The atmosphere is hardly relaxed however. A table of orcs glower at a table of off duty Legionnaires who cast dark looks at both the orcs and another table of mercenaries.

A group of off duty Legionnaires sit at this table. They seem preoccupied with the other inhabitants of this inn and dismiss you immediately as being less of a threat than the orcs and the mercenaries.

One of the Runics looks at you narrowly. He says 'I know you, you freed me from those hideous creatures in that Karnak town. I owe you my life. I'll let you in on a secret. We have set up some pit fights underneath the northeast guard tower.'

'Come over between 10 and 12 at night and join the action. Don't mention it to any prefects, its been outlawed. But we miss the gladiorial arenas back home. This is the closest we could get to copying it. There is precious little else to do here.'
The other legionnaires nod in assent. 'Hope to see you there, you could win some serious gold with your fighting skills.' He returns to his cups.
Some legionnaires are stealthily making their way into the tower. Several orcs and other city dwellers are following them. Enter?
Leave the arena?

The subterranean room booms with the noise of a bloodthirsty crowd of Runics and orcs watching figures fighting in the centre of the arena. The rules are simple: single combat only and combatants can only use weapons provided by the arena.
Do you wish to participate?
Your fighter shall now choose their gladitorial style. Make sure it's the gladiator who chooses the items, not a spectator.
You are ushered into the ring clutching your equipment in a bundle. The crowd goes wild. They cry for blood. You wait for your opponent...
Empty.
Who shall fight?
Two captured yeti are herded into the arena. They are very popular with the crowd since they are unknown in other parts of the Runic empire. Their savagery also makes them a crowd pleaser.
A captured bear is prodded into the arena. The screams of the crowd goad the mangy creature into a killing frenzy.
Some boars are led into the arena. They immediately charge you.
A massive feline is freed from its cage and prodded into the arena.
Some unhappy trolls are forced into the arena.
The Orcs go wild as a current Orc favourite enters the arena. He looks like he has carved his reputation from flesh of others.
A Runic champion enters the arena. The Runics go wild. The Runic eyes you with contempt and draws his finger across his throat. They roar their approval.

The crowd cheers as you exit the arena clutching your winnings. No sooner have you left then another bout takes place. The bloodthirsty and fickle crowd forgets you as they focus on the next spectacle in a never ending cycle of violence.
A sign reads 'Volenti non fit injuria.' Another sign reads 'Weapons are not allowed in the arena. Your equipment will be restored to you when you leave.'
A ladder leads up to the guardtower. Entry is forbidden.
Off duty guardsmen and other castle denizens lounge around at these tables. They nod to you in greeting. They return to what they were doing.
The Thane stands here in this small throne room. His wizard flanks him and several bored guards line the walls.

The felled Shadowgaunt falls back and undergoes a horrific transformation. It shakes and convulses. Horrified you stare in amazement as another head sprouts from its neck. Both heads turn to you and it renews the attack full of vigour.
The dying Shadowgaunt lets out a blast of pure negative energy.
The mysterious Aranflame crumples from the fatal blow.
Vesta falls to the floor. 'Save my beloved Porthenys.' She gasps before she falls dead.
Gwydion is hit by a fatal blow. He crumples to the floor. Strangely, his final expression is one of great joy and peace.
