An enchanter sits at this table, playing a game of chess. He seems lost in thought. He glances up at your approach. 'Ah, the eternal adventurers. How often have I said those words, and how often will I say it in the many futures?'

'Shall I join your party or shall I sit here indefinitely. I have no memory of my past but I see the many flows of possibility before me. Perhaps it matters not ... I don't know.' He shakes his head. 'Well, will you have me?' he asks nonchalantly.
Some giant badgers rush out of the undergrowth and attack.
A pack of wild boars rush at you.
A pack of famished wolves have been following your spoor. They take this opportunity to attack.
Some spiders leap from trees and attack.
Some giant snakes jump out of trees and slither toward you.
You enter what looks like a hollowed out mine shaft.
Select your most intelligent character:
The monstrous abomination collapses into its slimy vegetable components. Shrieking spirits stream from the remains and disappear into the air.
'I really don't know.'

Rowan peruses the vile book. He is clearly uncomfortable in its presence. 'The little of it that I can understand speaks of the cyclical nature of the Grey God and His connection to some comet that periodically comes close to our world.'

'This would make sense as history reveals various mentions of his scourge from time to time. The prophecy also speaks of something of great import: the Grey God manifests himself in the form of an Avatar while in this plane of existence.'

'The Avatar is impervious to damage. I suspect we will need the assistance of our own Gods to counter his infernal power. Do not attempt to face the Avatar until you are certain you possess the tools necessary to defeat Him.'
'I heard rumours of a gang of bandits making nuisances of themselves in the north. Other than that I know nothing.'

'Manannan is the God of the Sea and a very popular god for these coastal regions. He is wild and unpredictable, like the sea itself, and I have never been able to fathom what role he plays in the Struggle.'
Some unusual looking horses gallop from a nearby river. They rush towards you. As they near you notice these horses have fangs!
'You possess the Fomorian Hammer!' Rowan exclaims. '

A knight stands before you frozen in place. A thin transparent crystalline substance covers him entirely. He has very fine features and pointed ears. He is stretching down toward the skull in front of him. A look of despair is etched onto his face.

The ensorcelled skull is freed from the vile magic that possessed it. The knight suddenly animates. He turns to look at you sadly. His eyes focus on the skull in your hands. He speaks somberly 'you hold the skull of my youngest child.'
A skull sits at your feet.

'The vile Boneshavers turned my son's remains into a weapon. A spell weapon called a Tathlum. There is no depth to which they would not sink. They were unable to face me in battle so they slew my son and cast their curses on his skull.'

'While I stood entranced they desecrated the temple and slew my comrades. I watched it all, unable to even close my eyes.' He pauses. 'I am unable to sense any of my kind. Perhaps the Boneshavers tracked them down and killed them.'

He asks you the year. 'So, I stood here helpless for a hundred years while my people were cut down.' He says grimly. 'I have failed in my sacred task. At least I can reverse some of the desecration.' He begins to concentrate.

'I thank you for my deliverance. But there is much that I must do. We shall meet again, it has been foretold. My name is Peredur, formerly the guardian of the temple of Slieve Fuad. But now I have no ties and a score to settle.' With that he gallops out.
An ancient ruined temple lies here, partly reclaimed by the forest. Enter?

The temple has been long abandoned. Moldly skeletons line the floor. Clearly, they ended their days in violence. A knight stands motionless in the centre of the room. Behind him an altar has been smashed into bits. Skull motifs line the once rich mosaic.
You exit the abandoned temple.
You can hear a faint scratching noise from the closet door in the back of the room.
You hear the movement of stone somewhere in the distance.
Angry water spirits rise from the water and engulf you.
Huge crabs live on this shelf. They don't take kindly to your intrusion.
A bridge made of hardened sand leads through this watery room to a far shelf.
Hreidmar looks at the well. He looks confused. He says 'I don't understand, if you abandon a well this far north it freezes. But this one doesn't seem frozen at all.'
Serpents surface near you. They attack!

You venture boldly into lands untrod by the living in a century. The Centaurs have spread out behind you to form a flying skirmish line. They seem eager for battle. Moving forward you see an incredible scene unfold.

A battle is taking place before you - but the battle is taking place in slow motion. Huge shaggy beasts engage mounted knights in agonizing slow detail. Gradually the action of the combatants speeds up and begins to return to normal.

Before you have time to ponder this strange activity the battle moves toward you as the beasts press the outnumbered knights towards your position. You join a battle frozen in time for a hundred years!
Know fear. More of the huge beasts flood from the north.
Centaur reserves join the fray, charging into the heart of the enemy. You attack with renewed vigour.

Straggling units rally around your position. They look like they've been hit pretty hard too. Centaurs stare in wonder at the knights between tending to one another's wounds. A particularly blood stained knight charges up to you.

'I am not familiar with your tabard, but glad of your timely reinforcement.' He says politely. 'I thought I would make my final journey 'ere you arrived. Know that you have the thanks of Diarmuit ua Duibne.' He rides off. The Centaurs look stunned.
You overhear one say that the knight who addressed you perished more than a hundred years ago. The knights rally and charge to the north as more beasts surge towards you.

The valley seems full of combatants. You notice more of the knights charging against a defensive position of the beasts to the north. To the west you see Centaurs engaged in a vicious hit and run skirmish with the beasts. Again the battle is joined.
Again more beasts rush to aid their cruel brethren. Is there no end to them! The beasts let out a guttural roar and attack with increased ferocity. You fight on stoically.

You hear a odd sound in the distance. More reinforcements for the beasts no doubt. But then you start to recognize the sound. The calls of Runic battle horns fills the valley, echoing off the rocky sides.

The beasts fall back against your onslaught. They split into two groups. One groups heads through a canyon to the northeast, another heads through a canyon to the northwest. You take this opportunity to rest and reflect on your victories.

You see a company of Fir'bolg archers marching to your position. Their leader hails you. 'Well fought, we'll drive the rat-faces out before long.' He smiles weakly. He carries along the lines voicing similar statements to his fellows.

As he turns you notice that he holds his stomach tightly. Blood covers his leather vest and tunic. Clearly, he is using his last moments of life to increase morale among his battered troops. He passes from sight.

You hear a familar voice amongst the din. 'Hello again', says Rowan the Druid. 'I never doubted that you would have achieved so much. Arn has always smiled on those that make their own luck.' He looks older and more haggard then when last you saw him.

Suddenly, a wave of evil overwhelms you, thick like an oily cloud. You turn to see its source, a lone man in the distance. He incants an unholy prayer and you feel overwhelmed with the insatiable need for blood. You turn to the nearest victim: Rowan.

'Hold', shouts Rowan and the feeling lifts you. Around you you see the remnants of the invading force begin to fight savagely amongst themselves. 'Know that that was Clur'Can, one of the greatest disciples to serve the Grey God.'
'I had presumed him dead, but now it seems he was transformed into a lich. Perhaps to continue to serve his master in this land where the living were trapped by Ossian's magic.'

'I had wondered why the Shadowgaunt retreated, for they fear nothing, save their dread master.' He points to a small cairn to the north. 'Venture inside that place of death and destroy the lich Clur'Can before his spell rips this army apart.'

You stand before the eldritch cairn. Behind you a knight gallops you. 'Stay', he shouts. You recognize him as the knight you freed from the Tathlum in the desecrated temple of Slieve Fuad. 'It is I, Peredur. Clur'Can's magic has no hold on me.'
'It was he who ordered the death of my son. It was he who desecrated my sacred temple for his dark master. I shall have my vengeance.' He says grimly. Best not to argue with him. He joins you.
You do not have the luxury of time. Above your head an army of hope destroys iself.

You return to the surface. Rowan awaits you. 'Clur'can's spell has lifted, that can only mean you were successful. However, the damage has been done. The army, both new and old,  has been dealt a serious blow.'

'Gods cannot die as mortals understand death. They can however, be deprived of worshippers, as I, Domnu, have been. I wish this same fate visited upon the Mad God.' With that the sentience slowly dissipates.

'We must move against the Shadowgaunts before more treachery is sent against us. I shall attempt to summon further aid. I suggest you proceed north to hole the 'Gaunts in their fortresses before they can overwhelm us again.'

Rowan speaks urgently. 'You do not yet possess the necessary device to counter the Grey God's protection. Seek it out before you move further against him. Make haste, our remaining forces shall attempt to keep the 'Gaunts at bay.'
'You possess Domnu's Hammer. This gives me hope. Strike the Grey God's Avatar with it to temporarily dispel his invulnerability. Let us proceed.' Rowan waits expectantly.
Peredur steps forward. 'I too have waited long for this day, Clur'Can, I shall destroy you for your crimes against my sacred temple.' Battle is joined.
A fierce battle rages in this choke point. Shadowgaunts hold the position against a valiant assault by the much smaller Fir'bolg. You rush to their aid, joined by several knights and Centaurs.

The battle has drawn to a standstill before this ancient gatehouse. The Shadowguant stand fortified behind the massive black iron gates. Fir'bolg archers, flanked by Centaur, Danaan riders and even a Unicorn face the walls, waiting. Rowan turns to you.

Rowan speaks 'We seem to have a stalemate. We cannot breach the gates and the normally bloodthirsty Shadowgaunt will not emerge for some reason. They appear to be waiting for something ... or someone. Help is on the way, I ...' He in interrupted.

A tumult arises from the gatehouse. The massive gates open and Shadowgaunt pour out. And their head is a particularly massive 'Gaunt carrying a fearsome looking battle axe. They stop. The huge 'Gaunt roars and points at the empty space before him.

'He is challenging our leader to single combat.' Says Rowan. Before anyone can move Diarmuit ua Duibne of the Danaan Riders charges forward to meet the fell beast. All eyes watch the outcome of this battle.

The battle is hard fought, with much blood shed on both sides. Diarmuit calls to his war god Nuad to strengthen his arm. Alas, it is vain. The massive beast eventually catchs him with a cleaving blow with the mighty axe. Diarmuit falls dead.

The 'Gaunts roar with approval. The massive 'Gaunt raises his arms to accept their affirmation. He then points to you and then at the space in front of him. One of you can accept his challenge. Do so?
The 'Gaunts cannot restrain their aggression any longer.  They swarm upon you in a frenzy.
The gatehouse lies undefended.

Imperious gates rise above you blocking the tight canyon. Fir'bolg archers shower the walls with shafts to little effect. You wonder how you could possibly batter these walls down. You turn as familiar resonant voices echo through the canyon behind you.
'Ents', cries a Fir'bolg. 'The Ents have come'. Their flagging morale soars. Enormous Alder Ents file past you towards the massive black iron gates. They start hammering with their gnarly fists.
The gates crash inwards. 'Gaunts stream out to attack you.

The command structure of the invading army has been decimated. Troops start looking to you to follow. Stragglers from the many battles begin to form ranks behind you. Rowan nods approvingly. He whispers to a blackbird on his shoulder. It flies south.

You venture into a twisted forest of mushrooms. The very grass and rocks seem blighted by the aura of evil permeating this valley. A massive castle stands at the head of the valley. A sickly blueish light casts forth from a high tower.

Marching toward you are formations of Shadowgaunts, a huge 'Gaunt in the lead. You are heavily outnumbered even as the mixed troop at your back is bolstered by a trickle of newcomers of all races and species.

'They are led by their Jedda, Warskald. Beware his blade. It was dubbed 'Mercy Killing' by his foes for to be captured alive by the likes of him does not bear thinking about. We must hold them here for a time, my avian friends tell me allies are coming.'
Before you can respond the Shadowgaunts are upon you.
Above the din you hear the war cries of the Karnaks as Lord Godolphin charges the enemy, flanked by a war party. Pengelly guardsmen follow his lead. The battle continues.

You rest as around you see and hear groups of combatants engaged in rolling skirmishes. Mighty Ents take the field against a tight formation of 'Gaunts, pummeling them but taking terrible wounds in return.

The Shadowgaunts are implacable in their attack. They refuse to retreat and are beginning to break the army's morale. Hardly any Centaurs or Danaan riders are left standing. You are again engulfed in the melee.
Waves of dimunitive Knockers join the fray, accompanied by their allies of old, the Selkin. They show little fear as they swarm the much larger Shadowgaunt.

Gasping with the effort of your struggles you look around. The twisted forest is a scene of carnage. Bodies of the mixed alliance litter the floor. Shadowgaunts lie dead by the hundreds. Rowan moves among the wounded offering what relief he can.

He comes to you 'well fought. The Shadowgaunts have fled to their ancient cities through the eastern valley. But for you the final battle has yet to come. You must venture in the Grey God's castle and finish this.'

A bedraggled and bleeding Godolphin approachs. 'I shall aid them' he cries. 'No', Rowan says forcefully. 'They are fated to accomplish this task.' Godolphin relents crestfallen. 'Go now and face the Grey God. We shall finish what needs be done out here.'
Rowan lets his aura fill you.
The ancient structures of the Shadowgaunts fill the city. Various units from the mixed alliance comb the twisted lanes searching out the enemy. There are none to be found however.
There is a great deal of activity in the valley to the west. This way lies empty and silent. Your intuition tells you that west is the direction you should be heading in.

'I tell you what, if you pay his bond of 500 gold. You can take him with you - as far from here as possible.' The ogrish man nods his head at this suggestion. 'Yes, pay the money and I will serve you well. I fight with the strength of ten men.' He says.
Pay the bond of 500 gold?
'You don't have the gold, so don't waste my time.' The guard says irritably. You back away.
The guard takes the gold and releases the ogrish man. He thanks you and introduces himself as Beleg. 'You won't regret it.' He says. The guard shakes his head in doubt.

The Thane abruptly ends his conversation with the wizard. He sizes you up. He doesn't waste time. 'We have us a bandit problem in the area. Most of the guard force are otherwise engaged so I'm looking for a small strike team to crack some heads.'
'Interested?'

'Good, our scouts report suspicious movements of men around the cliffs near the lake to the northwest. You know the routine. Take this map. Wipe them out and report back for your reward.' The Thane returns to his business.
Hideous beasts clamber toward you.
'Good, go through the tunnel behind me. I've been digging it for some time now.' You walk through a well concealed hole in the wall and through a dank tunnel, tight passage.
The orcs seem to have laid claim to this large room. All eyes are on you. No move is made against you though.

You find the latch concealed in this tunnel and proceed into a dank room. Several orcs are waiting in here. They don't look interested in helping you escape. Instead they jump you for your possessions.
You search the room. It offers no escape.
You open the cupboard and witness a world gone mad.
The Runic innkeeper looks down his patrician nose at you. 'We only sell fine wines, if you can afford it.' He says the last as if he doubts that you could.

The innkeeper sniffs but pours the wine. You swill the wine around in your mouth. A solid wine, full of character, a hint of lavender. A good table wine - although the imported vines don't seem to have taken well to the damp climate and acidic soil.

The innkeeper loses some of his disdain and pours the sweet dessert wine into small glasses. It tastes sickly sweet and leaves a highly acidic after-taste in your mouth. It must have travelled at sea for some time.

'Of course', says the Innkeeper, desperately trying not to let the avarice in his eyes flood all over his face. He pours the wine from a dusty bottle. The wine is exquisite and well taken care of, but at the price what's the point.
The Guildmaster stands here. 'This Runic conflict has certainly hurt us deeply. With the trade routes cut off for so long, it will take years for us to recover contacts and partners.' He signs.
You show the prefect Gruumsh's Cleaver. 'Thats good enough for me, ' he says happily crossing the orc general's name off his list. 'Here's the bounty.'

You show the prefect the Runic battle standard. 'Fine work, the Sixth Legion will be very pleased, ' he says happily crossing the former Centurion's name off his list. 'Here's the bounty. Oh, but I'll keep the standard.'

You show the prefect the Rune Mask. 'That's his alright. I'm glad he's dead. That Cult of the Eighth Rune. Bunch of heretics and troublemakers.' He crosses off the name from his list and hands you the bounty.

'I had no idea they were connected to the Grey God. But from what you have told me they must be. It's a good thing you cleared them out of the abandoned Danaan stronghold. They would have eventually gathered a massive force to serve their grim Lord.'
'Perhaps Manannan is attempting to aid us against the Grey God. I can never understand his true motives. This relic that you seek might prove of use to us. Good luck.'

'You possess Fragarach, Manannan's own blade. A mighty weapon indeed.' Rowan looks carefully at it and frowns. 'But this is not the weapon to pierce the Grey God's invulnerability. There must be another. There must be.' He says grimly.
You don't know where to teleport to so the spell is wasted.
You set off the fire glyph!
Looking closely at this odd stone you see a tiny weathered face in the centre. Concentrating on the stone you feel a sentience within it. Thoughts spring unbidden to your mind.

You see a oddly shaped group of gnomes building magnificent towers of stone. Wondrous gardens cover the many layers of the towers. A shadow is cast upon the scene. The gnomes flee in fear from a group of demonic beasts that attack them mercilessly.

The gnomes defense is inadequate and they are rounded up and taken to some ghastly city. An image of the city forms in your mind as if from above. Quickly you write the image down before you forget. A faint voice says 'End it.' and all is quiet.
You hear a massive troop of mounted men coming your way. 'Clear the way' they cry and rush past you. They take no notice of you.
The Fir'bolg advise you to storm the fortress of the Seven while they comb the valley for orcs.
You don the Phylactery of Clur'can. Upon contact with flesh Clur'can is immediately given form once more and takes his revenge.
'Perhaps if you find it we can trade.' He returns to other pursuits.
You defeat the gateguards but see what looks like two entire legions rapidly approaching the gate. You back away before they engulf you with their vastly superior numbers.
Large felines attack!
Rejoice, the Loireag is vanquished! The Flood Hag is no more. You hear distant clapping of waves upon the shore.
The Praetor has dismissed you from his thoughts as only a true patrician can. The prefects grin at you maliciously.
Some surly orcs glance at you. They definitely don't want your company.
Innkeepers throughout the land rejoice as the scourge of all drinking establishments finally meets his end.
You stumble upon an orc patrol.
You encounter a pack of mercenaries.
Some demons that have been summoned but are now masterless see you and attack with a fury.
You stumble upon some of the faithful dutifully patrolling the area.
Some novices scurrying on some errand almost bump into you. They attack almost as instinct.
Undead, attracted to the overpowering evil of Clur'can, stumble toward you.

Your attention is directed to some dark rocks which appear to be moving toward you. Suddenly, they are revealed to be large, black crabs clambering toward you, pincers raised in anger at your intrusion.

You sense a presence in the room. Although the presence drips with evil it takes no notice of you. Rather it radiates joy at being free again. Whatever it is, it sweeps out of the room and away. What have you released?

The loom begins sewing the thread into a garment. The Sidhe script begins to glow as powerful dweomers are imbued into the garment. Finally a wondrous cloak is produced. The thread has been used up entirely.

This ancient loom is beautifully crafted and covered in mystical Elven script. Although you lack any skill in tailoring, the loom seems to operate of its own accord when presented with the thread you found.
You've found the dragon's hoard!
You deftly grab a burning piece of paper from the fire. Its looks like a page from a book and contains an odd magical symbol.
Yoink...
Who will open?

'Word has reached us! You cleared the mine! Well done. You have the gratitude of what is left of the Guild. You deserve the standard 10% prospector's fee. Here is 500 gold. Thank you.' Says the tinner.
The Runic Light Horse man the gates of this outpost. They allow you to enter.

Runic guards man these gates. 'Sorry citizen, no one is allowed through the wall until the area beyond has been pacified.' This is indicative of classic Runic thinking: if you don't control a situation build a wall around it.

These were merely the lead riders. They delayed you long enough to surround your position. Hundreds of Centaurs roam through the woods around you. You have no choice but to retreat. You slowly walk away from the fearsome ensemble.
Free
Reuse
An ancient and faded mural stands above what is left of the desecrated shrine. The mural depicts some kind of rider.
The cramped living quarters of the Knockerkin lie beyond this door.
Centaurs roam around in this large tent. They use this as a staging ground for patrolling the area. They take little interest in you.
You feel a barely suppressible desire to journey to the east.
You sense absolute nothingness in response.
Nothing noteworthy happens.
The earth is disturbed here. Investigate?

In your enhanced state you can make out every tuft of hair on the magnificent animals as they amble beside the lake. The clatter of their paws over the pebbles rings in your ears. The spray from a mighty claw slashing through the water hangs in the air.
After a time you wake. You feel very relaxed but somewhat hungry. You bid Greyclaw farewell and return to your journeys.

The defeat of Gremyr is a major accomplishment. Major powers turn their attention your way. Word of this deed will spread among the forces opposing the Grey God. It will also earn you the emnity of some very powerful beings.
That wiped the arrogant smirk off of what's left of his face.
The Dragonrider looks in amazement at his wounds. Convinced he was invincible, he seems to die more of shock than injury.
The Dragonrider desperately attempts to wipe off the blood from his shiny armour. He uses his last breath to keep up his apperance.
Some small hairy men dash past you in the grip of fear.
Greymr, dark hope of a new generation of worshippers of the Grey God, dies. A inky black cloud forms around him as his soul is removed in screaming agony.
The negative energies that make up this shroud of unlife are released in a horrific screech.
The Avatar's link to the Grey God is severed. His power on this plane has been drastically reduced. The Avatar falls to dust.
The Creeper breaks into a collection of twigs, leaves and soil.
The Hunter lets out a booming laugh as he is cut down. His love of killing so great that even his own death is greatly appreciated.
There seems to be something unusual about the corridor ahead. Who will search for traps?
A big bucket full of blood and gore.
Welk, that irrepressible ankle-biter has bitten the dust. Sadly...
The door reads 'Hall of Blood.' As you cross the door you hear the breaking of crystalline statuettes. Angreden defenders step from their places and attack.
The door reads 'Hall of Shadows.' You enter a room devoid of features other than four foul smelling candles. The flickering shadows around the candles slowly coalesce into vicious spirits.
The door reads 'Hall of Oblivion.' You sense a monstrous evil permeating this area.
You boldly enter the Shadowgaunt's stronghold. Everything is giant size. There are no defences. This is hardly surprising, why would such beasts require any form of defence?
The rearguard of the Shadowgaunt horde have positioned themselves in this featureless hall. Realizing that this is a fight to the finish they pounce upon you.
This plain and unadorned room seems to be a barracks of some kind. From the look of the spartan surroundings you get the feeling that the 'Gaunts know nothing of life except warfare.
Long racks of weapons and coffers full of military equipment fill this huge room. Unfortunately the equipment is all far too large for you.
A mighty pillared throne room lies beyond this door. It is completely deserted.
This must be a crypt for the fallen Jeddas of the Shadowgaunt. You notice that one is empty ready for the body of the beast you dispatched on the field of battle.

A small temple leads off from the throne room. A grisly skull shrine stands against the far wall. The room is not empty however, you see a oddly robed Shadowgaunt and some warriors huddled around the skull. At your intrusion they spring to attack.

Strange patterns adorn the floors of this room. The patterns shift as you watch them. Several demons appear to be feeding on the carcass of some unidentifiable body. They turn to you; dead eyes fix upon you as they move in...
Leave the Shadowgaunt stronghold?
Enter the Shadowgaunt stronghold?
An awesome individual stands before you bathed in a sickly indigo light. This could only be the object of your long struggle: the Avatar of the Grey God himself. It stands lifeless before you.

Slowly dark powers seem to awaken and the Avatar begins to stir. A voice you recognize from dark shrines and underground passage ways addresses you. 'Would be heroes come to put an end to my madness is that it?'

'Grovelling worms at my feet more like. I am aeons old and you are but ephemeral dust motes to be swept away. I possess a thousand souls far more powerful than you. I have swallowed realities whole and brought oblivion to those that would oppose me.'

'You bring the gift of a God who is no more. You think her pretty weapon can defeat a God? I enjoyed watching her scream in helplessness as I consumed the souls of her entire race. They should be honoured to have been granted the gift of oblivion.'

'I shall share my gift with you now. Then I shall consume your souls and send you out as my new disciples. You shall spread terror and pain among your world until my manifestation is complete. Come accept your legacy.'

The Avatar reels from the blow of the Fomorian Hammer. Domnu unleashes a devasting shock wave from her contained essence and the Avatar's divine invulnerability falters. The Goddess' sacrifice was great, she winks out of existence.
The Avatar summons more of the strange bat creatures and engages you.
You leave the stronghold to inform the assembled host of of your victory. A great cheer goes up.

Rowan smiles benignly at you. 'Well done Eternal Champions. Perhaps we shall recognize each other in our next incarnations? But I think not. I go now to serve in another campaign of the endless Struggle. My thoughts are with you.' He vanishes.

You are hoisted on the shoulders of several Centaurs and raced through the valley. Knockers, Selkies, Fir'bolg, De Daanan, Runics, Karnaks, even beasts of the forests join in the celebration.  Past emnities are forgotten in the joy of the moment.

Now comes the greatest challenge of all: peace. All of the assembled groups wish to speak with you and you are jostled back and forth. Eventually the groups begin to disperse and once again cast wary eyes at one another. You can finally rest.
The toadstool bursts into a cloud of itching spores.
The monstrous entity silent slips to the floor. An empty pile of rags lies at your feet.
No effect.
Who will attempt to open it?
The chest bears the seal of 'General Mojril'.
Gwydion is too proud to beg. He leaves to join his people.

You hear a rustling down the hall. You enter the large room. Everything is giant scale in here. A massive chair has been smashed and now forms a bonfire. A squad of heavily armed men stand around it trying to warm themselves.
The Dragonriders barely condescend to spare you a glance. They must assume you are servants and as such beneath their notice.
That doesn't seem to do anything. The door is unlocked though and you can pass freely.
The Thane asks you 'do you want to trade some items? I picked up a tidy little collection in my younger years.'
A simple sign on the door of this croft says 'Hreidmar'. The door is locked and no one appears to be home.
The Fir'bolg queen is slain. Her people look in stunned amazement. Then redouble their efforts.
Something passes through the undergrowth.
It is safe to camp among these apple trees for some reason.

The congregation sits in total rapture. The speaker notices your intrusion. 'Destroy the non-believers' he cries. The room turns into chaos as every head turns to stare at you with fury. The speaker flees east while his congregation engulfs you.
Owwww...

Beta testers - lets get this over with right at the beginning before we all lose our codes etc. If you are not a beta tester - email me at ntt@the-wire.com to become one. This scenario is not generally released otherwise. Tremordred.
Thanks beta testers. Enjoy yourselves. Not back to our scenario ...
The old centaur patiently hears your story. He then launches into a long speech.
Centaurs are rushing about the main tent preparing for war.
You stand before the foul smelling braziers. What do you want to do?
Nothing happens.
Yes but how?
You safely slide down the smooth corridor.
The Tinner is busy organising tin shipments to the Runic Empire. He has no time to spare for you.
Who will take on the monstrous being?
The Avatar of the Grey God has been vanquished. A great day for the forces of good.
You find an interesting item in the crumpled suit of armour.
You find an amulet in the foul smelling rags that used to enshroud Clur'can.
The frozen body of a Karnak human lies here, preserved by the snow. Searching the body reveals some interesting items.
The inhabitants of this cave uncoil from their stalagmites and slither towards you.

As you search the cabin a Nordman enters. He looks surprised to see you. 'I thought I was the only one mad enough to venture into this valley. What brings you here friends?' He says. You mention that you seek Hriedmar on behalf of Manannan.
He says 'Well you have found me. If this is a quest for the Sealord I will assist you. He has spared my life many times on the rough seas. I am at your service.' Hreidmar joins you.
'This well is very strange' says Hreidmar. 'A well left untended in this climate would be frozen solid within hours. But this well hasn't frozen at all?' He shakes his head.

The Prelate of Manannan gazes upon Fragarach, the Blade of the Sealord, with rapture. She reaches towards it, but then stops herself and pulls away. She regards you with awe. 'Truly you are blessed in the eyes of the Sealord.'

'It is only fitting that you take this wondrous artifact and bring glory to the name of the Sealord. Smite those that would seek to bring harm to the Faith. Go from here now. And now that Manannan smiles upon you.' The prelate bids you farewell.
It's too deep for you to reach unfortunately.

A massive gnoll smirks at you from the darkness of the cave. He bares large, dirty canines at you and beckons for you to approach. He grunts in a corruption of the common tongue that he wishes to engage in single combat.
Agree?
While the Chief was attempting to stall you his clan have readied themselves for your assault. They launch themselves at you.
Who will face the beast?
The tower is locked. Rowan has left for new pastures.

The simple croft is occupied by a weather beaten mariner. He sits outside in a thick fur coat gazing over the icy bay. He is watching the boats docked at the harbour. He seems lost in his dreams, most likely of sailing off into the frozen waters.
This house looks abandoned. A sign on the door reads 'House Garanhir'.
Which deity?
The Sealord cannot hear you from this place.
The Sealord seems indifferent to your plight.
It is too early in the day to invoke the Goddess of the Moon.
Arn smiles upon and bathes you in moonlight. Your fatigue dissipates and you feel energized.
It seems an entire day has passed.
Dagda cannot be reached in such a place.
Dagda lends you a small portion of his infinite wisdom. Only those of pure enough mind are able to see its worth.
The strange scene continues. The bard continues to play much to the delight of his audience of one. You are unable to intervene in this perplexing situation.
The Karnak lord is quickly dragged to safety by his fellows.
'Very well', says the Runic. 'I shall have to free myself.' He lunges at you.

This tribe grew to predominance among neighbouring tribes. It settled and built great cities, conquering and annexing its neighbours. Eventually an empire was forged which took the name Runic, in honour of the sacred Runes.

The book makes vague references to the Runes as if everyone reading the book would know all about them. One practice involves the selection of children upon their thirteenth birthday to visit the Runes to receive some sort of blessing.
What happens to the children is not mentioned. However those that are chosen are termed 'Rune-blessed'.

Some big humanoids crash through the forest and appear before you. They are very hairy. They have the legs of fauns, with cloven hooves and small horns. One speaks to you in a gruff voice 'Have you come for the Rut?'

'Good. You look strong. The strongest will lead us. We fight one on one until a new leader is chosen. No killing blows are allowed. Normally we fight bare handed, but you are so small that you may use your pretty weapons. Do you accept?'
Who will fight?

You watch as several of the shaggy beasts engage in vicious battles. They begin with a mighty crashing together of horns, followed by mighty pummels and wrestling. Eventually a particularly massive one takes the lead. You are summoned to take part.
The mighty humanoid falls to the forest floor. The other humanoids clap and dance around the forest glade on their faun legs.

The humanoids, or Urisks, as they call themselves, gather around you. 'You are strong. You are now the leader of the Urisks. Use these pipes to summon us when we are needed. We will come. Now we shall have a wondrous feast.'

You join the Urisk's feast and spend an interesting time with them. They wrestle and play excellent music on their pipes. They tell long highly exaggerated stories about their love lives. After a time with the lively group you leave.

A large tent has been set up in the forest glade. Urisks wander about. Their capacity for enjoying themselves seems boundless. They play pipes and tell each other stories. They hail you as their champion, clapping you heartily on the back.

The former leader of the Urisks, who you defeated to become the new leader, approaches you. 'You are strong. That is good. You are stronger than I. That is not so good for me. Leader, let me join you and serve you faithfully.' Allow him to join?
The Urisk bows respectfully to you and takes his leave. You leave the Urisks.
You take your leave of the humanoids. They return to their activities.
The mighty Urisk collapses. His last whispered words are 'I am glad that I should fall so that you may live, my leader.'
You enter the ancient vale of the Urisks. Whatever secrets may lie here will remain secret to you alas.

An ancient Urisk hobbles from the woods and regards you. 'Strange, you are champion ... but you are not Urisk.' He scratches his silver beard. 'No matter, leader, enter our sacred vale.' He plays a few notes on his pipes.
'Regard.' He says pointing at a faery castle which has suddenly appeared in the forest glade.
You see a mystical faery castle in this glade. Enter?
You hear faint laughter ring out among the trees.

The mighty Kerdrad is declared the leader of the Urisks. You are invited to join in the celebration. Former combatants drunkenly hang off each other and share highly exaggerated stories. After a time you leave.
You take this opportunity to rest and reflect upon your victories.
The innkeeper eyes narrow as he gazes upon Beleg. 'I know about you, Beleg, I won't be serving you or your friends. Now clear off.' He says angrily. Beleg shrugs his massive shoulders.
'See you in the bye-and-bye.'
Some strange cries ring in the distance.
A dead tree falls nearby.
Something dove behind a bush.
You step on a dry twig. That was audible for several hundred feet.
A group of townsfolk wander toward you. A small child is held by a young woman leading the pack. A woman beside her offers you some crumbling cake held in a cloth. Do you accept the cake?
The townsfolk nod approvingly. They wander past you. The cake is bland but nourishing.
The townsfolk are amazed at your rudeness. They shuffle past you, unwilling to meet your gaze.
A fine relic sits here. Take it?
The scroll reads 'A fine selection of gifts to aid thee. But be not excessive in thy desires.'
You enter a large room with a depressed centre. Statues of Urisks line the walls.
You leave the mystic place.
She transforms into a grey skinned faery of advanced age. Leering at you maliciously she begins to fade away into nothingness.
At the stroke of midnight, several grey skinned faery folk pop into existence near you. They take no notice of their surroundings but concentrate solely upon you. They speak in a strange rhymes:
'What 'tes to suffer for waun's ways; the sperrits com 'pon end of days, and wot desmal cowlds ye'll malaise... ' With that pronouncement they vanish. You feel suddenly ill.
'this day was very nearly past, and 'twoud p'raps by thy last; Shud our forgiveness not come to pass, fur effending that fey comely lass... ' With that pronouncement they vanish.
' 'tes zackly as I thoft 'twud be, the puttiest slaipers I did see; 'til the morraw a gift for thee... ' With that pronouncement they vanish. A gift has been left behind.
'Thee art a rogue, and we do knaw it, we've a score a ye and can shaw it; ye meddle so be waik for it. With that pronouncement they vanish. You feel the strength drain from your bodies.
'Pon thy brow we've set a mark, and be back 'fore the day be dark; if ye not be enjaying our wee lark...                         With that pronouncement they vanish. They have left a gift for you.
You reach into the bag and discover...
That you are suspended twenty feet above a lake. You crash down into the water. No harm done though. Some childish giggling accompanies your embarassment.
You reach into the bag and discover a small spotted egg. It begins to hatch. A small grey skinned faery emerges and winks at you. He begins to speak in the dreaful rhyming of the Quicklings.

'Bring the seng boird to the castle tay, wit es fedders so black and glassay, and yer cursed mark we will allay...'                     He winks at you and transforms into a blackbird. It chirrups at you amiably.
'I can't believe there's peace at last. I thought those Runics would overrun the land for sure.'

'Things are looking rosier for this town. I never thought much of that Godolphin but he is doing something right.' Another replies 'I reckon it has something to do with those strangers that are always hanging around.'
'I don't trust those Runics. They probably bought Godolphin off. You mark my words: they'll be here after the next spring thaw, and we'll all be slaves.'

The inn is abuzz with gossip about a large battle that took place against the Runics at the pass near Cairbre's stronghold. Some locals find it hard to believe that the battle was a victory. Others angrily insist that Arn has smiled upon them.

'I hear the Silverband has been broken. They say Godolphin put them to the sword. He is crushing any opposition to himself across the land. He now controls Ryn, and no one has heard a word from anyone from other towns in weeks. Probably his work too.'
The gates of the town have been broken down by desperate citizens trying to escape.
A pall of gloom overshadows this deserted town.
You mention to him that you found such a building beyond the mountains to the south west. 'Truly?' he says, 'approach and we shall talk more.'
It feels like you are trying to grasp a lightning bolt.
Probably just the wind...
A strange cry echoes from the rocky bluffs to the west.

'Now you can show your mettle, Kevardhu, we have some guests.' He turns to you. 'Know that you face Morjil Redemon, the greatest Orc tactician in history, scourge of the valley Sidhe, most honoured by Gruumsh ... ' His litany is drowned out by combat.
Another troll, much larger than the others emerges from the shadows of the room. He can only be the leader of the troll faction here, the cruel and sadistic Terksch, infamous throughout the land.
You find a key upon the body of the mighty warrior, Garanhir.
Shapes rush at you from the undergrowth!
Things slither out of a pile of rocks and surround you!
A pair of huge beasts lumber out of the darkness towards you. Bits of rock fall from their massive claws and mandibles.
You find some precious stones which were too dense for these creatures to chew through.
Aranflame makes a sudden decisive move on the chess board and the other player groans. He gives you a sly wink and takes his place in your party.
'Oh, I took you for adventurers, my mistake, the door is that way.'
With the demise of the Joykiller, the Seven has been effectively crushed as a power in this land.
These are the Thane's private quarters. All eyes turn to you as you are about to enter this room. Wisely, you back away.
The wind howls eerily along this battered headland.  Waves roll listlessly through the seaweed covered rocks catching you with a light spray.

Shapes move in the darkness ahead of you. Large, multi-limbed bodies drop lightly from the ceiling and a nightmare creature scuttles toward you on eight legs. You find yourself surrounded by monstrous spiders.
The hideous things twitch their last as you gather your breath.
A large passage leads into the darkness. Enter?
Leave the cave?
You find yourself alone with no explanation as to what just occured.
Gwydion gratefully joins your party.
More of the things stumble toward you.

You can't help but notice that the ship seems to have sailed into a school of alarmingly large fish.  The large fish jump out of the water and you get the impression that they are eyeing you as possible prey. Suddenly...
Hastily, you set sail and continue on your journey.

This tent is not part of the scenario - it is a place for me to test recent experiments before I totally reengineer everything and have to reverse things - if there are unsolvable bugs. So forget plot - look at them technically / stylistically instead.
Registration test.
Strange aquatic creatures have become attracted to the passage of the boat above their heads. They come closer ...
You detect slight disturbances in the ground around you. Bulbous heads poke through the soft earth and cast dead eyes upon you. Nightmare beasts clamber from their hiding spots and are upon you ...
As you leap nimbly from rock to rock you notice a thrashing in the water around you. A school of monstrous fish has become attracted to your movements ...
A large and well ordered barracks is located beyond this door. Many of the beds and wardrobes look unused, as if the Thane is suffering from a manpower shortage.

The door is engraved with a simple plaque reading 'Guard-Captain Vesta'. The room beyond is deserted and slightly dusty. Glancing around you see quite a few sentimental pictures and trinkets which seem at odds with the martial equipment.
Some mundane military equipment is stored here. Dull pole arms, shields and food stuffs are located in chests and along the walls.
A simple kitchen is located here. There is just enough room for the sweating cook to prepare his meals in this tight space.

The water seems to become solid beneath your feet as you walk across the waves. The feeling is quite unnerving. Though not nearly as unnerving as the group of enormous fish that seem to have surrounded you...
A flurry of tiny darts erupt from the undergrowth and fall amongst you. Horrible childish laughter accompanies this assault.
Your attackers remain unseen. Suddenly an unpleasant, wrinkly face peers through a bush and then a small body rushes away from you. Do you give chase?
Angrily you plow after the nimble figure. Just as you are about to catch it, a rope is pulled up across two trees catching you at neck height. Again that awful laughter surrounds you.

It seems your tormentors have decided to show themselves. A number of small, wizened faces surround you. Eyes filled with fey malice regard you. Twisted, and unseemly of form, the small beings emerge from cover to engage you.

Cautiously ... you let your small tormentor run away. He turns after a moment, and gesture rudely to you. Seeing you will not take his bait he begins to call to his kin in the surrounding brush. There is a commotion around you.

The wounded Quickling undergoes a bizarre fit of thrashing and wailing. Its limbs begin to extend as it grows into a monstrous being of dead green skin and fetid odour. It rises to its feet and regards you with intense malice.

Suddenly a great rustling of trees and bushes ensues. A mighty tree enters the battle, gesturing to the Quicklings angrily with its huge knotted limbs. They react with rage at this intrusion and set upon this mysterious newcomer.
The mighty tree takes a fatal blow and retreats into the undergrowth as inexplicably as it arrived.

After the battle you look around you.  The mighty tree seems to have disappeared into the forest without a trace. You are left with no explanation for these bizarre forest creatures. You notice something among the fetid remains of the Quicklings however.

It seems the Quicklings always get the last laugh. As you open the bag it quickly grows to a huge size and engulfs you. You fight and tear your way out of the foul smelling thing. Needless to say, you hear distant laughing...
You salvage some bright and dazzling blades out of this unfortunate experience.
At last ... an exit from these infernal caves.
The cave mouth seems to have disappeared.
I wonder what it is that is expected of you ... standing as you are on a small rock in a room full of lava?

They immediately begin to argue amongst themselves about whether they should rebuild or move to join the other Fir'bolg. Eventually, those that wish to stay overcome their opposition. There is nothing more for you here, and you move on...

A figure emerges from the hut. Under the grime you see that he is a Fir'bolg. 'Welcome to Cantref y Gwaelod' he says lamely gesturing to the devastation. 'Once a city of unearthly beauty and unmatched learning ... now a ruin.'
Several Fir'bolgs wait anxiously amid the grove of apple trees. Their eyes light up in a mixture of fear and delight at the sight of the Cauldron. 'Praise the moon and the apple!' One cries.
This appears to be a council chamber of sorts. It looks like the major decisions in Laerg life are made in this very room.
A cook sweats in this back room.
Shapes stir amidst the snowbanks. You find yourself surrounded by aggressive humanoids whose white fur blends almost perfectly with their frozen surroundings. They move in...
The snow seems disturbed here, and several sets of footprints lead toward the mountains. The footprints suggest that their owners have clawed feet and are quite large and heavy.
Impressive victory.

This low room is apparently a mausoleum. Ancient and crumbling crypts line the floor. Your entrance seems to have awakened some slumbering creatures of nightmarish appearance. What at first you took for heaps of rubbish begin to move!
Flesh hangs off the swollen creatures. They exude an unnaturally powerful stench of corruption and decay. They are upon you before you can prepare yourselves.
A secret passage is hidden behind the mural.
They have been ensorcelled to summon demonic guardians. Three gruesome demons materialise in the room and immediately attack!
You are left with the books and other assorted magical aides.
The guards merely laugh and slam the gates.
A well trodden path leads into this foul smelling cave. Enter?
Leave the cave?
Deep growls erupts from the darkness ahead. A group of the dogmen are waiting to pounce on you.
A large number of the dogmen await you in this cave having been alerted by their advance guards. Behind them you see their rudimentary kennels amid the fetid trees. They move to engage you.
Dogmen leap at you from the darkness, catching you off guard!
Beleg looks around. 'So this is Portenys, I hear they have a good pub: the White Hart. These Says can brew some lethal ale, almost as good as a jug of old Karnak scrumpy.' He says knowledgeably.
Beleg looks around the pub and rubs his hands with glee.
Beleg offers his opinion: 'This place looks as inviting as a pub after last call.'
Aranflame looks around. 'This architecture is characteristic of the Fomorians. It seems to have outlived them, though. From what I have read they haven't been seen in living memory.'

Beleg looks around. 'Not much atmosphere, but I heard these Runics know how to make some potent wines. Don't get me wrong, most of the time I think wine is for ponces, but when there's nothing else around ...'
Gwydion looks startled. 'I had heard about the Apple Isle, but I thought it was a place of great beauty. The stories must have been greatly exaggerated.'
Llywarch stops you. 'No time for that friends, we must go straight to the Watch Tower. What must be done, must be done. Trust me.' He says enigmatically.
Some Defenders and their leader cluster in this foul smelling kennel. Having watched you dispatch the dogmen, morale is not high with this rearguard. Do you allow them to leave in peace?
They lay down their weapons and strip out of their armour. They shuffle off, shamefacedly. Without all the armour, they look just like typical townspeople of Pengelly or Porthenys.
Realizing that this is the end of the questionable path they have chosen, the Defenders prepare to acquit themselves with some semblance of dignity.

Vesta calls out to them. 'Don't think I have forgotten your faces. When this is over we shall be talking again ... and you shall atone for your crimes. Perhaps then you shall be lucky enough to be accepted once more into society.'

Vesta looks down upon the fallen. 'I remember Thastos, and several of the others. They wandered off from guard duty several months ago. Whatever could have possessed them to tread this dark path?' She asks of no one in particular.

Vesta regards the dead with cold fury. 'I cannot blame these weak minded fools for the choices they have made ... I reserve judgement for the one that is behind this madness.' She says as she sharpens her blades in readiness.

The Thane regards Vesta with relief. 'I thought you were dead. Where have you been?' Vesta relates to the Thane the situation at Skull Keep. 'What vile madness is this?' He responds, 'I am glad you have returned, we need to rebuild our defences.'

Vesta informs him that she wishes to accompany you. The Thane is very displeased but spreads his hands in a gesture of defeat. 'I have never been able to change your mind once you've decided on a path. Very well.'

'I shall begin a recruitment drive, some townsfolk have wandered home claiming to have lost all memory of recent events. They must have been at Skull Keep. I will question them at length before allowing them back into our depleted ranks.'
'Good luck with your journeys ... I bid you farewell.' The Thane leaves.
Hreidmar looks with awe at the mighty blade Fragarach. 'Methinks I have bought myself several winters of calm seas for my part in this.' He says with satisfaction.

'Hail the returning heroes.' Maeth says with an exaggerated flourish. 'Come and share some tea with me.' He waves to some comfortable seats near a cheery fire. 'You have accomplished much in your visit to this troubled land.'

'Much wrong have you righted, but sadly the land has paid a terrible price. One that it will never recover from I fear. Many of the ancient races have been pushed back into hiding. Much of the magic of this land has been drained in the Struggle.'

'The Karnaks are at peace with the Runics for now. But the time of the Runics is at hand, and the Karnaks will slowly and inevitably be absorbed into their society. The Seys of Porthenys and Pengelly too will grow and expand and move into our lands.'

'But I do not waste my time in despairing for what will be lost. Those who struggle blindly against the inevitable only fool themselves.' He sips at his tea and ponders. 'It was an honour to have known you, this will be the last time we speak.'
You bid Maeth farewell and leave his cottage.
You enter Godolphin's manor to loud acclaim.

Karnak warriors and townsfolk have already begun drinking themselves into a stupor. Godolphin regards you with triumph in his eyes. 'Glad to see you made it back, but you have proven yourselves to be the most dangerous force in this land, so no wonder.'

'It has been a great honour knowing you, I hope my small force was of use at the very end. Folk such as you only come around once a cycle ... and though I get the idea that I am but a bit player in some larger drama, it was a pleasure.'

You join the Karnaks in their festivities for a time and then take your leave. The Karnaks wish you safe journeys and bid you fond farewell. You remember to check your room one last time for anything you might have left there.
Karnaks wave to you in greeting. They are friendly, but there is a distance to them that wasn't there before.
Ryn guardsmen stare at you. One musters the courage to say 'Ryn is always open to you, great ones.'

The Praetor regards you. 'News has been brought to me of some interesting events in the east, no doubt greatly exaggerated. I am no great believer in these mystical beings which my weaker minded troops speak of.'
'I have enjoyed our little chat,' says the Praetor in a manner which indicates otherwise, 'I have much work to attend to, and bid you good day.'
The mighty contraption takes too much damage and flounders. Its occupants leap from it and continue the attack.

They voyaged along the large river which terminates at the nearby lake. They then pacified the orcs to the west and settled in the arable land that they found there. Some long to return home, while others seem quite content in this new land.
You have a slightly better understanding of them now. They bid you farewell.
A horde of trolls has now gathered around the bulwark. Too many for you to handle on your own. You are forced to retreat.
Karnak reinforcements rush in.
The Karnaks gaze with awe at the assembled might of the Runics before them. But whatever fear they feel they mask well.
You hear the sounds of Karnak battle music approaching.
The Ryn defenders look around nervously. Suddenly Karnaks appear behind the Ryn defenders and tear into them. Godolphin rubs his hands with mirth. 'Think they can out-fox me do they.' He says.

Although this concludes the major plotline of the scenario, there are plenty of sidelines for you to explore if you haven't already. Good luck finding them and I hope you enjoyed the scenario. Thank you for registering. Tremordred.
Some trolls converge on you.
Several Light Horsemen charge to your aid.
The tinner nods to you politely.
The Savant stares at you almost as if he is seeing right through you. He nods benignly but otherwise has little more to say.
This would appear to be the kitchen. A busy cook works overtime to meet the strict requirements of his demanding clientele.
You feel a strange pull towards this place.
Kerdrad stammers in amazement. 'The Vale ... the vale. I knew I was wise to throw the fight and let you win.' He looks askance at you.
A castle rises high above this rocky island. A portal yawns open. Enter?

You stand on the shore of sea of blood. The viscous matter oozes against the black rocks. The movement of this 'sea' in no way reminds you of water. There is no tide, but instead, you sense the blood ebbs and flows to a different cycle.
In this cycle you are the prey. The blood surges over the rocks to wash against your feet.
And then is gone.

You gaze into what looks like an archway leading into utter blackness. A foul stench of dried blood seaps out of the archway. This would appear to be a rift between this world and another. Something monstrous surely awaits you on the other side. Enter?
After a period of intense disorientation you arrive in a surreal landscape. The sickly stench of blood infuses the air, the earth and even the vegetation.
A shape materializes out of the gloom. A small child grins up at you. A huge rictus splits its face and blood red feral eyes peer up at you. You recognize the Child of Night. He advances toward you.
The Child of Night says 'I would have words with you, if you please ...'

The Child seems to blush with the compliment. 'You are too kind, but in truth most of the souls I have harvested of late I owe to your ample bloodthirstiness.' He bows to you with a flourish. 'But now is not the time for fond memories.'

'Know that the Demon hordes support you in your move against the Grey God. His craving for oblivion threatens us all... I was sent to warn you about this plane. Although we of the Abyss understand this plane, the Glooms, no better than yourselves ...'

'We do know that the Grey God has retreated his Avatar to an island fortress in a sea of blood. There is a boat, and we know that access to the boat is hidden somewhere in 'the Pattern.' You will know it when you see it. But know that it lives.'

'The Pattern will rise against you, as will the rest of this plane. Look around you, this is what a world becomes when the Grey God has achieved victory. Not a single soul to harvest nor child's nightmare to collect.' He sighs.

'I doubt we'll meet again. I will have to grow another body. It could take hundreds of years.' He glowers at you, then grins impishly again. 'Unless ...' His eyes widen as he snaps his overlarge mouth shut. His image begins to shimmer and waver.
And he is gone.

You launch an attack at this creature of pure malice. It passes straight through him. He mimics being thrown back and clutches at his chest in a bout of overacting. He laughs, 'Fools, I lost my body, don't you remember? I am just a shade here. Listen.'
There is a pull at your mind. An alien presence is trying to penetrate your thought process.
The feeling continues ... even stronger now. Suddenly the presence recedes from your mind. However, a clear impression is left...
This strange crystalline dwelling stands in stark contrast to its nightmarish surroundings. It is a thing of grace and beauty around which the grotesque forest has left a glade.
You enter and see what looks like a wisp of prismatic light dancing around the room in some sort of rhythm. A probing sensation enters your minds once more. You experience another thought-message.
The light slows down to a soft hum and then slowly winks out of existence.
The thick blood oozes and pops. It boils violently at your approach and then seems to eject globs of vileness into the air. The globs take shape and advance...
A cairn lies here, lying like a scab amidst the channels of blood. Open the cairn?
A revolting nether beast springs out of the opening as if desperate to be freed of its confines. It gazes upon you hungrily and attacks with a bellow.
The Pattern falls silent. The blood starts to flow more like a normal river, toward the sea. As the blood thins out, you notice something in the southeast part of the Pattern.
A strange fragile structure is revealed once the blood flows from this depression. There is an entrance. Do you enter?
After a barely tangible feeling of movement you find yourself in front of a ship.

This tortured plane of existence begins to unravel without its 'master.' You find yourselves violently ejected from it only to arrive in the Shadowgaunt's stronghold in front of the now consumed rift.
You leave the stronghold.
Monstrous bats are attracted to the motion of the boat!
A revolting nether beast springs out of the opening as if desperate to be freed of its confines. It gazes upon you, summons some of its kin, and then moves to swarm you.
For an instant you sense that a being of immense power has cast his gaze upon you. You are left with a lasting impression, as if your retinas had been burned by staring too long at the sun.
If they are listening ... you would never know it.
On the edge of the ice sits a hut. An ancient frost giant can be seen inside.
